jobs.title: Teknisi FWA XL Smart
jobs.description:
pt. karunia indah cahaya membuka lowongan kerja sebagai teknisi fwa xl smart untuk penempatan area tasikmalaya. perusahaan bergerak di bidang kontraktor telekomunikasi. tanggung jawab meliputi instalasi, pemeliharaan, dan penanganan teknis jaringan fwa xl smart di lapangan.

pria usia 18-35 tahun dan berdomisili di tasikmalaya. memiliki sim c serta kendaraan pribadi. diutamakan lulusan smk/sederajat dengan latar belakang teknik instalasi tenaga listrik (titl) atau teknik jaringan komputer. bersedia bekerja di ketinggian, memiliki sikap disiplin, jujur, dan mampu bekerja sama dalam tim.

jobs.title: Merchant Succes Executive (Sales)
jobs.description:
kami mencari merchant succes executive (sales) untuk bergabung dengan tim kami. bertanggung jawab untuk meningkatkan penjualan dan mencapai target penjualan. melakukan analisis pasar dan kompetitor, serta membangun hubungan dengan merchant.

laki-laki/wanita usia maks 35 tahun, minimum pendidikan sma sederajat, memiliki pengalaman sebagai sales fmcg, memiliki komunikasi skill yang baik, memiliki kendaraan roda dua, memiliki sim c aktif, pengalaman menjual mesin edc & akuisisi

jobs.title: Merchant Succes Executive (Sales)
jobs.description:
bukuwarung sedang mencari merchant succes executive (sales) untuk melakukan akuisisi merchant dan penjualan mesin edc di berbagai wilayah di jawa tengah dan diy. posisi ini bertanggung jawab untuk memperluas jaringan merchant dengan dukungan gaji pokok, tunjangan pulsa dan transportasi, serta jaminan bpjs.

pria atau wanita dengan usia maksimal 35 tahun dan pendidikan minimal sma sederajat. kandidat wajib memiliki pengalaman sebagai sales fmcg, kemampuan komunikasi yang baik, serta memiliki kendaraan roda dua dan sim c aktif. pengalaman dalam menjual mesin edc dan akuisisi sangat diutamakan.

jobs.title: Head of Business Development, MENAU
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Germany, Jordan and Lebanon.**

**Background**

Over the past 90+ years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild through long-term, sustainable development solutions. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC’s mission is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. The International Rescue Committee is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 28 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC also helps refugees resettle in the US and become self-sufficient. The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

**Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD)**

The Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD) have a portfolio of humanitarian relief, post-crisis recovery, and development programs under their remit. This work focuses support in five key areas: ensuring safety from harm, improving health, increasing access to education, improving economic well-being and ensuring people have the power to influence decisions that affect their lives. In all these programs, there is a drive to address the unique needs of women and girls (who represent the majority of those displaced) – and the universal barriers they face.

**The Awards Management Unit (AMU)** is one of four pillars within CRRD. The unit is responsible for identifying, securing, and supporting the management of all funding from statutory/government donors. The AMU is a bridge between donors and country programs: providing expert technical advice to the country teams, while maintaining portfolio-level visibility to ensure consistency and compliance and manage risk. This pillar ensures that donor compliance policies and procedures are implemented consistently and supports all staff working across the award management cycle for all restricted funding from global government sources.

**The Purpose of the Role**

Reporting to the Director, Awards Management, the Head of Business Development (HBD), MENAU, leads IRC’s business development efforts in support of the region’s country programs and is a key part of IRC’s global business development team, serving as the region's representative in developing and implementing IRC’s global business development strategy. The HBD plays a strategic role in the planning, identification, and successful pursuit of new business in line with country Strategy Action Plans (SAPs). HBD support includes all phases of the business development process, including strategic planning, donor outreach and engagement, pre-positioning (capture), partnering, proposal development, due diligence, issues letter and agreement negotiation.

The HBD is responsible for maintaining regional level oversight of all business development for institutional donors in the IRC’s Middle East, North Africa, and Ukraine (MENAU) region, which comprises country programs in Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria, Ukraine, and Yemen. As a member of the Regional Program and Award Support (RPAS) team, the HBD also provides business development support to IRC’s Emergency Response in the Occupied Palestinian Territories (oPt).

**Scope and Authority**

The Head of Business Development exercises overall leadership for business development in the region and line management of regional Program Development Advisors (PDAs). The role oversees regional and supports country business development strategies and planning, including reviewing the pipeline and individual opportunities and ensuring appropriate resourcing for successful bid submissions. The HBD provides development oversight of regionally assigned opportunities and serves as a key regional focal point for global opportunities supported by AMU’s Proposal Leadership team.

**Key Working Relationships**

The HBD reports to the Director, Awards Management (DAM) and manages regional PDAs. The HBD works closely with the regional Senior Management Team, all RPAS team members, and the wider AMU Global Business Development team, including peers in the Donor Engagement, BD Services, and BD Strategy, Operations, & Resourcing teams. The HBD also collaborates with other teams within the Crisis Response Recovery and Development Department, especially AMU, the Emergency Unit, and Technical Excellence, as well as with External Relations, Global Supply Chain, Finance, Office of General Counsel, and other key departments within IRC who contribute to regional business development efforts. The HBD serves as point of contact with external donor and partner stakeholders during the pre-award stage, as applicable per region.

**KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES**

***Planning and Strategic Leadership (40%)***

- Provide strategic vision on regional BD efforts in support of country program Strategy Action Plans (SAP), in collaboration with regional and AMU leadership.
- Maintain visibility on the overall pipeline across all public and institutional donors, in collaboration with RPAS team members.
- Maintain up to date knowledge of donor funding priorities and geographical interests relevant to IRC’s areas of work.
- Provide advice, analysis and guidance to AMU, Regional and Country leadership on BD trends, target-setting, donor engagement, and support needs in the region, ensuring leaders have the right level of information to make decisions.
- Lead and support BD strategy development efforts and planning at regional and country level, to establish clear funding priorities and targets, to support decision making and enable effective positioning and resource planning.
- Coordinate support to country teams in the identification, tracking and pursuit of new business opportunities across a variety of technical sectors and donors, including ensuring that technical brainstorming, partner, and competitor landscape analysis and win theme sessions with technical and country staff are occurring.

***End to End Program Development (20%)***

- Support effective and timely Go/No Go decisions, including sharing initial assessment of new opportunities and providing insight and inputs based on donor knowledge, likelihood of success and experience.
- Plan and manage effective division of bid leadership across the portfolio at capture and live stages of development to ensure appropriate support on all opportunities.
- At the early stage of opportunity identification, work with country teams, DAM and others in identifying and addressing escalated support needs.
- Act as the regional business development focal point for escalated bid opportunities, providing regional advice and coordinating escalated support in connection with bid leads assigned by the Proposal Leadership team or others.
- Collaborate with other BD staff, especially Proposal Leadership team members and technical staff on high demand opportunities and multi-country and TU-led bids.
- Ensure the following Bid Leadership responsibilities are performed consistently and effectively by the assigned BD Lead (HBD, PDA, Proposal Leadership team member, or other) on each public opportunity in the regional portfolio:
- Collaborate with technical units, country offices, and other colleagues to support conceptualization of winning program and bid designs, including support to building effective partnerships and consortia.
- Provide effective proposal support, ranging from proposal management to comprehensive support, confirming responsiveness to and compliance with solicitation documents and with IRC’s requirements. Ensure required reviews and approvals are secured prior to submission to donor.
- Provide guidance on donor policies and ensure project design is responsive and compliant with donor expectations, rules, and regulations.
- When providing proposal management support, coordinate concept note and/or proposal development, including sharing initial assessment of new opportunities, reviewing timelines, ensuring the proposal team adheres to deadlines, supporting recruitment, assisting in budget development, ensuring document completion, organizing meetings, and compiling notes, and drafting and proofreading proposal sections. This includes support to country office teams in the management and maintenance of IRC’s award management system.
- Review agreements, in coordination with relevant RPAS post-award focal point, to ensure accuracy and highlight key compliance requirements, in coordination with post-award, Compliance & Policy and country Grants teams.
- Facilitate internal After-action Reviews with country teams, technical units, regional team, and other relevant stakeholders to collect lessons learned. Support efforts to share feedback beyond the region as part of IRC’s wider business development learning agenda.
- Work across teams to ensure successful handover from pre-award to post-award, that lessons learned are captured, and best practices are shared, in support of improved knowledge management and through the development of relevant tools.
- Maintain complete and accurate electronic files, including final submission packages and IRC data products (e.g., Opportunity Database, OTIS).

***Donor and Partner Engagement (10%)***

- In line with IRC’s Partnership Ambition, contribute to increasing the volume and equity of IRC's work with local and regional partners (with a focus on women-led national organizations) by coordinating support to country programs in identifying partnership opportunities, identifying strong partners, and finalizing teaming arrangements.
- Support partnering conversations with international partner HQs where needed.
- Support countries and region in planning effective donor, partner, and peer engagement, in collaboration with colleagues across the organization.
- Represent IRC externally to donors, peers, and partners.

***Capacity Building and Training (10%)***

- Collaborate with other HBDs and stakeholders to share best practices and lessons learned, and to develop and improve tools as identified in the BD team workplan.
- Contribute to developing, updating, and delivering business-development related training for the region, including roll-out and refreshers of the IRC Business Development Process training. This will be done in collaboration with RPAS team members,
- Develop, strengthen, and share capacity of other IRC staff - including direct reports, IRC country and regional teams - to identify opportunities and develop strong program design and proposals, including BD processes.
- Support in recruiting, onboarding, and training of new country, regional grants and partnerships team members in collaboration with RPAS team members.

***Staff Management, Learning, and Development (15%)***

- Supervise and mentor direct reports, including communicating clear expectations, providing regular and timely performance feedback, document and discuss performance issues if needed, and deliver high-quality documented annual performance reviews.
- Ensure direct reports are trained on all relevant IRC processes and donor regulations.
- Support direct reports in achieving annual objectives, acting as a trusted and accountable manager, mentor, and professional resource, including promoting collaboration, enabling adequate resourcing, and ensuring accountability.

***Other Responsibilities (5%)***

- Contribute to AMU and regional strategic priorities and initiatives.
- Support with translation to regional or donor languages when necessary.
- Participate in special projects, working groups and other tasks as assigned.

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

Essential Skills, Knowledge, and Qualifications:

- Substantial experience and a successful track record leading large proposal teams on complex subject, multi-year, multi-partner proposals with minimal supervision.
- Experience developing and supporting humanitarian and development proposals for NGOs.
- Experience with strategies and proposal processes of key government/statutory donors – US Government, FCDO, EU institutions (DGs ECHO, INTPA, MENA), UN, and other donors (CDCS, AFD, GAC, Sida, GFFO, BMZ, SDC, etc.).·
- Experience collaborating with and supporting national and community-based partners.·
- Experience in proposal budgeting a plus.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to effectively collaborate across a variety of relationships in a multicultural environment.
- Demonstrated ability to collaborate equally effectively with colleagues in remote and diverse teams, including as team leader for proposals.
- Clear, compelling writing skills, preferably with previous experience with proposal writing.
- Ability to multi-task and prioritize effectively.
- Ability to travel internationally (approximately 20% of time).
- Fluency in English required. Fluency in Arabic desirable.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Chargé.e de mission auprès de la direction générale - Siège Dakar - H/F
jobs.description:
**PRÉSENTATION ALIMA**

**L’ESPRIT ALIMA :** *La raison d’être d’ALIMA est de sauver des vies et de soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, sans aucune discrimination identitaire, religieuse ou politique, à travers des actions basées sur la proximité, l’innovation et l’alliance d’organisations et d’individus. Nous agissons avec humanisme, impartialité et dans le respect de **l’éthique** médicale universelle. Pour accéder aux patients et aux patientes, nous nous engageons à intervenir de façon neutre et indépendante.*

**LES VALEURS et PRINCIPES de notre action, inscrits au sein de notre CHARTE :**

1. Le patient d’abord
2. Révolutionner la médecine humanitaire
3. Responsabilité et liberté
4. Améliorer la qualité de nos actions
5. Faire confiance
6. L’intelligence collective
7. Responsabilité environnementale

ALIMA promeut et défend les principes des droits humains fondamentaux. ALIMA a une approche de tolérance zéro envers les personnes coupables d’actes de violences sexistes et sexuelles ainsi qu’envers l’inaction face à des faits de violence supposés ou avérés. La protection des personnes bénéficiant et impactées par notre intervention est notre priorité absolue dans tout ce que nous faisons. Toute personne collaborant avec ALIMA s’engage à :

- Respecter la charte, le code de conduite, les politiques institutionnelles incluant la politique de protection contre les abus de pouvoir et les violences sexistes et sexuelles, la politique de prévention de la corruption et de la fraude
- Signaler toute violation aux politiques, documents cadre et procédure à une supérieure, un supérieur, une référente, un référent ou à l’adresse alert@alima.ngo

**SOIGNER - INNOVER – ENSEMBLE :**

Depuis sa création en 2009, ALIMA a touché plus de 18 millions de bénéficiaires dans 15 pays, principalement en Afrique. En 2024, nous avons développé 59 projets de réponse médicale humanitaire pour répondre aux besoins de populations touchées par les conflits, les épidémies et l’extrême pauvreté. L’ensemble de ces projets se font en appui aux autorités sanitaires nationales à travers les structures de santé (dont hôpitaux et centres de santé). Notre action découle d’une adaptation constante aux réalités du terrain et aux progrès de la médecine. En 2024, ALIMA a atteint 5,9 millions de bénéficiaires. Nous travaillons en partenariat, notamment avec des ONGs locales, dès que cela est possible afin de nous assurer que nos patients et patientes bénéficient de l’expertise là où elle se trouve, que ce soit au niveau de leur pays ou du reste du monde. Par ailleurs, pour améliorer la réponse humanitaire, nous menons des projets de recherches opérationnelles et cliniques notamment dans le domaine de la lutte contre la malnutrition et les fièvres virales hémorragiques

**NOS THÉMATIQUES PROJET :** Malnutrition, Santé sexuelle et reproductive incluant les violences basées sur le genre, Santé Primaire et secondaire, la chirurgie, les soins pédiatriques, les maladies tueuses tel que Paludisme, IRA, Diarrhée, Épidémies (Fièvres hémorragiques, méningite, Choléra, Rougeole, Dengue, Covid-19).

**L'ÉQUIPE ALIMA :** plus de 2000 personnes œuvrent actuellement pour ALIMA. Les équipes terrain, au plus proche des patients, reçoivent leur support des équipes de coordination généralement basées en capitale des pays d’intervention. Celles-ci reçoivent le support des 4 équipes desk et de l’équipe du service urgences et ouvertures basées au siège opérationnel de Dakar, Sénégal. Les équipes de Paris et New-York travaillent activement à la collecte de fonds ainsi qu’à la représentation d’ALIMA. Le reste de la Galaxie ALIMA comprend des individus et des équipes partenaires qui travaillent pour le compte d’autres organisations telles que les ONGs médicales BEFEN, ALERTE Santé, SOS Médecins / KEOOGO, AMCP-SP, Demtou, les organismes de recherche PACCI, INSERM, INRB, les Universités de Bordeaux ou de Copenhague, l’ONG Solidarités International et bien d’autres.

**NOS PAYS D’INTERVENTIONS :**Mali, Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, Nigeria, Niger, Tchad, République Démocratique du Congo, Cameroun, Ethiopie, Guinée, Soudan du Sud, Mauritanie, Sénégal, Soudan et Haïti.

LIEU DU POSTE

Dakar, Sénégal

LIENS FONCTIONNELS ET HIERARCHIQUES

- Poste de support au sein de la direction générale
- Rend compte au Directeur général adjoint (supervision directe)
- Collabore directement avec le Directeur général et le Directeur général adjoint
- Interagit avec les membres du comité de direction, les équipes du Siège et des personnalités extérieures

MISSION ET ACTIVITES PRINCIPALES

Le/la chargé.e de mission auprès de la direction générale a pour mission d’**appuyer au quotidien** le Directeur général et le Directeur général adjoint d’ALIMA dans **l’organisation et le suivi des dossiers prioritaires** de la direction. Il.elle apporte support, suivi, conseil et aide à l’analyse pour faciliter la prise de décision.

En 2027, dans ses tâches d’appui, un accent particulier sera porté sur :

- la préparation, la rédaction, le suivi et la revue du plan d’action annuel d’ALIMA, en lien avec le cadre stratégique pluriannuel
- le pilotage et le suivi des dossiers de partenariat entre ALIMA et les acteurs nationaux, particulièrement les ONG nationales et les structures de recherche
- la maîtrise des risques organisationnels d’ALIMA

1. **Appui général à la direction**

- Rédiger et préparer des documents et supports, aider à la synthèse des échanges et au suivi des décisions.
- Prendre contact et organiser les échanges avec les interlocuteurs clés, en interne et en externe, pour faire avancer les dossiers prioritaires de la direction.
- Participer de façon permanente à la réflexion pour l’atteinte des objectifs de l’organisation.
- Appuyer la gestion des budgets et des dépenses relatives à la direction générale.

1. **Plan d’action annuel d’ALIMA**

- Cadrer et suivre la méthodologie.
- Planifier et organiser les séminaires et réunions avec les managers et les équipes.
- Aider à la rédaction et participer à la réflexion, en particulier sur la cohérence entre les différentes priorités et les différents chantiers, et entre le plan et le cadre stratégique et la charte ALIMA, le contexte externe, et les moyens humains, techniques et financiers disponibles ou à mobiliser.
- Assurer la communication interne sur l’avancée des travaux et la diffusion du plan, en vue d’une bonne appropriation.
- Planifier et appuyer la revue du plan d’action à mi-parcours.

1. **Pilotage et animation du partenariat avec les acteurs humanitaires nationaux**

- Suivre et analyser les dynamiques de localisation de l’aide humanitaire et du Humanitarian Reset, et leurs implications pour ALIMA et ses partenaires (acteurs humanitaires, structures de coordination de l’aide, bailleurs de fonds).
- Appuyer le pilotage stratégique du modèle de partenariat d’ALIMA et de son évolution.
- Planifier et organiser les séminaires et actions nécessaires sur le sujet.
- Appuyer la mise en œuvre des activités de soutien au développement des ONG nationales : auto-diagnostics organisationnels, suivi des priorités, développement d’outils, partage des expériences et des leçons apprises.
- Rédiger les conventions cadre et assurer le suivi administratif du partenariat.

1. **Maîtrise des risques organisationnels**

- Appuyer le suivi et la mise à jour des analyses des risques organisationnels, conformément à la politique de gestion des risques d’ALIMA.
- Appuyer la gestion des dossiers à la demande de la direction et en coordination avec les différents départements : documentation, organisation des étapes, suivi des résultats, aide au suivi administratif et juridique.
- Assurer le suivi et la veille concernant l’enregistrement d’ALIMA dans les différents pays de présence et auprès des autorités et institutions pertinentes.

Cette description des tâches n’est pas exhaustive.

EXPERIENCES ET COMPETENCES

**Formation :**

- Formation supérieure en gestion, sciences politiques, droit, développement international ou communication

**Expériences :**

- 5 ans d’expérience au sein d’une organisation internationale, d’une ONG ou d’une administration en lien avec la solidarité internationale
- Expérience réussie sur un poste d’attaché auprès d’une direction, de chargé de support aux opérations, de relations bailleurs et reporting, ou de communication et plaidoyer dans le secteur de l’aide internationale

**Compétences et Qualités**

- Qualités d’analyse et de synthèse
- Fortes compétences rédactionnelles
- Diplomatie et sens de la concertation
- Aisance dans les échanges et la prise de parole
- Rigueur, sens de l’organisation et respect des délais
- Sens de la confidentialité
- Intérêt manifeste pour les dynamiques et l’actualité internationales, particulièrement africaines

**Langues :**

- La maîtrise du français et de l’anglais est indispensable et sera évaluée lors de l’entretien

CONDITIONS

**Durée et type de contrat** : CDD de droit sénégalais - 12 mois renouvelable, avec période d’essai de 3 mois

**Prise de poste** : décembre 2026

**Salaire** : selon la grille de salaire en vigueur au Siège de Dakar

ALIMA prend en charge :

- 2,75 jours de congés payés par mois
- La couverture santé pour l’employé.e et ses ayants droit

jobs.title: 23852 Project Officer (Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion) (P)
jobs.description:
Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) in Cameroon and the direct supervision of the Head of Programmes, and in close coordination with relevant units, Government counterparts, and partners, the Project Officer (Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion) will support the implementation of activities under the Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion Unit within the IOM Cameroon Country Office.

The Project Officer (Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion) will provide technical and operational support for project-funded interventions in the areas of labour migration, migration and trade, skills development and training, skills mobility partnerships, business and human rights, migrant inclusion, access to decent work and social protection, and other migration and sustainable development-related areas in line with IOM mandates.

The Project Officer (Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion) supports project implementation and coordination activities at national and regional levels and contributes to the delivery of project outputs in line with IOM global frameworks, regional priorities, and national development objectives.

1. Support, under the guidance of the Head of Programmes, the implementation of donor-funded projects under the Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion Unit, including programmes on labour mobility, diaspora engagement, skills development, cross-border trade, and socio-economic inclusion, in line with IOM and donor requirements.
2. Support the full project cycle (planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and closure), ensuring timely delivery of outputs, outcomes, and indicators as defined in approved project documents.
3. Assist in the day-to-day implementation and administrative coordination of assigned project tasks, including preparation and regular update of work plans, implementation schedules, procurement plans, risk matrices, and monitoring tools.
4. Provide technical support for the implementation of labour mobility and skills-based interventions, including ethical recruitment, skills partnerships, labour–trade–mobility initiatives, private sector engagement, and diaspora contributions to development.
5. Support the implementation of diaspora engagement activities, including skills transfer, investment mobilisation, entrepreneurship support, and contributions to resilience and regional cooperation initiatives.
6. Work closely with Government counterparts at national, regional, and local levels to support implementation of migration, employment, trade, and social inclusion activities.
7. Support in the implementation of socio-economic inclusion activities, including entrepreneurship support, financial inclusion, business formalization, and capacity building for women, youth, migrants, and small cross-border traders.
8. Support the integration of cross-cutting priorities in assigned tasks, including gender equality, youth empowerment, protection mainstreaming, disability inclusion, conflict sensitivity, and environmental sustainability.
9. Provide day-to-day supervision and guidance to assigned project staff, and support coordination with consultants and implementing partners, including performance monitoring and review of technical deliverables.
10. Support coordination with Resource Management, HR, Procurement, and Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) units to facilitate budget monitoring, compliance, timely procurement, and effective use of project resources.
11. Prepare and consolidate, in coordination with the Head of Programmes, donor deliverables, including narrative and financial reports, technical inputs, concept notes, and funding proposals, and contribute information and documentation as required.
12. Support monitoring, evaluation, and reporting activities, including data collection, results analysis, documentation of lessons learned, and dissemination of good practices.
13. Maintain working relationships with partners and relevant stakeholders, including with UN agencies, development partners, regional organisations, civil society, workers’ and employers’ organisations, and private sector actors.
14. Identify operational risks and implementation constraints and report issues to the supervisor and support the implementation of corrective actions, undertake duty travel as required.
15. Perform other duties as assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Labour Economics, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Law, International Relations, Political Science, Human Rights, Social Sciences, or a related field from an accredited academic institution, with two years of relevant professional experience; or
- University degree in the above-mentioned fields from an accredited academic institution, with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Progressive professional experience in labour migration, labour mobility, skills development, employment, social inclusion, or related migration and development fields, with demonstrated application in African contexts;
- Proven experience in project coordination and implementation, including results-based management, donor reporting and compliance, preferably within multi-country or regional programmes;
- Hands-on experience engaging with government authorities, regional institutions, UN agencies, international and national organizations, social partners and private sector actors in Africa;
- Experience supporting initiatives related to skills development, ethical recruitment, migrant worker protection, labour governance, business and human rights, and/or socio-economic inclusion;
- Demonstrated experience working in Central Africa, and/or supporting regional or sub‑regional initiatives (e.g. CEMAC, ECCAS), with understanding of regional integration, mobility and labour dynamics; and,
- Prior exposure to complex operational or border contexts in Africa, is an asset.

**Skills**

- Solid technical knowledge of labour mobility, migration governance, skills development and employment systems, including understanding of African and Central African contexts;
- Solid familiarity with UN system policies, rules and procedures, including implementation of donor-funded programmes;
- Good analytical and drafting skills, including preparation of reports and programme documentation;
- Good coordination and stakeholder engagement skills, including experience working across ministries, regional stakeholders and implementing partners; and,
- Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, supervise teams, and deliver quality results in deadline-driven environments.

**Languages**

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of Portuguese and other official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: 23673 Project Development and Donor Liaison Officer (P)
jobs.description:
Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) in Ghana (resident), Togo, and Benin, and in close collaboration with the relevant units at the Regional Office (RO) and Headquarters (HQ), the Project Development and Donor Liaison Officer will be responsible and accountable for supporting the coordination and facilitation of project development, donor and institutional reporting in the fields of migration management, emergency response, as well as assisting with liaison activities with counterparts in the government, UN agencies, and other relevant stakeholders in line with IOM’s regional and country strategies.

**Responsibilities**

1. Contribute to the development of results-based programmes and projects, concept notes and project proposals, in close coordination with the CoM, Project Managers, United Nations Country Team (UNCT), relevant donors, government counterparts and project partners, by providing technical inputs and support that respond to emerging trends and priorities and that are in compliance with IOM and donor interests and requirements.
2. Review resource requirements, document programmatic needs, gaps and opportunities. Contribute to the alignment to IOM global, regional and country strategies during project development and donor reporting, including supporting and promoting use of Strategic Results Framework (SRF) global results and indicators.
3. Support the endorsement process for concept notes and project proposals. Support the Project Managers in drafting donor reports in close coordination with relevant units in the Country Office (CO) and RO in line with IOM policies, standards and internal procedures.
4. Research potential and realistic funding opportunities among government and non-government donors, review calls for proposals and collect donor information. Draft donor profiles and guidance notes on donor priorities and assist with developing approaches to expand the IOM donor base.
5. Support effective working relationships with donor counterparts and project/programme partners, such as government authorities, diplomatic missions, and other relevant agencies and working groups.
6. In coordination with relevant Units in the CO, draft visibility and other resource mobilization materials and organize donor briefings and visits.
7. Capacity building and training activities in the field of programme development, donor and institutional reporting and the roll-out of the SRF for CO’s staff through workshops and seminars.
8. In support of knowledge management, maintain accurate, updated and pertinent records of all correspondence, project development and donor and institutional reporting files, and related information in IOM’s relevant software application.
9. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, International Development, Political or Social Sciences, Migration Studies, Law, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in supporting results-based project development and reporting, technical writing and editing, preferably in the international development/humanitarian sector;
- Proven experience in donor relations and grant management for specific donors of IOM’s interest;
- Demonstrated experience with Results-Based Management approach and other strategic planning approaches; and,
- Proven experience in donor report writing in humanitarian and/or development settings.

**Skills**

- Demonstrated communication, writing and organizational skills; ability to prepare clear and concise reports;
- Demonstrated knowledge of monitoring and evaluation concepts, approaches and methodologies;
- Proven analytical and planning skills; capacity to establish working relationships with
governmental authorities, national and international institutions and Non-Governmental Organizations;
- Demonstrated capacity to supervise and train support staff; ability to work effectively and harmoniously with colleagues from varied cultures and professional backgrounds;
- Demonstrated ability to work with accuracy under constraints and pressure; high sense of confidentiality, initiative and good judgment;
- Demonstrated personal commitment, efficiency, flexibility, drive for results, creative thinking; and,
- Good level of computer literacy, including database applications.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: 23559 Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Officer (P)
jobs.description:
Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) in Afghanistan and the direct supervision of the Head of the Programme Support Unit and in coordination with relevant units at Headquarters (HQ) and the Regional Office (RO), the Monitoring and Evaluation Officer will be responsible for leading the management of the monitoring, evaluation, learning, reporting and communicating functions of the Country Office (CO), supporting the CoM in identifying IOM-relevant project opportunities, developing the country strategy and project proposals and liaising with government counterparts, United Nations Country Team (UNCT), and other development partners, as necessary.

**Responsibilities**

**Institutional and Operational Set-Up**

1. Supervise and guide the implementation of the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) activities of the CO according to projects/ programmes/strategy result matrices and M&E plans, in close coordination with the Project/Programme Managers and other relevant IOM staff and partners.
2. Ensure adherence to existing Evaluation and Monitoring policies and guidelines and Results-Based Management (RBM) roadmaps, frameworks and guidance, including proper use of Project Information and Management Application (PRIMA) for monitoring, reporting and evaluation.
3. Contribute, in collaboration with the Regional M&E and Risk Management Officer, to the development of plans, tools and systems to monitor implementation of projects/programmes and/or strategies within the CO focusing on activities, results, expenditure, budget, risks and assumptions, in line with donor/UNCT requirements, IOM strategies, and institutional M&E and reporting requirements.
4. Ensure that risks are assessed and new ones identified during the regular monitoring of project activities, and where appropriate ensure that associated Project Risk Register Matrix and Risk Treatment plans are monitored and regularly reviewed.
5. Provide substantive inputs to strengthen the capacity of IOM staff and partners to carry out M&E activities in the CO through training, mentoring, and coaching.
6. Regularly update the evaluation and monitoring plans for projects/programmes/strategies at the CO, including identification of key performance questions, indicators, and parameters for monitoring and evaluating performance in line with the Strategic Results Framework (SRF), and share the evaluation plan with the Regional M&E and Risk Management Officer on a regular basis.
7. Actively engage in M&E activities for and with UN Agencies, UNCT, donors, government and external partners at country level, including on possible joint monitoring and evaluations, for instance in the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) Evaluation.
8. Document good practices and lessons learned through analysis of monitoring findings and evaluation reports, identify causes of potential bottlenecks and corrective measures, and facilitate discussion of related M&E and RBM findings and challenges with relevant IOM project staff, management, and partners.
9. Facilitate regular feedback from beneficiaries and stakeholders on activities and services provided through the organization’s support, in close coordination with field units and relevant focal points of CO.

**Reporting and Communication**

1. Support Project/Programme Managers in compiling periodic donor reports in line with the M&E plans and agreed reporting schedules, as well as the CoM/ Head of Office (HoO) in compiling data for UNCT reporting requirements.
2. Provide comprehensive inputs for materials requested by the UNCT/ Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) or individual agencies, Government institutions, Donors, IOM relevant Units at HQs, RO and/or other partners.
3. Monitor the work of Implementing Partners (IPs) by receiving and reviewing progress reports in a timely manner as per agreement with IOM, UN and donors' terms and conditions.
4. Provide technical support to IP to improve the quality of data collection, consolidation, analysis, and reporting through capacity building and regular monitoring visits to the field.
5. Support the CO’s communication strategy through documenting IOM activities such as capturing case studies, life-changing stories for donor/UN reports, updating CO’s social media accounts, and producing quarterly newsletters and local media briefings.
6. Contribute to the preparation of meetings and events, to include donor/UN briefings, donor visits, and conferences.
7. Manage submissions for the IOM global institutional reporting processes, including the Institutional Questionnaire.
8. Conduct M&E activities that can contribute to the management and analysis of migration trends and related data relevant for IOM in the country.

**Project Development Support**

1. Contribute to the identification of new project development opportunities in close coordination with CoM, Project/Programme Managers, and RO’s Thematic Specialists, and in line with IOM global frameworks and CO’s strategy.
2. Provide inputs for the development of project/programme logic, including Results Matrices and Theory of Change, and for the monitoring and evaluation sections of project proposals/strategies.
3. Ensure that adequate monitoring and evaluation costs are budgeted and advocated for as per IOM M&E policies, guidelines, and Project Handbook.
4. Participate in UN, donor, sectoral, working groups, and other meetings aimed at development of new projects, for instance within Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM) regional and national networks.
5. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Political Science, Business or Public Administration, International Studies or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in project/strategy conceptualisation, development, monitoring, reporting and evaluation;
- Experience in capacity-building activities, including design and delivery of trainings;
- Experience in liaising with governmental and diplomatic authorities as well as with national and international institutions;
- Demonstrated experience and familiarity in financial and business administration;
- Proven understanding and experience of internal and international migration issues in the country and in the region;
- Experience in organizing consultations, workshops and seminars with high-level stakeholders;
- In-depth knowledge and experience of the broad range of migration-related subject areas dealt with by the Organization;
- Demonstrated knowledge and experience of monitoring and evaluation concepts, approaches and techniques including qualitative and quantitative methods, participatory approaches, and evaluative methodologies; and,
- Demonstrated knowledge and experience of UN and bilateral donor programming and institutional requirements.

**Skills**

- Demonstrated writing and research skills;
- Excellent communication and analytical skills;
- High degree of judgment and initiative, ability to work with a high degree of independence within assigned areas;
- Demonstrated interpersonal and teamwork skills; and,
- Proven ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with people of diverse cultural and national backgrounds.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Career Development Specialist, NVPPA
jobs.description:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Program Background:**

The National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement (NVPPA) is a nationwide, fully virtual program through which the International Rescue Committee (IRC) serves newly arrived refugees under a cooperative agreement with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR). Participants receive career navigation, training, job placement support, and direct financial assistance to advance an individualized career goal. NVPPA operates alongside other federally funded programs, such as initial resettlement services and Matching Grant, and is designed to complement rather than replace or duplicate these programs.

**Job Overview**

The Career Development Specialist is the participant's primary point of contact in the program, working remotely with refugees across the country by phone, video, and online tools. From intake and eligibility verification through an approved Professional Advancement Plan (PAP), this position guides each participant toward their career goal, whether that means finding a training partner, completing credential evaluation and recertification, or moving forward with an approved vehicle purchase. The role coordinates closely with the Economic Empowerment Technical Unit, administrative and job development staff, and external resettlement partners to ensure participants move smoothly between services, while maintaining accurate case records and documentation in Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) in line with ORR reporting requirements and IRC financial controls.

**Major responsibilities:**

**Outreach and Intake**

- Conduct virtual outreach, intake, and enrollment for eligible participants, including verifying eligibility documentation.
- Coordinate with IRC offices, resettlement agencies, and local partners to identify and connect with eligible participants.

**Career Navigation**

- Complete a skills assessment with each participant and develop an individualized Professional Advancement Plan (PAP) that defines their career goal, pathway, and planned use of direct financial assistance.
- Review the PAP with each participant, provide feedback on the career goal, and confirm that proposed use of funds meets ORR eligible-use requirements.
- Provide ongoing navigation by phone and video to help participants access training, credential evaluation and recertification, and other approved supports.
- Research career advancement, certification, and vocational education opportunities across state and local labor markets.
- Connect participants to resources and services within IRC and in their local communities.
- Maintain working knowledge of credential evaluation services and state licensing requirements in high-demand fields, and carry a caseload of participants pursuing those pathways.

**Coordination**

- Work with the Economic Empowerment Technical Unit, Administrative Staff, and Job Development staff so participants move smoothly between navigation, training, and placement services, and to ensure financial assistance requests align with approved PAPs.
- Coordinate with other service providers, including PIR providers and Matching Grant employment specialists, to support co-enrollment and avoid duplication of services.

**Compliance**

- Maintain accurate, timely case files in Efforts to Outcomes (ETO), including documentation and the service and outcome data required for ORR reporting.
- Ensure documentation for each financial assistance request is complete before submission, consistent with IRC financial controls.

**Job Requirements (Simplified)**

- 1-2 years of demonstrated experience in a human services field, preferably in a nonprofit or social services setting.
- Strong written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to build rapport with clients by phone and video.
- Ability to deliver services remotely to clients across states and time zones, protect client confidentiality and sensitive documents, and work independently as part of a fully virtual team.
- Experience managing a high-volume caseload, with strong organization, prioritization, time management, and follow-through.
- Ability to build and maintain productive internal and external relationships.
- Ability to research and navigate workforce, education, and social service systems in unfamiliar local markets.
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office, video conferencing, and remote collaboration tools, and with tracking and reporting information in a database.
- Commitment to anti-racism, ongoing learning, and equitable service to all eligible clients.
- Fluency in spoken and written English.

**Preferred**

- Undergraduate degree in Social Work or a related field
- Experience in workforce development, career coaching, or case management.
- Lived experience as a refugee or immigrant.
- Experience with Efforts to Outcomes (ETO).
- Familiarity with credential evaluation, professional licensing, or recertification pathways.
- Fluency in an additional language relevant to current refugee populations.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $19-$28/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: CHEFFE OU CHEF DE PROJET H-PST - FRANCE
jobs.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Votre mission principale sera d'assurer le pilotage stratégique, opérationnel, financier et partenarial du projet H-PST (formation sécurité humanitaire) financé par ECHO et de garantir la bonne gouvernance du consortium, l'atteinte des résultats du projet et le déploiement d'un dispositif de formation harmonisé destiné au secteur humanitaire, en coordination avec les partenaires et les parties prenantes concernées.
Dans ce cadre, vous aurez pour responsabilités de :
Piloter la gouvernance et la coordination du consortium;
Assurer le pilotage et la mise en oeuvre du projet;
Piloter le développement du dispositif de formation H-PST
Coordonner le déploiement des formations et l'accompagnement des partenaires;
Assurer le suivi, l'évaluation et la capitalisation du projet;
Assurer la gestion contractuelle, financière et la diffusion des résultats du projet;
Contribuer au recrutement de l'équipe et la manager.

Profile :

Vous êtes titulaire d'une formation supérieure de niveau Master (Bac+5) en gestion de projet, relations internationales, action humanitaire, sécurité/sûreté, ingénierie de formation ou domaine connexe.
Vous avez une expérience confirmée dans le pilotage de projets complexes impliquant plusieurs acteurs et partenaires, ainsi que dans les domaines de la sécurité personnelle humanitaire, des formations HEAT/H-PST, de l'ingénierie pédagogique ou des dispositifs de formation de formateurs.
Vous avez une expérience dans la coordination de consortiums ou de mécanismes de gouvernance multipartites.
Vous avez une expérience avérée dans la gestion de financements institutionnels et le suivi des exigences contractuelles, budgétaires et de reporting.
Vous avez une expérience de management d'équipe et de coordination fonctionnelle de parties prenantes multiples dans le secteur humanitaire international.
Vous maîtrisez l'anglais.

Conditions d'emploi:
Statut : cadre Intégré - CDD de 15 mois à partir du 4 janvier 2027 - Temps plein
Lieu : Montreuil
Rémunération : de 46K à 55 K euros bruts annuels sur 13 mois selon expérience
Avantages: 25 jours par an de CP et 21 jours de RTT
Couverture santé, prévoyance : prise en charge à 80% par ACF
Dispositifs de maintien de salaire (maladie, maternité, paternité)
Indemnités Transport : prise en charge à 50% du forfait entre le domicile et le lieu de travail
Indemnités Tickets-restaurant (Carte déjeuner Up): prise en charge à 60% par l'association pour une valeur de 8euros
Ouvres sociales du CSE (chèques cadeaux, remboursement activités culturelles, ...)
Télétravail : ouvert à tous et toutes depuis le territoire métropolitaine
Temps de présentiels collectifs imposés / également obligatoires par l'employeur : pour les réunions et événements collectifs (jusqu'à 3 jours par mois) et 2 jours de présence obligatoire lors de votre intégration dans l'équipe
Indemnités de télétravail
Formation: Accès illimité et gratuit à la plateforme d'e-learning Talentsoft
ACF s'engage pour les personnes en situation de handicap et lutte activement contre toutes les formes de discrimination.

jobs.title: Assistant Safety Advisor – Syria (national staff only)
jobs.description:
**Organisation Background**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts. INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. INSO provides daily support to more than 1,500 NGOs operating in 24 of the world’s most insecure countries. INSO is registered in the Netherlands, with its headquarters located in The Hague, a city renowned for its international focus on peace and justice.

**INSO Syria**

The Syria program supports more than 290 NGOs delivering urgently needed aid and assistance to an estimated 13.1 million people across the country. First launched as an emergency response operation in 2014, INSO Syria has grown to become a program covering all Syrian governorates, with a Country Office in Damascus. The Syria conflict is unique and complex: you will find that every day is different and there is always more to learn.

**Job Summary**

Under the direct supervision of the Safety Advisor, you will collect and verify information and enter data into CHDC. You will assist the SA and the Deputy SA with the development and management of a local information network and provide liaison with NGOs using INSO services in the region.

**Main Responsibilities**

- Develop a diversified and consistent network of contacts at the communal and regional levels.
- Develop, verify, and summarise safety and security information in a concise and actionable format. Enter the information into CHDC.
- Proactively ensure daily liaison with field monitors and submit requests for information to deadlines.
- Assist the SA and the Deputy SA in the preparation of relevant reports, area assessments, and other INSO products.
- Assist the SA and the Deputy in visualising and analysing data by using charts and mapping tools.
- Help to enhance INSO information collection capacity in the region.
- Act at short notice with due regard to developing events.
- Ensure strict compliance with INSO HR, financial, and logistics procedures.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Experience**

- Minimum 2 years of relevant professional experience in security analysis, humanitarian coordination, or information management.
- Strong analytical and report-writing skills.
- Ability to produce clear, concise written products in English.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel required).
- Strong Arabic and English language skills (spoken and written).
- Prior field assessment experience is an asset.
- Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Security Studies, or a related field.

*Nice to Have:*

- Experience with databases or incident tracking systems.

**Core Competencies**

- Professionalism – Demonstrates neutrality, integrity, and ethical conduct in all interactions and responsibilities.
- Organisation – Manages time, priorities, and workloads effectively to ensure efficient task delivery.
- Resilience – Maintains performance and composure while working under pressure and tight deadlines.
- Accuracy – Ensures close attention to detail and precision in work, documentation, and processes.
- Communication – Builds positive relationships and communicates clearly and effectively with diverse stakeholders.

The successful candidate must demonstrate:

- Commitment to humanitarian principles.
- Political neutrality and impartiality.
- Integrity and professionalism.
- Respectful engagement with colleagues and partners.

**Terms & Conditions**

12-month renewable fixed-term contract, 1.75 working days annual leave per month, private health insurance coverage or allowance.

**INSO’s Safeguarding Policy**

INSO is fully committed to safe recruitment, selection and vetting of all potential new staff, trustees and volunteers. We ensure rigorous compliance with our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy throughout the recruitment process. INSO is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and the selected candidate will be required to undergo the relevant misconduct disclosure checks as part of the final hiring steps.

jobs.title: Spécialiste Contrôle Interne et Conformité
jobs.description:
INTERSOS est une Organisation Humanitaire Non Gouvernementale, à but non lucratif, qui a pour objectif d’assister les victimes de désastres naturels et de conflits armés. INTERSOS base son action sur les valeurs de la solidarité, de la justice, de la dignité humaine, de l’égalité des droits et des opportunités pour tous les peuples, du respect des diversités, de la cohabitation, de l’attention aux groupes sociaux les plus vulnérables.

## **TERMES DE RÉFÉRENCE**

- **Intitulé du poste :** Spécialiste Contrôle Interne et Conformité
- **Code :** SR-46-10333
- **Pays :** RCA (République centrafricaine)
- **Lieu d’affectation :** Bangui avec déplacement sur terrain dans les zones de mise en œuvre des projets
- **Date de prise de fonction :** 01/12/2026
- **Durée du contrat :** 6 mois
- **Sous la supervision de :** Chef de Mission
- **Supervision fonctionnelle :** N/A
- **Personnes à charge :** N/A
- **Type de lieu d'affectation :** sans famille

## **CONTEXTE GÉNÉRAL DU PROJET**

La République centrafricaine est confrontée depuis plus de deux décennies à des crises complexes et récurrentes, caractérisées par des dynamiques sécuritaires, sanitaires et climatiques.

Bien que des évolutions positives soient observées dans certaines zones, la situation reste fragile, avec des poches d’insécurité persistantes sur certains axes et localités, affectant l’accès aux services essentiels et les conditions de vie des populations.

Par ailleurs, le pays fait face à des chocs humanitaires récurrents, notamment des épidémies (dont le choléra), ainsi que des aléas climatiques tels que les inondations, qui aggravent la vulnérabilité des communautés.

Dans ce contexte, les besoins humanitaires demeurent élevés, en particulier dans les secteurs de l’accès à l’eau, de l’assainissement, de la santé et de la protection.

INTERSOS est présent en RCA depuis 2014 et met en œuvre des interventions humanitaires visant à répondre aux besoins des populations affectées, dans le respect des principes d’humanité, de neutralité, d’impartialité et d’indépendance.

L’organisation dispose d’un bureau de coordination à Bangui et d’une présence opérationnelle dans plusieurs préfectures, notamment la Kémo, Bamingui-Bangoran, Nana-Gribizi, Haute-Kotto, Ouham et Ouham-Pendé.

## **OBJECTIF GÉNÉRAL DE LA POSITION**

Le/La Spécialiste du Contrôle Interne et de la Conformité contribue au renforcement des mécanismes de contrôle interne, à la prévention de la fraude et au respect des politiques, procédures et exigences applicables au sein d’INTERSOS.

Il/Elle assure le traitement des signalements sensibles et la conduite des enquêtes relevant de son périmètre, réalise des contrôles et audits de conformité, et veille au suivi des risques ainsi qu’à la mise en œuvre des recommandations.

Il/Elle contribue également au renforcement des capacités du personnel en matière de conformité, de prévention de la fraude et de respect du cadre de sauvegarde de l’organisation.

## **PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS ET TÂCHES**

**Gestion des signalements sensibles et conduite des enquêtes**

- Assurer la conduite des enquêtes relatives aux signalements sensibles impliquant des membres du personnel, des volontaires, des partenaires ou des prestataires de services, conformément au cadre de sauvegarde d’INTERSOS et aux procédures opérationnelles relatives aux signalements et aux enquêtes (SOP Whistleblowing and Investigation).
- Formuler des recommandations sur les suites à donner aux signalements, sur la base des conclusions des enquêtes menées.
- Identifier les causes profondes des incidents et irrégularités constatés, et proposer des mesures correctives et préventives adaptées.
- Assurer, en coordination avec l’Auditeur interne au siège, la gestion et la mise à jour de la base de données en ligne dédiée aux signalements.

**Réalisation des audits de conformité et suivi des contrôles internes**

- Réaliser des audits internes de conformité, notamment des vérifications ponctuelles des fournisseurs, de la gestion des actifs et des stocks en entrepôt.
- Effectuer des contrôles inopinés (spot checks) afin de vérifier le respect des procédures internes et d’identifier les éventuelles irrégularités.
- Contribuer au respect des lois, réglementations, politiques et procédures internes applicables, notamment à travers des actions de sensibilisation et de formation.
- Coordonner la préparation et le suivi des rapports SCUML de l’EFCC ainsi que les vérifications ponctuelles liées aux questionnaires de l’EFCC.
- Collaborer avec les équipes concernées pour répondre aux demandes des bailleurs relatives à la conformité et aux contrôles internes.
- Localisation, coordination et reporting.

**Gestion des risques et suivi des recommandations d’audit**

- Tenir à jour la matrice des constats d’audit et des recommandations, et assurer le suivi de leur mise en œuvre.
- Contribuer aux évaluations des risques et tenir à jour le registre des risques et des audits, en collaboration avec les équipes programmes et opérations.
- Assurer le suivi auprès des départements concernés de la mise en œuvre des mesures correctives et des engagements formulés dans les rapports d’audit.
- Veiller au respect des exigences de conformité définies par INTERSOS, les bailleurs de fonds et les autorités compétentes, et assurer le suivi des actions nécessaires à leur mise en œuvre.

**Renforcement des capacités du personnel en matière de conformité**

- Organiser et animer des formations et des séances de sensibilisation à destination du personnel sur les questions de conformité, de prévention de la fraude et de respect des procédures internes.
- Informer et accompagner les équipes dans la compréhension et l’application des politiques, procédures et exigences de conformité applicables au sein d’INTERSOS.

**Participation aux réunions avec les bailleurs sur la prévention de la fraude et la conformité**

- Participer aux réunions avec les bailleurs de fonds portant sur la prévention de la fraude, le contrôle interne et les questions de conformité, et contribuer aux échanges relevant de son domaine d’expertise.
- Ces tâches ne sont pas exhaustives. Le/la titulaire du poste peut être amené(e) à accomplir d’autres tâches et responsabilités en lien avec sa fonction, selon les besoins opérationnels de l’organisation et les instructions de sa hiérarchie.

## **PROFIL REQUIS**

### **Éducation**

- Être titulaire d’un diplôme universitaire en audit, comptabilité, finance, gestion des risques, droit, administration ou dans un domaine pertinent.

### **Expérience professionnelle**

- Justifier d’une expérience professionnelle pertinente en contrôle interne, audit, conformité, gestion des risques ou investigation.
- Une expérience dans une ONG internationale ou dans le secteur humanitaire constitue un atout.
- Une expérience dans la conduite d’enquêtes liées à des signalements sensibles et dans la prévention de la fraude constitue un atout.

### **Exigences professionnelles**

- Bonne connaissance des principes de contrôle interne, d’audit et de conformité.
- Capacité à analyser les risques, à conduire des investigations et à formuler des recommandations adaptées.
- Bonne maîtrise des outils de suivi, de reporting et de gestion des risques.
- Capacité à traiter des informations confidentielles avec discrétion et impartialité.
- Bonne maîtrise des outils informatiques, notamment de la suite Microsoft Office.

### **Langues**

- Maîtrise du français, à l’oral comme à l’écrit.
- Maîtrise des langues locales constitue un atout.
- La maîtrise de l’anglais constitue un atout.

### **Exigences personnelles**

- Intégrité, impartialité et sens élevé de l’éthique professionnelle.
- Discrétion et respect strict de la confidentialité.
- Rigueur, esprit d’analyse et souci du détail.
- Autonomie, sens de l’organisation et capacité à gérer les priorités.
- Bonnes capacités de communication et aptitude à collaborer avec différents interlocuteurs.

## **CONDITIONS GÉNÉRALES ET AVANTAGES**

- **Fourchette de salaire :** 05 - …
- **Hébergement :** Shared Guesthouse
- **R&R :** Le personnel d'INTERSOS tenu de travailler pendant des périodes prolongées dans des lieux d'affectation soumis à des conditions périlleuses, stressantes et difficiles bénéficie d'une période régulière et obligatoire de repos et de récupération (R&R). Cette mesure vise à protéger sa santé et son bien-être et à garantir une performance de travail optimale lors de la reprise de ses fonctions, tout en préservant la capacité opérationnelle de l'Organisation. Les avantages liés au R&R ne constituent pas une compensation financière pour le degré de pénibilité et d'insécurité d'un lieu d'affectation. Admissibilité : les membres du personnel recrutés en tant que personnel international de terrain dont le contrat indique un lieu d'affectation R&R comme lieu d'affectation principal et dont la durée du contrat est égale ou supérieure à 4 mois civils. R&R : il consiste en 7 jours de récupération psychophysique toutes les 8/10/12 semaines, selon le lieu d'affectation. Une indemnité de 1 000 € y est associée.
- **Rémunération :** la rémunération mensuelle pour chaque poste est définie conformément à la grille salariale et à la grille de fonctions standard internationale d'INTERSOS, en tenant compte de l'expérience du candidat sélectionné. Elle est communiquée lors de l'entretien avec les ressources humaines, ou en tout état de cause lors de la première étape du processus de sélection.
- **Transport :** vols A/R pour l'humanitaire. Pour toute mission d'une durée d'au moins 9 mois, un billet d'avion supplémentaire vers le pays de résidence et le retour sur le lieu de mission sont pris en charge par l'Organisation pour le travailleur humanitaire.
- **Assurance médicale :** assurance accidents et décès ; assurance responsabilité civile ; remboursement des vaccins, du certificat médical et du test PCR pour le déploiement ; soutien psychosocial sur demande pour le travailleur humanitaire.
- **Visa :** INTERSOS prend en charge les frais et l'assistance pour l'obtention du visa pour le travailleur humanitaire.
- **Congés annuels :** 2,5 jours par mois.
- **Formation d’intégration :** cours d'orientation en ligne : chaque nouveau membre du personnel reçoit une formation préparatoire avant le départ, adéquate pour fournir les informations nécessaires relatives à la structure d'INTERSOS et aux principaux processus décisionnels et outils de travail, afin de faciliter son intégration au sein de l'Organisation.
- **Remarque 1 :** INTERSOS applique une « politique d'apprentissage et de développement » (Learning & Development Policy) qui inclut la possibilité de bénéficier de formations et de participer à des formations internes et externes. La priorité sera accordée au personnel travaillant pour INTERSOS depuis plus de deux ans.
- **Remarque 2 :** la classification des lieux d'affectation avec accompagnement, R&R et sans accompagnement est soumise à des critères de sécurité, d'accès aux services de santé et d'éducation, et n'est pas négociable.

## **COMMENT POSTULER:**

Les candidats intéressés sont invités à postuler en suivant le lien ci-dessous:

[https://www.intersos.org/en/field-eng/#intersosorg-vacancies/vacancy-details/6ae2fcddb8cf9539fc720855/](https://www.intersos.org/en/field-eng/#intersosorg-vacancies/vacancy-details/6ae2fcddb8cf9539fc720855/)

Veuillez noter que notre processus de candidature est composé de **3 étapes très rapides**: **s’inscrire** (incluant votrenom, mail, mot de passe et nationalité), se **connecter** et **postule**r en joignant un **CV** en version **PDF**. Avec cette plateforme, les candidats pourront suivre l'historique de leurs candidatures avec INTERSOS.
Veuillez également mentionner le nom, le poste et les coordonnées **d'au moins trois références: deux superviseurs hiérarchiques et un référent RH**. Les membres de la famille sont à exclure.

**Seuls les candidats sélectionnés pour le premier entretien seront contactés.**

jobs.title: Global Roving and Emergency Response Humanitarian Access and Safety (HAS) Manager
jobs.description:
**What we’re looking for:**

Are you an experienced humanitarian access and security professional ready to make an impact across some of the world’s most challenging emergency contexts?

NRC is looking for a **Global Roving and Emergency Response Humanitarian Access and Safety (HAS) Manager** to provide expert guidance, operational support and training to our teams worldwide. This is a dynamic, field-facing role that involves deploying to NRC operations to strengthen humanitarian access, safety and security risk management. You will work closely with country leadership, emergency response teams and the Global HAS Unit, reporting to the Global Expert HAS Adviser – Strategy and Planning, with direct field-level management during deployments.

As part of NRC’s global HAS team, you will contribute to enabling principled humanitarian action while protecting the safety and wellbeing of our staff, partners and the communities we serve. The team develops and oversees the policies, systems and standards that help NRC deliver assistance safely, even in complex emergencies and protracted displacement settings.

*Essential requirement:* Fluency in both English and French is required.

**What you will do:**

- Lead and monitor the implementation and compliance of NRC security risk management framework with the aim of managing safety and security risks towards NRC staff, project participants, and assets
- Develop NRC’s approach to humanitarian access at a country level, including through developing Access Plans, and assisting country offices in navigating complex negotiations and dilemmas around adherence to humanitarian principles
- Provide technical advice in developing or reviewing country office HAS Operational Plans and budgets as part of their strategy development/review processOn occasion, may be required to act as a Regional Head of HAS during leave periods or vacancies
- Ensure that access, and security risk management solutions adhere to the principles and policies of NRC, as well as the humanitarian principles (of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence) and International Humanitarian Law (IHL)
- Mentor and build capacity of HAS staff/teams in the field during deployments
- When deemed necessary and with the approval of management teams, establish networking and coordination mechanisms in areas where they are assessed to be essential but currently do not exist
- Provide technical support to the selection of and capacity sharing with, local implementing partners
- Upon request, assist in conducting access severity assessments and delivery of trainings on humanitarian access negotiations and engagement, internally as well as to local actors and implementing partners
- Any other tasks as delegated by the line manager

Please download a more detailed[**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAeIa4ZXmPHTIRo4ujMFBkwAU5l4KC4Doz7fOUUUrvIkJI?e=qNhuYS) for more specific and generic duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- Minimum 5 years of experience from working as a manager, such as an Area Manager or Country Director in a humanitarian/recovery context with responsibilities for safety and security
- Proven, solid and relevant experience in HAS work, preferably in the NGO (non-governmental organisations) environment
- Experience in administration and budgeting for HAS roles and activities.
- Previous experience from working in complex and volatile contexts (posted in a high-risk environment)
- Experience in gathering, organizing and analysing HAS related information
- Flexible and with a strong team spirit.
- Fluency in English and French, both written and verbal required.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Oslo, Norway (Global Roving)
- Contract: 1year.
- Travel: Up to 75%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s Mobile salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.
