jobs.description:
**A propos de la Chaîne de l'Espoir**

La Chaîne de l’Espoir est une ONG internationale fondée en 1994. Elle a pour vocation de renforcer les systèmes de santé pour donner à chacun et en particulier aux enfants les mêmes chances de survie et de développement.

Nous intervenons dans 25 pays par une approche globale, centrée sur l’enfant mais également sur les mères et les communautés défavorisées :

- Prévention et dépistage dès le plus jeune âge, notamment dans le cadre de programmes de santé à l’école.
- Soin et chirurgie, afin de répondre aux besoins les plus urgents des enfants et de leurs mères.
- Formation et transferts de compétences aux équipes locales grâce à notre réseau international d’experts dans tous les domaines de la chirurgie.
- Construction et équipement de structures hospitalières adaptées aux besoins locaux.

**Poste et missions**

Rattaché à la Directrice générale, vous pilotez l’audit, le contrôle interne et la gestion des risques au siège et dans les bureaux pays. Vous mobilisez les managers, faites aboutir les mesures correctrices et accompagnez les équipes sans vous substituer à elles.

Vous rendez compte à la Direction générale et au Comité d’audit et de contrôle interne (CACI). Vous exercez également, en toute indépendance, les fonctions de Délégué à la protection des données (DPO) et cogérez la cellule de signalement avec la DRH.

**Cartographie et gestion des risques**

- Actualiser les cartographies des risques de l’association et des bureaux pays avec leurs responsables ; suivre les mesures de maîtrise et alerter sur les risques majeurs.

**Audit interne**

- Définir les audits prioritaires, les conduire au siège et sur le terrain, puis formuler des recommandations hiérarchisées et opérationnelles.
- Piloter le suivi des plans d’action avec les managers, vérifier leur réalisation, faire remonter les blocages et appuyer, si besoin, les audits bailleurs.

**Contrôle interne, procédures et conformité**

- Faire évoluer les procédures et outils de contrôle interne avec les services et veiller à leur appropriation et application, au siège comme sur le terrain.
- Superviser la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme (LAB/FT), le criblage des parties prenantes et la gestion des dérogations.

**Protection des données personnelles – fonction DPO**

- Conseiller les services et référents RGPD ; suivre la documentation des traitements, les demandes d’exercice des droits et les incidents de données personnelles.
- Contrôler la conformité RGPD, prioriser les recommandations, vérifier les actions mises en œuvre par les services et alerter la DG, dans le respect de l’indépendance du DPO.

**Éthique et cellule de signalement**

- Sensibiliser à la prévention de la fraude, de la corruption, des conflits d’intérêts et de l’exploitation, des abus et du harcèlement sexuels (PSEAH).
- Cogérer avec la DRH la cellule de signalement ; veiller au traitement confidentiel et impartial des alertes, au suivi des mesures correctrices et à un circuit indépendant en cas de conflit d’intérêts.

**Reporting, gouvernance et CACI**

- Fournir chaque mois à la DG un tableau de bord priorisé (risques, audits, contrôle interne, RGPD et plans d’action) ; alerter sur les risques critiques et proposer les arbitrages nécessaires.
- Préparer avec la trésorière, présidente du CACI, les réunions, rapports et comptes rendus ; suivre les décisions et recommandations.

## Profil recherché

**Formation et expériences**

- Bac+5 en audit, contrôle interne, gestion des risques, conformité, finance ou domaine comparable ; formations complémentaires en RGPD, enquêtes internes ou prévention de la fraude appréciées.
- Au moins 8 ans d’expérience en audit, contrôle interne, risques ou conformité. Une expérience en ONG internationale ou organisation comparable, au siège ou sur le terrain, est fortement souhaitée.
- **Expériences avérées :** cartographie des risques, audits, déploiement du contrôle interne et conduite de plans d’action transversaux avec des résultats démontrés.
- **Atouts supplémentaires :** expérience DPO, gestion de signalements et d’enquêtes sensibles, criblage, audits bailleurs et coordination avec des fonctions support et opérationnelles.

**Compétences et qualités requises**

- **Leadership transversal :** mobiliser sans autorité hiérarchique, responsabiliser les managers et obtenir des résultats concrets sans faire à leur place.
- **Analyse et décision :** hiérarchiser les risques, rédiger des recommandations claires et produire des tableaux de bord utiles aux arbitrages.
- **Intégrité et discernement :** traiter les situations sensibles avec indépendance, confidentialité, impartialité, diplomatie et fermeté.
- **Pédagogie et écoute :** convaincre, former, accompagner le changement et conduire des entretiens, y compris délicats.
- **Bailleurs :** connaître les exigences des partenaires français (AFD, CDCS), européens (ECHO, INTPA) et onusiens, ainsi que les contraintes du terrain.
- **RGPD :** disposer des connaissances requises pour exercer la fonction de DPO avec indépendance de jugement.
- **Outils :** très bonne maîtrise d’Excel, Word et PowerPoint ; bonne pratique de SharePoint et Teams pour la gestion documentaire.
- **Langues :** excellente maîtrise du français et anglais professionnel, à l’écrit comme à l’oral.
- **Organisation :** autonomie, sens des priorités, méthode, disponibilité et flexibilité.
- **Engagement :** adhésion aux principes humanitaires et au code d’éthique de La Chaîne de l’Espoir, avec pragmatisme.

**Conditions**

- Statut cadre – CDI
- Date de démarrage souhaitée : 15 décembre 2026
- Mutuelle prise en charge à 80%
- Remboursement abonnement transport à hauteur de 50 % ou indemnité mobilité durable (vélo) de 45 euros/mois
- Tickets Repas d’une valeur de 12,10 euros pris en charge à 60%
- Charte de télétravail : jusqu’à 3 jours par semaine après le premier mois en présentiel
- 23 jours de RTT annuel
- Fourchette salariale : entre 45 600 et 50 400 euros brut annuel selon profil et expérience
- CE: chèques cadeaux

jobs.title: Request for Quotation for Final Independent Project Evaluation service, for the Italian project
jobs.description:
**Request for Quotation for Final Independent Project Evaluation service, for the project titled “Towards More and Better Employment through Enhanced Support to Private Sectors in Southern Iraq – with a Focus on Green Business”**

**2. Background information**
**Private sector development in Iraq is challenged by several factors, as the economy is largely dominated by the oil sector, and state-owned enterprises further impede incentives for private sector growth and diversification in the wider economy. Moreover, local firms struggle to become competitive within national and international markets, and an abundance of cheap imports combined with low levels of investment has hindered the development of nascent domestic activities1. Iraq is also known for a challenging business environment, which makes it difficult for “start-ups” and/or MSMEs to flourish and expand their business in the formal economy and green businesses. According to the World Bank report in 2020, Iraq is ranked 172 out of 190 countries for “ease of doing business”2. This relates in particular to the financial and time-related costs of setting up businesses, which the report estimated take 26.5 days on average and cost about 14.6% of income per capita.**
**Another factor that halts private sector development is access to credit, where Iraq is ranked 186 out of 190 countries in the world. ILO research on financial inclusion from 2019 highlights several challenges to accessing credit and formal financing services3. The banking sector in Iraq is considered relatively small with limited capacity, leading to strong competition from informal financial service providers. The previous illiquidity of banks has also resulted in low levels of trust among the population in the banking sector, while private-sector banks consider many SMEs to be very high risk, thus reducing the likelihood of lending to what effectively represents most enterprises in Iraq. A survey conducted in 2020 by UNDP on MSMEs, covering Baghdad, Basra and Nineveh (where 20% of the nation’s MSMEs are located) found that only 1 percent of micro-enterprises held bank accounts, rising to 2.6 percent among small enterprises and 16 percent among medium enterprises, while 30 percent of enterprises had attempted but failed to obtain financing, and 55 percent showed reluctance to borrow4. To support SME’s access to finance, the Central Bank of Iraq initiated a “One Trillion Iraqi Dinars Initiative5” in 2014, but uptake was identified as low, partly related to the difficulty of finding bankable projects but also due to the lack of guarantee required by the banks from the MSMEs.**
**Lack of business management skills and financial literacy, coupled with lack of access to credit and loan services, makes it even more complex for entrepreneurs and enterprises to startup businesses in Iraq. Furthermore, Iraq's private sector is characterized by high rates of informality and a decent work deficit.**
**Iraq is characterized by a “demographic window of opportunity” with a very large young population and a working-age population growing at a higher rate than the overall population, but is currently unable to catalyse on this opportunity, as job creation is not keeping up with the growing size of the workforce6. The situation is considered a “jobs crisis of unprecedented proportions”7**
**Despite all the above-mentioned challenges, the sector has enormous potential for growth and job creation if there is an enabling business environment for MSMEs. The ILO, having the expertise and experience globally, in the region and in Iraq, namely: building on its well-established business and financial management tools, and its previous agreement with the Central Bank of Iraq, aspires to**
achieve the following two objectives while creating more and better jobs through this project in two governorates of Southern Iraq, Basra and Muthanna. These are: 1) Improve the business ecosystem for MSMEs in Iraq to grow and thrive through policy options, along with national and subnational dialogue amongst key stakeholders in private sector development; and 2) Capacitate and empower national/subnational financial and non-financial institutions to better support entrepreneurs and MSMEs to unleash their full potential.
The ILO signed the development cooperation agreement with the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, and the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS) dated 09 March 2023 to implement the project. The project intends to deliver the following three outcomes while aspiring to attain the aforementioned key objectives:
1\. Enhanced business support ecosystem for MSMEs to grow and thrive with a focus on the green economy.
2\. Improved business and financial management skills at the meso and micro levels (institutional and individual).
3\. Improved financial inclusion of start-up businesses and MSMEs with a focus on the green economy.
The logical framework and Theory of Change (ToC), which depict the underlying results chain, indicators, targets, sources of verification, and assumptions regarding each project objective, can be found in Annex 1.
This project is designed to contribute towards the achievement of several objectives of the current Decent Work Country Programme (DWCP) for Iraq (2019-2023). In particular, it contributes to the achievement of Outcome 4, which is creating more and better employment opportunities, ensuring that private sector development supports the much-needed creation of new jobs.
Moreover, it also contributes to the accomplishment of some important objectives of the ILO Programme & Budget (P&B) 2022-2023, which set out the strategic objectives and expected outcomes for the organization’s work, Outcome 4: Sustainable enterprises as generators of employment and promoters of innovation and decent work. The project's implementation is also expected to contribute to achieving the Country Programme Outcomes (CPO) IRQ 126 and IRQ 127.
Most importantly, the project contributes to the attainment of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) under the UNSDCF (2020-2024) for Iraq under strategic priority 2: Growing the Economy for All, especially in what concerns the promotion of inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment, and decent work for all (SDG 8), target 8.5 “achieve full and productive employment and decent work for all women and men, including for young people and persons with disabilities, and equal pay for work of equal value”.
All proposed activities have been looked into through a gender and disability inclusion perspective and reinforce equal consideration of women and Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) while implementing the activities.
Project management set-up and implementation arrangement: The governance structure of the project is led by a project Steering Committee comprised of concerned Ministries from the Government of Iraq (MoLSA, CBI, MoT, MoP), Social Partners (Workers’ and Employers’ organizations), Chamber of Commerce, IFI, MFI, and Trade Unions, which was established in the early implementation phase of the project. The Steering Committee has been overseeing implementation, facilitating

coordination and communication with policymakers, central and local authorities, other service providers and donors. The Steering Committee held one annual meeting to review project progress and capture lessons learned.
At the local government level, the Directorate of Labour and Social Affairs, Directorate of Youth and Sport and Directorate of Environment are the main counterparts of the project. The ILO has also been extensively engaging with Business Development Service (BDS) providers, TVET centres, development partners and civil society organisations) to strengthen collaboration in delivering services through the centre.
The project is implemented under the overall guidance and supervision of the ILO Country Coordinator based in Baghdad, with the project team based in Baghdad and Basra that includes the Project Manager and National Senior Project Officer who are responsible for overall planning, technical guidance, activity implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting of the project in close collaboration with local implementing partners.
Operational Support Unit (OSU) stationed in Erbil and Baghdad provides administrative and financial services to the project team. The Enterprise Development and Employment Specialists of the ILO Beirut DWT backstop the project. Programme Support Unit at the Regional Office for Arab States (ROAS) – Beirut provides administrative support to the project. ENTRPRISE and SECTOR departments at Headquarters provide technical support to the project.
Short-term International/National experts services were also provided for preparing technical support, guidelines, training materials, supervision and other required assignments.

jobs.title: Request for Proposals: Nationwide Assessment of Digital Safety Preparedness in Ukraine's Education System
jobs.description:
Finn Church Aid (FCA) invites qualified research organizations, consulting companies, and individual consultants to submit proposals for conducting a nationwide assessment of digital safety and cybersecurity readiness within Ukraine's education system.

The assessment will contribute to the second phase of the Digital Shield Ukraine initiative, which aims to strengthen the protection of children and adolescents from online threats by improving digital safety competencies, institutional preparedness, and cooperation between educational institutions, law enforcement agencies, and child protection services.

## Scope of Services

The selected service provider will be responsible for:

- Conducting a nationally representative quantitative survey of at least 1,200 teaching and non-teaching education staff.
- Conducting additional assessments among pupils and students, including interviews, focus group discussions, and competency-based assessments.
- Assessing the institutional readiness of educational institutions to prevent, identify, and respond to digital threats.
- Examining risks related to cyberbullying, online manipulation, fraud, grooming, recruitment through digital platforms, and other emerging online threats.
- Reviewing relevant Ukrainian legislation, policies, and applicable EU standards.
- Assessing inter-agency coordination and existing reporting and referral mechanisms.
- Developing a Digital Safety and Cybersecurity Readiness Index and institutional self-assessment tools.
- Preparing comprehensive analytical reports, baseline indicators, and evidence-based recommendations for Digital Shield Ukraine – Phase 2.

## Required Qualifications

Applicants should demonstrate:

- Relevant experience in conducting research, evaluations, or assessments in education, child protection, digital safety, cybersecurity, or related fields.
- Experience applying quantitative and qualitative research methods.
- Capacity to conduct research across different regions of Ukraine.
- Availability of qualified specialists with expertise in research methodology, statistical analysis, digital safety, safeguarding, and relevant legal frameworks.
- Ability to deliver high-quality research outputs in accordance with the Terms of Reference and the established implementation timeline.

Detailed eligibility requirements and evaluation criteria are provided in the Terms of Reference.

jobs.title: Communication Officer_Maiduguri
jobs.description:
**Job Purpose**

Contribute to the **implementation of operational communication strategy and the strengthening of external communications** in the mission according to INTERSOS standards.

Aim at **building INTERSOS visibility, acceptance and leverage** inside the country.

Focus on media alert, local media management and content diffusion and support the production of quality multimedia materials.

**Reporting to:**

**Hierarchical:** Communication Coordinator (in absence: Head of Mission)

**Functional**: HQ Communication Coordinator

**Key Responsibilities**:

**Internal Communications and Accountability**

- Help in promoting INTERSOS external communications principles and material towards the National Staffs. Sensitize National Staffs about potential external communications risks
- Monitor the international and national media and social media highlighting any relevant content for the humanitarian response in the country and for INTERSOS’ programmes
- Implement an ‘early warning system’ on national/regional issues and news
- In collaboration with Project/Programme Managers, ensure the respect of visibility guidelines and donors’ compliance
- Ensure the respect of INTERSOS’ protection, communications, and privacy policies and guidelines
- Ensure the proper allocation and management of the communication budget at country level, in coordination with the Finance department
- Provide technical training to staff members to increase their ability of producing multimedia content material

Education

Professional experience

jobs.title: 23705 Project Officer (Disaster Risk Management (DRM)) (P)
jobs.description:
IOM South Sudan implements a broad portfolio of programmes across humanitarian coordination and response, resilience, peacebuilding, transition and development, working closely with the Government of South Sudan, communities, development partners and other stakeholders. Within its community resilience portfolio, IOM implements programmes aimed at strengthening resilience to climate-related shocks, disaster risk and displacement, including the Regional Climate Resilience Program (RCRP), implemented in partnership with the Government of South Sudan with financing from the World Bank. The programme seeks to strengthen flood resilience and reduce the impacts of flooding in targeted areas of South Sudan through flood risk management, climate-resilient infrastructure and strengthened institutional capacity.

Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) and the direct supervision of the Project Manager (Community Resilience) in Juba, and in close coordination with relevant IOM units and government counterparts, the Project Officer (Disaster Risk Management (DRM)) will be responsible and accountable for supporting the implementation of DRM and flood resilience activities under Regional Climate Resilience Program (RCRP) and across IOM South Sudan's community resilience portfolio. The Project Officer (DRM) will provide technical support on flood risk assessments, hydrological and hydraulic studies, infrastructure design and implementation of flood mitigation works, including dykes, drainage systems, culverts, embankments and other climate-resilient infrastructure. The Project Officer (DRM) will also support the technical review of designs and specifications, monitoring of construction works and quality assurance activities, and assist with the coordination of DRM governance and institutional capacity-building activities, and support the integration of disaster risk reduction and climate resilience into programme planning and implementation.

**Responsibilities**

1. Provide technical support for the planning, design, and implementation of flood risk management and climate-resilient infrastructure under RCRP, including dykes, drainage systems, culverts, embankments, and related works, to support technically sound, climate-resilient, and sustainable investments.
2. Review and provide technical inputs to flood risk assessments, hydrological and hydraulic modelling, feasibility studies, engineering designs, drawings, technical specifications, bills of quantities and other technical documentation, identifying issues and recommending appropriate technical solutions in accordance with applicable standards and project requirements.
3. Monitor the implementation of flood mitigation infrastructure through regular field visits and technical reviews, assessing construction progress, quality of works and compliance with approved designs, specifications, environmental and social requirements and agreed workplans, and flagging technical or implementation issues and recommending appropriate corrective actions to the Project Manager.
4. Support technical coordination with the Government of South Sudan, engineering consultants, contractors and other relevant stakeholders on infrastructure design and implementation, flood risk management and DRM, including through participation in technical meetings, site inspections and review processes.
5. Support the development and implementation of disaster risk management and institutional capacity-building activities, including DRM training, risk-informed planning, preparedness, operation and maintenance arrangements and strengthening of relevant national, state and local government structures.
6. Support the integration of disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation, environmental sustainability, community engagement, protection and inclusion considerations into infrastructure planning, design and implementation, supporting resilient and sustainable programme outcomes.
7. Monitor assigned technical and programme activities and prepare technical inputs for project reporting, including progress updates, technical briefs, presentations and other documentation, identifying implementation constraints, risks and emerging issues and proposing appropriate follow-up actions to the Project Manager.
8. Contribute technical inputs to guidance, lessons learnt and knowledge products on flood risk management, climate-resilient infrastructure and DRM, documenting good practices and supporting their application across IOM South Sudan programming.
9. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Civil Engineering, Water Resources Engineering, Hydraulic Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Disaster Risk Management, Climate Change/Climate Governance, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in the planning, design, implementation and/or technical oversight of flood risk management and climate-resilient infrastructure, including dykes, drainage systems, culverts, embankments or similar infrastructure;
- Experience in reviewing engineering designs, drawings, technical specifications, bills of quantities and other technical documentation related to infrastructure works;
- Experience in monitoring construction works, including field inspections, assessment of progress and quality, identification of technical issues and follow-up on corrective actions;
- Experience with flood risk assessments, hydrological and/or hydraulic studies and modelling, including application of technical findings to infrastructure planning and design;
- Experience in disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation and/or resilience programming, preferably including institutional capacity building and risk-informed planning;
- Experience coordinating with government authorities, engineering consultants, contractors, communities and other technical stakeholders in the implementation of infrastructure or DRM programmes;
- Experience working in humanitarian, recovery, stabilisation or development contexts, preferably in fragile or conflict-affected environments; and,
- Experience working in South Sudan or a comparable operational context is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Demonstrated technical knowledge of flood risk management, climate-resilient infrastructure and disaster risk reduction;
- Ability to review and interpret engineering designs, drawings, technical specifications and bills of quantities;
- Demonstrated knowledge of relevant engineering standards, construction quality assurance and infrastructure operation and maintenance principles;
- Proficiency in relevant engineering and technical software, including AutoCAD and/or GIS applications; knowledge of hydrological/hydraulic modelling software is an advantage;
- Demonstrated analytical, technical writing, reporting and communication skills; and,
- Demonstrated proficiency in standard office software, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Social Cohesion Officer - MMC, Jere and Mafa
jobs.description:
## Key responsibilities

### 1. Conflict and context analysis

- Carry out a conflict and do-no-harm analysis at each facility site. Identify the groups involved, what divides and what connects them, past tensions, power dynamics and risks linked to the facility.
- Map stakeholders for each facility: landowning families, traditional leaders, host community members, returnees, IDPs, women and youth groups, and government offices. Note each group's interests and expectations.
- Update the analysis every quarter. Advise the Project Manager on conflict risks before key decisions on land, membership, plot allocation or benefits.

### 2. Ownership and land tenure process

- Lead the ownership and tenure audit. Collect and review Phase 1 MoUs, land donation letters, Certificates or Rights of Occupancy, community resolutions and site records.
- Facilitate consultations with landowning families, first separately and then jointly with government and communities, using free, prior and informed consent principles.
- Support negotiation of the land-use instrument for each site (long-term lease, conditional donation or regularisation through the Ministry of Lands) and of the landowner recognition and benefit package.
- Draft the Tripartite Facility Management Agreements with the legal adviser. Coordinate their signing by the lead MDA or LGA, the cooperative and the landowning family or traditional institution.
- Organise public validation meetings where each agreement is explained in local languages and a summary is displayed at the facility.

### 3. Governance structures

- Facilitate transparent selection of members and supervised elections of the Facility Management Committees, with protected seats for a Women's Lead, a Youth Lead and a landowner representative.
- Support each group to draft its constitution and bye-laws, including term limits, removal procedures, conflict-of-interest rules and a code of conduct.
- Set up and support the LGA Facility Oversight Committees in MMC, Jere and Mafa. Provide technical support to the secretariat of the State Asset Oversight Committee.
- Train committees in leadership, transparent decision-making, inclusive participation and accountability to members.
- Put the safeguards against elite capture in place: public display of membership lists and plot allocations, quarterly social audits, and General Assembly meetings.

### 4. Social cohesion and peacebuilding

- Facilitate community dialogues between landowners, host communities, IDPs and returnees, women and youth, and government officials, to agree a shared vision for each facility.
- Lead the development and signing of a Government–Community Compact in each LGA, setting out what government and communities each commit to.
- Organise landowner recognition events at commissioning, together with traditional and government leaders.
- Coordinate quarterly joint monitoring visits and the twice-yearly community open days.
- Set up, train and mentor Peace and Grievance Committees in mediation and dispute resolution. Make sure they include traditional, religious, women, youth, landowner and IDP/returnee representatives.
- Mediate disputes over land, access, water allocation, membership and benefits directly. Escalate unresolved cases through the agreed path: facility committee, then traditional leader and LGA mediation, then the Facility Oversight Committee.

### 5. Early warning and accountability

- Maintain a log of tensions, disputes and how they were resolved. Report it every two months to the LGA Oversight Committees and monthly to the Project Manager.
- Make sure grievances are linked to the Feedback and Complaints Response Mechanism (FCRM). Refer protection concerns to the Protection focal point.
- Help design and analyse the social cohesion perception survey (baseline and endline) with the MEAL Officer.

### 6. Supervision of community mobilisers

- Plan and supervise the community and committee work of the three community mobilisers.
- Train them in facilitation, mediation basics, conflict sensitivity and safe referral.
- Review their reports, and check the quality and inclusiveness of meetings they organise.

### 7. Handover readiness

- Assess the ownership, governance, inclusion and cohesion criteria of the handover readiness scorecard for each facility.
- Document lessons learned on ownership resolution and social cohesion for WFP and partners.

### Cross-cutting duties

- Stay impartial and be seen to be impartial. Never take sides in disputes or make commitments on behalf of government or landowners.
- Make sure at least 40% of members of every governance structure are women and youth, and that persons with disabilities, returnees and IDPs take part meaningfully.
- Follow PSEA, safeguarding, confidentiality and security procedures.
- Carry out any other reasonable duties related to the project, as assigned by the Project

**Essential requirements:**

## **Qualifications, experience and competencies**

### Education

- **Essential:** a university degree (B.Sc or HND) in Peace and Conflict Studies, Sociology, Political Science, Law, Public Administration, Development Studies or a related social science.
- **Desirable:** a Master's degree in Peace and Conflict Studies, Development or Law.

### Experience

**Essential**

- At least 4 years of experience in social cohesion, peace building, community governance or conflict-sensitive programming.
- Proven experience facilitating community dialogues and mediating disputes, preferably over land, water or shared resources.
- Experience setting up or strengthening community structures such as committees, cooperatives, WUAs or peace committees, including elections and constitutions.
- Experience working with traditional institutions and State and LGAs in North-East Nigeria.
- Experience with NGOs, UN agencies or government programmes in humanitarian or recovery settings.

**Desirable**

- Experience negotiating land-use, asset handover or community ownership agreements.
- Knowledge of customary and statutory land tenure in Borno State, including the Land Use Act.
- Experience with livelihoods, WASH or infrastructure projects where communities share assets.
- Experience with Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) and feedback mechanisms.

### Skills and competencies

- Excellent facilitation, negotiation and mediation skills.
- Able to stay neutral, build trust and handle sensitive information with discretion.
- Strong analysis of power and conflict dynamics, and sound judgement on risk.
- Clear writing of agreements, meeting records and reports.
- Cultural sensitivity and respect for local customs, with a commitment to inclusion of women, youth, persons with disabilities, IDPs and returnees.
- Commitment to PSEA, safeguarding and humanitarian principles.
- Proficient in MS Office or Google Workspace.

### Languages

- **Essential:** fluent English and Hausa.
- **Strongly desirable:** fluent Kanuri.

jobs.title: Protection Case Management & Cash Assistance Consultancy
jobs.description:
**TERMS OF REFERENCE**

**Consultancy for the development of a protection case management and cash for protection framework for the Protect Aid Workers mechanism**

**Background**

Humanitarian workers face increasing risks in the course of their work. In response to these challenges, a consortium of NGOs, including [Legal Action Worldwide](https://legalactionworldwide.org/) (LAW), [Global Interagency Security Forum](https://gisf.ngo/) (GISF) and [Protect Humanitarians](https://protecthumanitarians.org/) (PH), established the **Protect Aid Workers** (PAW) mechanism with the support of DG ECHO.

The mechanism assists humanitarian workers who have experienced a critical incident, face an immediate threat to their safety or well-being, or have been arrested, detained or are facing legal proceedings linked to their humanitarian work. Support aims to reduce protection risks, prevent further harm, facilitate recovery and improve the well-being of affected individuals and their families. Since its launch, the mechanism has supported approximately 750 humanitarian workers and their dependants across 20 countries.

PAW is structured around three complementary pillars:

- Pillar 1: Provision of direct assistance to humanitarian workers through financial and legal assistance
- Pillar 2: Development and dissemination of good practices, peer-learning opportunities, technical resources and collaborative initiatives aimed at strengthening aid worker protection and duty of care systems across the humanitarian sector.
- Pillar 3: Engagement with decision-makers to raise awareness of risks faced by aid workers and promote stronger protection policies and practices.

The ambition of PAW is to establish a comprehensive and survivor-centred support model. The mechanism combines case management, financial assistance and access to specialised services tailored to the needs of affected individuals.

Requests for support may be submitted through organisations or directly by aid workers. Applications are reviewed by a case management team responsible for verification, needs assessment, eligibility review and support planning.

A central component of the mechanism is the provision of protection grants. These grants may be provided directly to affected individuals and their families or channelled through organisations delivering support on their behalf. Assistance may cover a wide range of protection-related needs, including relocation, safe accommodation, legal representation, medical care, psychosocial support, temporary income replacement and other measures aimed at reducing protection risks and supporting recovery. Over time, the mechanism has also increasingly relied on unrestricted cash assistance where appropriate, enabling affected aid workers to prioritise and address their own protection and recovery needs in a flexible and dignified manner.

Alongside financial assistance, the mechanism provides access to specialised legal support and is progressively strengthening referral pathways for mental health, healthcare and other protection-related services. While these components have expanded significantly over recent years, they remain at different stages of development and would benefit from further structuring and integration within an overarching case management framework.

1. **Purpose of the consultancy**

Over the past two years, PAW has experienced significant growth in terms of geographical coverage, number of cases supported and diversity of assistance provided. While this expansion has demonstrated the relevance and effectiveness of the mechanism, it has also highlighted the need to further consolidate and formalise its direct support model.

The mechanism has progressively developed a range of practices, tools and decision-making processes relating to case management, protection grants, cash assistance and specialised referrals. In particular, the use of cash assistance has expanded over time, including through the growing use of unconditional cash transfers where appropriate, allowing humanitarian workers to address urgent protection and recovery needs in a flexible and dignified manner.

While this evolution has enabled PAW to provide tailored support across a wide range of contexts and protection risks, several components of the model have developed incrementally in response to operational realities. As a result, approaches to case management, grant allocation, cash assistance modalities, referral pathways and documentation requirements are not yet fully standardised.

**Objectives of the consultancy**

The overall objective of this consultancy is to review and strengthen the Protect Aid Workers direct support model by developing a coherent operational framework integrating protection case management, cash assistance and referral mechanisms.

The consultancy should build on existing PAW practices and tools, identify areas for improvement, and provide practical recommendations, procedures and tools that enhance consistency, accountability, quality and decision-making while preserving the flexibility required to respond to diverse protection contexts and individual needs.

**Scope of work**

The consultant will:

- Review existing PAW guidance, tools, templates, databases and operational procedures related to case management, protection grants, cash assistance and referrals.
- Review a sample of case files, grant decisions and support modalities implemented through the mechanism.
- Consult with relevant consortium members and stakeholders involved in the management and delivery of direct assistance.
- Assess the extent to which current practices align with recognised good practices and international standards in protection case management
- Review the applicability of the DG ECHO Cash and Voucher Assistance policy framework to the PAW mechanism and ensure that proposed approaches to protection grants and unrestricted cash assistance are consistent with relevant donor requirements and good practices.
- Identify gaps, strengths, risks and opportunities for improvement.
- Develop recommendations and operational tools to strengthen the overall direct support model.
- Develop and/or revise standard operating procedures, templates, workflows and decision-making tools required to support implementation.

The consultancy’s primary objective is to review and adapt existing tools, and to develop any necessary new ones, to improve efficiency and standardise decision-making mechanisms while ensuring full alignment with international and donors standards.

**Deliverables**

Deliverable 1: Diagnostic and inception report

The consultant will conduct a review of the current PAW direct support model and produce an inception report presenting:

- An analysis of the existing case management, protection grant, cash assistance and referral systems.
- An assessment of strengths, gaps, risks and opportunities for improvement.
- A review of alignment with relevant protection standards, cash assistance good practices, and DG ECHO requirements.
- Recommendations for strengthening the overall direct support model.
- A proposed structure for the future operational framework, including the documents, procedures, tools and resources to be developed during the consultancy.

Deliverable 2: Operational framework package

Based on the agreed recommendations, the consultant will develop a draft operational framework package for review by the consortium. The package may include, as relevant:

- Standard operating procedures.
- Case management workflows.
- Decision-making frameworks.
- Eligibility and assessment tools.
- Referral mechanisms and related templates.
- Cash assistance and protection grant guidance.
- Documentation and accountability tools.
- Any additional operational resources identified as necessary during the diagnostic phase.

**Planning & coordination**

The Consultant will be under the overall guidance of a steering committee. The consultancy will be conducted through the following steps:

- Review of PAW documentation combined with consultations with relevant consortium members and stakeholders.
- Submission and presentation of the Inception Report (Deliverable 1).
- Review and validation of findings and recommendations by the steering committee.
- Development of a draft Operational Framework Package (Deliverable 2).
- Review and consolidation of comments from the steering committee.
- Submission of the revised and final Operational framework package.
- Facilitation of a final workshop to present the final framework, key recommendations and implementation considerations.

**Consultant's profile (individual or team)**

- Advanced university education (bac + 5) in one of the following fields: social services, sociology, political science, law, gender and other similar training
- Significant (+5 years) experience in humanitarian protection programmes
- Strong expertise in case management
- Significant experience in cash assistance, including cash for protection
- Demonstrate experience in developing guidelines, standard operating procedures and tools
- Understanding of different humanitarian contexts and stakeholders
- Knowledge of gender, diversity, inclusion and protection issues
- Fluency in English, French is a plus
- Excellent analytical and writing skills

**Timeline**

The assignment is expected to take 2-3 months from the time of signing of the contract, with possible extension based on identified additional needs and potential longer term advisory services as necessary and if required. We are seeking a consultant who is available to start to work shortly after the deadline for submission of tenders.

jobs.title: Venezuela - Asesor de Seguridad (national)
Terms of Reference for Documentation Support of selected Partner Organisations’(Pos) stories of change under the ADA Framework Programme 2023-2026.
jobs.description:
**1. Background**

horizont3000 is an Austrian non-governmental organisation working in sustainable development cooperation. Based in Vienna, with offices in the four focus areas East Africa, Central America, Senegal and Mozambique, we are backed by eleven Austrian Catholic grassroots organisations.

We support partner organisations (POs) and locally led initiatives through co-financing based on grant schemes, medium to long-term advisory services and knowledge management to facilitate learning and sharing processes. Our projects and programmes are embedded in two main sectors, Human Rights & Civil Society and Sustainable Livelihoods, with a focus on Gender Equality, Climate Action and Policy Dialogue.

We work with communities who have been marginalized in claiming their rights and leading self-determined lives, foremost with smallholder farmers, disadvantaged women, children and youth, women’s and human rights groups as well as indigenous people.

The know-how3000 (kh3000) programme intervention is implemented by horizont3000 and its regional and country offices. It is part of the Austrian Development (ADA) framework programme 2023-2026 “Gender Equality 4 Sustainable Development.”

The ongoing horizont3000 ADA framework programme 2023-2026 is committed to proactively pursuing the goal of gender equality. Therefore, it is key to document experiences to capture, and communicate the project's most significant results, lessons, and impact, but also demonstrate the project's contribution to gender equality, women's empowerment, and positive social change in communities.

horizont3000 therefore seeks a qualified consultant to effectively capture the stories and produce high-quality film for proper documentation and meaningful Knowledge sharing.

**2. Objective of the Consultancy**

The objective of this consultancy is to capture the project's most significant results, lessons, and impact while demonstrate the project's contribution to gender equality, women's empowerment, and positive social change in communities through;

1. Capturing four high-quality video clips of stories of change that demonstrate the outcomes and impact of the project-on-project participants and communities with a focus on stories of women’s empowerment, strengthening gender equality or engaging men and boys.
2. Producing a mini documentary/ video clip reflecting experiences from 5 project gender focal points and 2 horizont3000 staff
3. Capturing professional photographs of key moments and project participants.
4. Developing a mini booklet featuring selected stories of change, lessons learned, and best practices to inform future projects.

**3. Scope of Work**

Under the supervision of the horizont3000 East Africa Gender Focal Point, the incumbent will be responsible for the following tasks:

- Participate in inception meeting with horizont3000 to agree on objectives, methodology, timelines, guidelines that should be used, and deliverables.
- Review relevant project documents to understand the scope and achievements of the know-how3000 (kh3000) programme.
- Develop a detailed work plan for the assignment, including timelines for interviews, field visits, and content development.
- Visit selected Partner Organisations (POs) to capture high-quality photos and video footage of h3 selected stories of change.
- Document experiences shared by gender focal points as well as h3 project staff to reflect impact and lessons learnt.
- Review and refine 4 stories of change with accompanying photos and graphics.
- Produce 4 video clips (3–5 minutes each) of stories of change
- Produce 1 mini documentary/video clip (5-15 minutes) reflecting experiences from 5 project gender focal points and 2 horizont3000 staff in line with the stories of change.
- Draft a mini booklet featuring selected stories of change, lessons learned, and best practices to inform future projects.
- Work closely with horizont3000 Gender team to incorporate feedback and finalize all deliverables.
- Submit final deliverables, including comprehensive report of the assignment, all raw footage, photos, and reports, in high-quality formats.

**4. Duty Stations**

The assignment will be conducted primarily in Uganda, Tanzania and Kenya as follows;

1. **Uganda:** horizont3000- Kampala,AFIRD- Mpigi District and Caritas MADDO- Masaka District
2. **Tanzania:** OWSL- Mwanza
3. **Kenya:** PACIDA- Marsabit

**5. Expected deliverables**

Expected outputs under this consultancy are as follows:

- Inception report including a detailed work plan for the assignment, including timelines for interviews, field visits, and content development.
- 4 video clips (3–5 minutes each) of stories of change
- 1 mini documentary/video clip (5 -15 minutes) reflecting experiences from 5 project gender focal points and 2 horizont3000 staff.
- 10 simple digital flyers/ infographics to illustrate stories of change and impact
- A maximum of 100 edited high-resolution pictures from the 3 duty stations.
- Final designed mini booklet reviewed by horizont3000 (digital version).
- All raw and edited content (photos, videos, and reports) submitted in digital formats.

**6. Duration and Timeline**

The consultancy will be conducted as follows;

- November 13th 2026: An inception meeting to discuss the assignment details, work plan development, and review of project documents.
- November 23rd - 5th December 2026: Interviews and field visits.
- December 7th -11th, 2026: Development of video clips, mini documentary, digital flyers, infographics and booklet
- December 14th 2026: Review, revisions, and submission of final deliverables.

**7. Budget**

The consultant should propose a budget that covers their fees (based on daily rate), communication costs, taxes, and any other relevant expenses. The budget should be submitted along with the technical proposal. The total budget for the scope of work outlined under 3.) should not exceed 20,000,000 Uganda Shillings including taxes.

**Note:** horizont3000 will cover in country travel costs during the course of the assignment.

**8. Required Qualifications**

The consultant should meet the following qualifications:

- Expertise in documentation, storytelling and communication strategies for NGOs.
- Proficiency in photography and videography, including editing and production of professional-quality documentaries. If the consultant is working with a team, the one of the team members should be an expert photographer.
- Strong writing skills with the ability to produce clear, engaging, and visually appealing reports.
- Strong communication skills and the ability to simplify complex concepts for non-technical audiences.
- Excellent command of English, working proficiency in spoken Kiswahili.
- Previous experience working with NGOs in East Africa or similar organizations is an added advantage.

9\. Applications will be evaluated based on the following criteria:

- Technical proposal (40%)
- Financial proposal (20%)
- Qualifications and experience (20%)
