jobs.title: Senior Advisor for GBV in Emergencies
jobs.description:
NCA works with partners and international networks to provide emergency assistance, support long-term development and advocate for a just world. As a senior thematic advisor, you will combine an organisation-wide perspective with sustained, practical support to assigned country offices. Working alongside country advisors, thematic colleagues and humanitarian coordinators, you will help shape programme approaches, assure technical quality and connect country-level experience with global learning, policy and advocacy. The role involves travel to country offices and humanitarian responses.

As Senior Advisor for GBV in Emergencies, you will help strengthen high-quality, evidence-based gender-based violence (GBV) prevention and response programming across NCA’s humanitarian work. Working closely with country offices, partners and global networks, you will provide technical leadership and help turn international standards and evidence into effective, context-sensitive programming. You will strengthen technical capacities, support learning across contexts and contribute to the continued development of NCA’s GBV work.

**How you work**

You bring strong technical expertise together with sound judgement and a practical, collaborative approach. You listen carefully, build trust and make complex standards relevant and useful in different contexts. You are comfortable providing technical direction while creating space for country teams to take ownership, and you enjoy supporting colleagues and partners to strengthen their capacities. Working across cultures, teams and departments comes naturally to you, and you contribute to an environment where people share experiences and learn from one another. You bring flexibility, reflection and composure, including when working in demanding situations.

**Your responsibilities**

- Strengthen programme quality through survivor-centred, evidence-based approaches aligned with the IASC GBV Guidelines and the Minimum Standards for GBV in Emergencies, adapting tools and guidance to country contexts, with a particular focus on case management.
- Promote the integration of GBV prevention and response into broader humanitarian programming, collaborating with other thematic advisors and humanitarian colleagues.
- Provide thought leadership in your areas of expertise and contribute to the content and execution of NCA’s Humanitarian Strategic Plan.
- Promote programme innovation and cross-country learning, maintain an overview of portfolio developments and thematic trends, and document good practices and lessons learned.
- Provide technical advice and regular follow-up for GBV programmes in assigned country offices, advising on strategy, programme design, implementation and results-based management.
- Provide technical input and quality assurance for monitoring, evaluation and reporting, working with country offices and relevant colleagues to strengthen evidence-based programming.
- Build the technical capacity of country office staff and partners through participatory training, mentoring, coaching and practical guidance.
- Support funding proposals and resource mobilisation in collaboration with country offices and the Donors & Partnership team, ensuring technical quality and adherence to donor and organisational requirements.
- Represent NCA in relevant technical working groups, coordination platforms and networks; advise colleagues and senior management on GBV.
- Contribute technical expertise to policy, advocacy and internal and external communication.

**Your qualifications**

- An advanced degree in social work, social sciences, gender studies, humanitarian affairs, international development or a related field. Substantial relevant field experience may compensate for formal education.
- At least five years of specialised experience in GBV prevention and response programming in conflict, post-conflict or humanitarian settings, including at least three years of international experience.
- Strong technical knowledge of international standards for GBV in Emergencies and practical experience applying survivor-centred approaches.
- Demonstrated experience providing technical leadership, advice and quality assurance across the programme cycle, including programme design, results-based management, monitoring and reporting.
- Solid experience in training, mentoring and capacity development, particularly through participatory approaches.
- Experience developing funding proposals or providing quality assurance for their technical components.
- A good understanding of humanitarian coordination mechanisms and experience collaborating with country teams and partner organisations.
- Fluency in written and spoken English. French and/or Arabic are an advantage.
- Ability and willingness to travel to country offices and humanitarian responses, including high-risk contexts and, when required, at short notice

**What we offer**

- A meaningful role with the opportunity to strengthen humanitarian GBV programming across multiple country contexts.
- Collaboration with engaged colleagues and partners in an international, multicultural and interdisciplinary environment.
- Opportunities to contribute to programme innovation, technical development and shared learning.

**Ethical Commitments**

Norwegian Church Aid is committed to high standards of ethics and accountability in all that we do. As an employee, you will be required to sign the following documents when entering into an employment contract:

- **ACT Alliance Code of Conduct**
- **Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, Harassment, and Child Safeguarding Policy**

These are binding documents for all employees. We therefore ask you to familiarise yourself with them before applying. You can find the documents on our website: [https://www.kirkensnodhjelp.no/etterettelighet](https://www.kirkensnodhjelp.no/etterettelighet)

**Accountability**

Norwegian Church Aid places great importance on being accountable in all that we do. The people we meet through our work, those who support our work, and other stakeholders should know that they can trust us.

jobs.title: Aquaculture & Feed Production Officer
jobs.description:
**JOB PURPOSE:**
Under the supervision of the Livelihood Project Manager, the Aquaculture and Feed Production Officer is the technical lead for the fish farms in MMC, Jere and Mafa and for the Mafa Fish Feed Production Centre. The goal is that all four run as productive, profitable community enterprises, with affordable local feed, good fish husbandry and value addition.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**1. Assessment and planning:**

• Carry out a technical assessment of each fish farm: pond condition and capacity, water source and quality, stocking history, mortality, growth rates, feeding practices and records.

• Lead the fish farm profitability diagnostic with the Business Development Officer. Analyze stocking density, feed conversion ratio (FCR), survival, harvest weights, selling prices and cost per kilogram.

• With the Agricultural and Infrastructure Engineers, define the technical requirements for pond rehabilitation at MMC and Jere and for the replacement feed mill line.

• Prepare a production plan for each farm: species (mainly catfish), stocking density, staggered stocking and harvesting calendar, and expected output.

**2. Fish farm rehabilitation and restocking:**

• Advise the engineers on pond layout, depth, inlets and outlets, and water management needs during rehabilitation.

• Oversee pond preparation before stocking: liming, fertilizing where appropriate, filling and water quality checks.

• Source certified, healthy fingerlings or juveniles from reputable hatcheries. Supervise transport, acclimatization and stocking.

• Set up a staggered stocking cycle so ponds are harvested in rotation and income is regular.

**3. Production management and fish health:**

• Train and coach pond teams in feeding schedules, water quality monitoring (temperature, dissolved oxygen, pH, ammonia), grading, predator control and pond hygiene.

• Set up disease prevention and biosecurity: quarantine of new stock, safe handling and the right response to mortality. Link to veterinary and fisheries extension services.

• Monitor growth through regular sampling and adjust feeding to improve the FCR and reduce waste.

• Make sure every farm keeps pond-by-pond records of stocking, feeding, sampling, mortality, harvest and sales.

**4. Fish Feed Production Centre:**

• Work with the Agricultural Engineer on specifying, installing and commissioning the replacement feed line (hammer mill, mixer, pelletizer or extruder, dryer, bagging).

• Develop feed formulas for each growth stage (starter, grower, finisher) using local ingredients such as maize, soybean, groundnut cake, fishmeal, premix and binders. Balance protein, energy and cost.

• Set up quality control: ingredient checks (moisture, mould, aflatoxin risk), batch records, pellet size, stability and floating or sinking behavior, and safe storage.

• Train 5–8 operators, mainly youth, in machine operation, formulation, hygiene, safety, stock control and record keeping.

• Plan ingredient procurement with the Business Development Officer, including bulk buying at harvest when prices are lowest, and plan feed supply to the three project farms and other buyers.

• Run the centre as a practical training hub for youth groups and other fish farmers in feed formulation and processing.

**5. Processing, value addition and marketing:**

• Train members in fish processing: smoking and drying with improved kilns, hygiene, packaging and storage. The aim is to reduce post-harvest losses and add value.

• Help set up fee-based smoking services for non-member producers where feasible.

• With the Market Linkages and Digital Solutions Officer, link farms to buyers in Maiduguri markets, restaurants, institutions and traders. Plan harvests to match demand and use price information to time sales.

• Provide production data to the Business Development Officer for pricing, business plans and cost recovery.

**6. Sustainability, monitoring and reporting:**

• Develop simple SOPs for pond management, feed production and fish processing, in English and Hausa.

• With the Asset Management Officer, make sure aquaculture equipment and inputs are recorded and maintained.

• Link each farm and the feed centre to the fisheries department and ADP extension officers who will support them after handover.

• Submit monthly technical reports with production, FCR, survival, feed output, sales and challenges. Provide MEAL data and contribute to the handover readiness assessment.

**Cross-cutting duties:**

• Promote environmentally sound practices: responsible water use and discharge, and safe handling of chemicals and feed ingredients.

• Make sure women and youth have fair access to roles in production, feed processing and fish processing.

**Education & Professional Requirements:**

**Education:**

• **Essential:** a university degree (B.Sc. or HND) in Fisheries and Aquaculture, Animal Science (with a fisheries or nutrition option), or a related field.

**• Desirable:** An M.Sc. in Agriculture.

**Professional experience Essential:**

• At least 4 years of practical experience in fish farming, preferably catfish in earthen or lined ponds, including production planning, fish health and record keeping.

• Hands-on experience in fish feed formulation and production using local ingredients, including running or supervising a small feed mill.

• Experience training farmers or community groups in fish production.

• Experience with NGOs, UN agencies or government agricultural programmes in North-East Nigeria or a similar setting.

**Desirable:**

• Experience with feed extruders or pelletizers, and with feed quality control.

• Experience with fish processing (smoking and drying) and market linkages.

• Experience supporting cooperatives or community-run aquaculture enterprises to become profitable.

• Knowledge of the fish value chain and markets in Borno State.

**Personal requirements**

• Strong technical knowledge of fish nutrition, water quality, biosecurity and fish health.

• Able to analyze production data such as FCR, survival and cost per kg, and turn it into practical advice.

• Excellent practical training and coaching skills, suited to adults with low literacy.

• Problem-solver who is comfortable working hands-on at pond side and in the mill.

• Integrity in input, procurement and quality checks.

• Commitment to inclusion, PSEA and humanitarian principles.

• Proficient in MS Office or Google Workspace, especially spreadsheets.

**Languages**

• **Essential:** fluent English; good spoken Hausa.

• **Desirable:** Kanuri.

jobs.title: Agricultural Engineer
jobs.description:
**JOB PURPOSE:**
Under the supervision of the Livelihood Project Manager, the Livelihood Agricultural Engineer is the project's technical lead for all engineering works. They design, supervise and commission the irrigation, aquaculture, feed mill and greenhouse infrastructure in MMC, Jere and Mafa LGAs, and train the community operators who will run and maintain it.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**1. Technical assessments:**

• Carry out condition assessments of all agricultural facilities: irrigation systems, ponds and water supply, the feed mill and its power supply, and the greenhouse.

• Run a hydraulic assessment at the MMC and Jere irrigation farms: water source yield, command area, crop water demand, head and flow, drainage and return flow, and sump location.

• Assess whether any existing feed mill parts can be reused, and whether the building and power supply can carry the replacement line.

• Identify risks to the sites, including flooding, theft and power supply, and propose engineering measures to reduce them.

• Produce an assessment report for each facility, with bills of quantities (BoQs) and cost estimates, for approval by the Project Manager and the LGA Oversight Committee.

**2. Design and specification:**

• Size and design the recirculation pumping systems: pump, solar array and inverter, sump or collection tank, intake screens, filters, valves, pipework and pump house.

• Prepare drawings and specifications for pond rehabilitation (desilting, liners or embankments, inlets and outlets, overflow) and the related water supply works.

• Write the technical specification for the replacement feed production line: hammer mill, mixer, pelletiser or extruder, dryer, sieving and bagging, and power supply.

• Specify greenhouse repairs and any minor civil works (pump houses, ingredient stores, fencing).

• Get technical sign-off from the Ministry of Water Resources (pumps) and the relevant fisheries and agriculture departments.

**3. Procurement support:**

• Prepare technical specifications, BoQs and evaluation criteria for tenders. Value warranty, local after-sales service and spare parts availability as well as price.

• Sit on technical evaluation panels and advise on contractor and supplier selection.

• Inspect goods on delivery against specifications before acceptance.

**4. Construction and installation supervision:**

• Supervise contractors and installers on site daily. Check workmanship, materials, measurements and compliance with drawings.

• Keep site diaries, issue instructions and record any variations, and certify work for payment.

• Enforce health, safety and environmental standards on site, including safe electrical installation and safe working around water and machinery.

• Escalate delays, defects or cost overruns to the Project Manager immediately.

**5. Testing, commissioning and handover of works:**

• Lead testing and commissioning: trial irrigation cycles, pump performance (flow and head), pond water-holding tests, and feed mill test runs with pellet quality checks.

• Commission jointly with the government technical counterpart, the facility committee and the supplier, and record results in commissioning certificates.

• Collect as-built drawings, operation manuals, warranties and starter spare parts for every installation.

**6. Operator training and maintenance systems:**

• Train irrigation operators (5–7 per scheme), pond teams and feed mill operators in operation, troubleshooting, preventive maintenance and safety.

• Develop simple SOPs and preventive maintenance schedules for each asset, in English and Hausa with pictures where useful.

• With the Asset Management and Logistics Officer, enter every engineered asset into the asset register: specifications, serial numbers, warranty, expected useful life and condition rating.

• Build a list of local technicians and spare parts suppliers for each asset type.

• Advise the facility committees and the Enterprise Development Officer on maintenance and replacement costs, so the asset renewal reserves are set at the right level.

**7. Monitoring, reporting and documentation:**

• Submit weekly site progress reports with photos and monthly engineering reports.

• Track the indicators the MEAL Officer needs on infrastructure functionality: pump hours, breakdowns, repair times and asset condition.

• Take part in quarterly joint monitoring visits and the annual asset verification. Prepare the engineering part of handover inventories.

**Cross-cutting duties:**

• Use designs that are climate-smart and low-cost to run, such as solar pumping and efficient water use, and suitable for community management.

• Apply do-no-harm and conflict sensitivity: consult landowners and communities before any works that affect site boundaries or access.

• Follow PSEA, safeguarding and security procedures. Make sure contractors and their workers sign and respect the Code of Conduct.

*Carry out any other reasonable duties related to the project, as assigned by the Project Manager*.

**Education & Professional Requirements:**

**Education:**

• **Essential:** a B.Eng. or B.Sc. in Agricultural Engineering, Agricultural and Bio-resources Engineering,

**• Desirable:** An M. Eng or M.Sc. in irrigation, water resources or agricultural mechanization. Membership of the Nigerian Society of Engineers (NSE) or the Nigerian Institution of Agricultural Engineers. Training in solar pumping systems.

**Professional experience Essential:**

• At least 4 years of hands-on experience in agricultural engineering.

• Experience designing and supervising small-scale rural infrastructure works preparing BoQs, supervising contractors, certifying work and commissioning.

• Experience training community operators in operation and maintenance.

• Experience with NGOs, UN agencies or government agricultural programmes in North-East Nigeria or a similar setting.

**Desirable:**

• Experience with aquaculture infrastructure and with agro-processing equipment such as fish feed mills, pelletizers or extruders.

• Experience with solar-powered irrigation and greenhouse systems.

• Experience with handing assets over to communities, and with asset registers or maintenance management systems.

**Personal requirements**

• Strong technical design skills, including hydraulic calculations and solar pump sizing. Able to use AutoCAD or similar drawing software.

• Able to write clear technical specifications, BoQs and site reports.

• Practical problem-solving on site, with high standards for quality and safety.

• Able to explain technical concepts simply to community members and operators with low literacy.

• Integrity in procurement and contractor management.

• Commitment to safeguarding, PSEA, gender inclusion and humanitarian principles.

• Proficient in MS Office or Google Workspace.

**Languages**

• **Essential:** fluent English; good spoken Hausa.

jobs.title: Finance Manager, South Korea
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**BACKGROUND**

Over the past 90 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in some 40 countries, providing emergency relief and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 28 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC also helps refugees resettle in the US and become self-sufficient.

The IRC global network has its headquarters in New York and London. IRC Europe is part of this network with offices in the UK, Germany, Sweden, Belgium and Switzerland. In addition, the IRC has a partnership with Stichting Vluchteling in the Netherlands.

The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

Read more about the IRC here: [https://www.rescue.or.kr](https://www.rescue.or.kr/)

**EXTERNAL RELATIONS AND THE PRIVATE FUNDRAISING FUNCTION**

The External Relations (ER) department is comprised of four complementary functions, including Private fundraising, in which this role falls under. To enable IRC to deliver its organizational commitments, the ER department has established a bold new approach that will enhance its ability to raise diverse and flexible funding aligned with IRC’s top priorities, while raising our profile and influence. The ER team is an international team, with colleagues in more than 10 offices globally.

Within Private Fundraising sits the Mass Markets unit. This unit is currently made up of seven teams – US, UK, Germany, Sweden, Korea, Digital & Remote Markets and our Supporter Journey and Acquisition teams. Mass Market’s primary goal is to increase the number of sustainers we have globally, via targeted and cost effective acquisition and by building meaningful connections with our donors to ensure we can retain them. By increasing our sustainer numbers and capitalizing on cash giving moments we aim to grow unrestricted revenue for IRC and the people we serve.

**STRUCTURE AND PURPOSE OF THE ROLE**

In the role of Finance Manager, you will be the strategic finance leader for IRC Korea, responsible for driving financial results, transparency, and system modernization – most immediately through leading the rollout and localization of Integra, IRC’s global finance system, for the Korea office. You will manage and mentor the Finance team and serve as the primary liaison for other functional areas supporting the Korea office, contributing to strategic direction and operational problem-solving through your area of professional expertise.

**KEY AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Working within a Finance matrix structure, you will be responsible for and oversee:

**1. Controllership:**

- Ensure compliance of donor funds in Korea with local and relevant international regulations, including tax, accounting standards, and reporting requirements.
- Manage the financial records of IRC Korea and responsible for timely monthly/annual closing, financial reporting.
- Managing Audit and financial compliance, acting as a key point of contact with external parties including auditors and tax authorities.
- Lead the deployment of IRC’s global ERP system “Integra” for IRC Korea, ensuring both IRC and local statutory requirements are met.
- Act as primary focal point for the Integra Delivery team during the deployment period.
- Preparation of annual statutory financial statements and other local financial regulatory reporting as required, in coordination with HQ Global Finance and external parties where required.
- Provide monthly payroll information to the outsourcing firm and review calculations before finalizing.
- Maintain an appropriate financial control environment, ensuring financial records are maintained and that weekly and monthly financial routines are completed.
- Ensure accurate data between Integra and fundraising system (Donus), maintaining monthly financial reconciliations.
- Ensure regular communications with the IRC Global Finance Accounting & Consolidation team, particularly during month end/year end.
- Ensure internal IRC financial reporting is carried out to time and quality.
- Prepare reports for the Executive Director on an agreed basis

**2. Treasury & Risk Management:**

- Identify and manage financial risks, including currency exchange. Provide insights into the financial health of IRC Korea.
- Working with the treasury team, identify and recommend appropriate banking service providers and lead setting up banking relationships, if needed.

**3. Financial Planning & Analysis**:

- Lead the annual budget and planning process for IRC Korea in cooperation with the Executive Director, including reporting and follow-up.
- Work in conjunction with the Executive Director and Global FP&A team to finalize annual budgets.
- Ensure appropriate financial planning, budgeting and monitoring for IRC Korea and in line with IRC requirements.

**4. Functional Leadership**:

- Manage, train and mentor the Finance team members in using Integra and as the finance function grows.
- Foster a high-performance culture of learning and best practice to ensure the finance function’s goals are met.

**OTHER RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- To comply with the culture and policies governing IRC Korea.
- To represent IRC in a manner that ensures appropriate communication with our supporters and stakeholders.
- To develop and maintain a positive working relationship with other departments and teams in IRC Korea and IRC globally.
- To attend meetings, conferences, and training courses as directed.
- Abide by organizational policies and practices, and the Code of Conduct.
- Support diversity and equality of opportunity in the workplace

**WORKING RELATIONSHIPS:**

- You will report to the Executive Director of South Korea, in partnership with the Director of Finance, Europe.
- Regular liaison with the Global Finance Accounting & Consolidation team and Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) team in HQ.
- External Relations colleagues as needed.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

**Qualifications:**

**Essentials:**

- Multi-year background from qualified financial work (Min. 10 years of experience in Fiance with more than 3 years of managerial roles)
- Academic education (degree) business administration and accounting
- Strongly preferred experience with finance/ERP systems (e.g., Microsoft D365 Finance & Operations, or similar)
- Fluent Knowledge of English and Korean

**Preferrable:**

- Experience in Operations management

**Skills/character:**

- Ability to be strategic and creative in developing and implementing new income-generating activities.
- Strong relationship-building, interpersonal and negotiation skills.
- Excellent people management skills, including the demonstrated capacity to lead, motivate, develop and engage a multi-disciplinary team with a collaborative and supportive management style.
- Ability to lead effectively through a period of significant systems and process transition.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Business Development Officer (Enterprise Development)
jobs.description:
**JOB PURPOSE:**
Under the supervision of the Livelihood Project Manager, the Business Development Officer (Enterprise Development) makes sure the ten facilities in MMC, Jere and Mafa LGAs run as viable businesses. They set up the business plans, prices, bookkeeping, cost recovery and access to finance that let each enterprise pay its own way after handover.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**1. Enterprise assessment and feasibility:**

• Assess the current business position of each facility: what it produces or sells, costs, prices, income, records and capacity.

• With the Aquaculture and Feed Production Officer, lead the financial side of the fish farm profitability diagnostic: cost per kilogram, break-even price and the main sources of loss.

• Contribute to market and feasibility studies for each enterprise model, working with the Market Linkages Officer.

**2. Business plans and financial models:**

• Develop a simple, realistic business plan for each of the ten enterprises with its members. Each plan covers products and services, production targets, pricing, costs, cash flow, breakeven and staffing.

• Build costing and pricing tools for each model: piece rates for tailoring, fish and feed prices, the irrigation service fee per plot or season, and seedling prices.

• Set the internal transfer price for feed sold from the Fish Feed Production Centre to the project fish farms. It must be fair to both sides.

• Present the business plans to the members' General Assembly and the LGA Oversight Committee for approval.

**3. Cost recovery, revenue sharing and reserves:**

• Design each enterprise's revenue-sharing plan in line with its Tripartite Facility Management Agreement. The plan covers operating costs, the asset renewal reserve, member earnings, the landowner and community development share, and administration.

• Work with the Agricultural Engineer and the Asset Management Officer to calculate the maintenance and replacement costs that set the size of each asset renewal reserve.

• Help each enterprise open and fund a separate reserve account.

• Help plan the tapering of transitional stipends, so enterprise income takes over operator pay as planned.

**4. Financial management systems and coaching:**

• Set up simple bookkeeping for each enterprise: cash book, sales and receipts, stock and input registers, order book (tailoring), fee register (irrigation), and a monthly profit statement.

• Coach treasurers and records keepers monthly until they produce accurate accounts on their own.

• Make sure monthly financial statements are posted at each facility and presented to members.

• Support the quarterly social audits and prepare committees for review by the LGA Oversight Committee.

• With the Market Linkages and Digital Solutions Officer, introduce digital record-keeping and sales tools where they fit.

**5. Cooperative registration and legal set-up:**

• Support each operating group to register with the State Department of Cooperatives, or as a community-based organization where more suitable.

• Help open bank accounts with dual signatories (at least one a woman) and set spending limits and cash-handling rules.

• Support the Governance and Social Cohesion Officer to make sure the financial rules in the constitutions match the business plans.

**6. Entrepreneurship training:**

• Design and deliver training for at least 300 participants (minimum 50% women and 30% youth). Topics: entrepreneurship, business planning, financial literacy, record keeping, costing and pricing, and cooperative business management.

• Deliver refresher sessions and on-the-job coaching tailored to each enterprise type.

**7. Access to finance:**

• Link at least 200 participants to Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs), microfinance institutions or other financial services.

• Help at least 100 participants access working capital through savings, loans or other financial support. Prepare enterprises to present a credible case to lenders.

• Advise on the start-up stock and input support from the project, and how it is repaid into each cooperative's revolving fund. 8. Monitoring and reporting

• Track each enterprise's monthly revenue, costs, profit, reserve balance and cost-recovery status. Share the data with the MEAL Officer.

• Flag enterprises that are falling behind their business plans and propose corrective actions.

• Contribute the enterprise viability part of the handover readiness assessment and of the reports to WFP.

**Cross-cutting duties:**

• Design pricing, fees and benefit-sharing so they are fair and affordable, and do not exclude vulnerable households, women, youth or persons with disabilities.

• Guard against elite capture and misuse of enterprise funds. Report any suspected fraud immediately.

• Follow PSEA, safeguarding and security procedures.

*Carry out any other reasonable duties related to the project, as assigned by the Project Manager.*

**Education & Professional Requirements:**

**Education:**

• **Essential:** a university degree (B.Sc. or HND) in Business Administration, Accounting, Economics, Agricultural Economics/Agribusiness, Cooperative Studies or a related field.

**• Desirable:** A Master’s degree or MBA.

**Professional experience Essential:**

• At least 4 years of experience in enterprise development, agribusiness, cooperative development or livelihoods programmes.

• Proven experience developing business plans, costing and pricing models and cash-flow projections for small or community-based enterprises.

• Experience setting up bookkeeping systems and coaching low-literacy groups to keep records and manage funds.

• Experience training adults in entrepreneurship and financial literacy.

• Experience working with NGOs, UN agencies or government programmes in North-East Nigeria.

**Desirable:**

• Experience in agricultural value chains such as aquaculture, feed, irrigated horticulture or tailoring.

• Experience with VSLAs, microfinance or linking groups to banks.

• Experience with cost-recovery models for shared community assets, such as water user fees.

• Familiarity with WFP livelihoods and resilience programming.

**Personal requirements:**

• Strong numeracy and financial analysis. Advanced Excel or Google Sheets for financial models.

• Able to turn business concepts into simple tools and language for community members.

• Good facilitation, coaching and training skills.

• Integrity and sound judgement in handling sensitive financial matters.

• Able to work independently in the field and manage many enterprises at once.

• Commitment to gender equality, inclusion, PSEA and humanitarian principles.

**Languages**

• **Essential:** fluent English; fluent spoken Hausa.

• **Desirable:** Kanuri.

jobs.title: (Senior) Global Project Manager for HQ, based in Geneva, Switzerland
jobs.description:
## **BACKGROUNG ON IMPACT & REACH**

REACH was born in 2010 as a joint initiative of two International NGOs ([IMPACT Initiatives](http://www.impact-initiatives.org/) and [ACTED](http://www.acted.org/)) and the United Nations Operational Satellite Applications Programme ([UNOSAT](http://www.unitar.org/unosat/)). REACH’s **purpose** is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarter is based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support on its fields of intervention.

## **BACKGROUNG ON THE POSITION**

We are currently looking for a **(Senior) Global Project Manager** to join IMPACT’s Global Programmes section at IMPACT Headquarters in Geneva.

**Title:** (Senior) Global Project Manager

**Location:** Geneva, with occasional travels

**Line management:** Reports to the Head of Global Programmes

**Contract duration:** Open ended contract

**Start date:** ASAP

## **POSITION PROFILE**

The Global Project Manager will be responsible for overseeing the effective management and implementation of a portfolio of strategic global projects secured by IMPACT Initiatives, under the supervision of the Head of Global Programmes. The Global Project Manager will work closely with Global Programmes Managers, country teams, HQ departments, donors and external partners, and maintain a functional link with the Head of Projects and Partnerships Support (PPS).

The Global Project Manager will oversee and coordinate key aspects of the programme cycle across the portfolio, including implementation follow-up, donor reporting, support to grant management processes, partner engagement, funding allocations and the identification of programme-level risks and dependencies. In doing so, they will support organisational leadership in maintaining visibility over programme performance, facilitating effective decision-making, and ensuring alignment across the various stakeholders involved in programme delivery.

The position aims to complement, rather than duplicate, existing grant administration, compliance, financial monitoring and contractual management functions led by PPS and Finance. The role leverages tracking systems and processes maintained by these teams to support programme-level coordination, oversight and decision-making. Likewise, the role complements, rather than replaces, the leadership responsibilities of Global Programmes Managers and other designated activity leads, such as country representatives for the country-level portion of project implementation, who retain accountability for programme strategy, technical direction, methodological choices and implementation approaches.

The position requires a profile combining strong project management skills with a practical understanding of humanitarian programme implementation in the field of assessments, analysis and applied research. The Global Project Manager should be comfortable coordinating across multiple countries and teams, consolidating complex information for institutional donor reporting, facilitating engagement across a wide range of stakeholders, supporting funding allocation processes, and helping resolve implementation bottlenecks in complex operating environments. Previous experience managing humanitarian programmes, familiarity with IMPACT's work and understanding of the assessment and analysis sector are therefore strongly valued.

## **FUNCTION & RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Global Project Manager's responsibilities will be delivered under the supervision of the Head of Global Programmes and in close collaboration with all SLT members, HQ departments and country teams, particularly the Head of PPS. The role serves as a key programme management focal point across complex global programmes, supporting effective coordination, decision-making and follow-up across multiple stakeholders and functions. They will include:

1. **PROJECT COORDINATION AND DONOR REPORTING**

- Oversee the implementation of assigned global projects and ensure progress against approved activities, deliverables, indicators, budgets and contractual commitments, building from existing tracking tools implemented by PPS and Finance teams where relevant.
- Develop and maintain detailed project-level workplans that can be shared with all project stakeholders to increase visibility on project ambitions, timelines and status.
- Coordinate project kick off meetings and regular project progress and quality reviews with Global Programmes Managers, country teams, partners and relevant HQ departments;
- Maintain oversight of contractually required deliverables and reporting deadlines across assigned grants and coordinate/consolidate high-quality narrative reporting to institutional donors, including inputs from country teams, partners and relevant HQ departments;
- In close coordination with the Project and Partnership Support (PPS) and Finance teams, coordinate donor queries and contractual modifications, including amendments, budget revisions and no-cost extensions, as required;

**2. RISK IDENTIFICATION AND MANAGEMENT**

- Identify implementation delays, bottlenecks and risks, and support relevant teams in defining and following up on corrective measures;
- In the case of major risks that can have organizational implications or require cross-department engagement, ensure, via the Head of Global Programmes, that the Executive Team and the Senior Leadership Team are informed and enabled to take action.
- When required, liaise with Finance and PPS teams to initiate possible contractual realignment;
- Ensure that implementation challenges, lessons learned and associated mitigation measures are appropriately documented and leveraged in subsequent phases of the project.

**3. POOLED FUND MANAGEMENT**

- In collaboration with the Head of Global Programmes and the Head of PPS, support the coordination internal pooled funding and allocation mechanisms, from the preparation of allocation processes through tracking of activity progress and deliverables;
- Coordinate the review and follow-up of allocations, ensuring processes are appropriately documented and aligned with project objectives and donor requirements;
- Monitor implementation, deliverables and reporting across recipient countries and maintain a consolidated overview of progress;
- Liaise with the Projects and Partnership support team Finance Department to ensure organizational visibility around implementation delays, under-spending and other risks and facilitate corrective action, reprogramming or reallocation where required.

**4. DONOR AND PARTNER ENGAGEMENT**

- Engage with project focal points on the donor side to provide updates on activity progress, and help orient them to the right focal points within the organization depending on their queries (for example, re-direct questions around contracting and payment modalities to the PPS or finance teams).
- For projects delivered in a consortium (as of October 2026, the ECHO Policy HIP project) :
- Track partners’ activity progress against project level workplans, and consolidate reporting.
- Facilitate and chair partner meetings to provide and collect progress updates on the delivery of the project, identify and troubleshoot delivery issues.
- Ensure partners understand and comply with relevant project, donor and IMPACT programmatic, financial and reporting requirements, and communicate any compliance risks promptly with PPS for action.
- Identify partnership-related challenges or compliance issues and facilitate their timely resolution with the support of PPS and Finance teams.

**5. FUNDRAISING**

- In close coordination with the Head of Global Programmes and the PPS team, initiate engagement with existing donors around project renewals or extensions
- Convene project activity leads and key partners around the identification of programmatic priorities for the next iteration of projects in the context of a renewal
- In support of the Executive Team, contribute to funding diversification by supporting the implementation of an organizational fundraising appeal, which may require engagement and relationship building with new institutional donors as well as philanthropies.
- With the support of the Communications and Advocacy and Global Programmes team, develop fundraising materials that can help convey IMPACT’s value added to a wide variety of potential funding partners across the humanitarian, development and private sectors.

## **KEY DELIVERABLES**

- Assigned global and multi-country projects are implemented in line with agreed workplans, budgets, deliverables and donor requirements.
- High-quality donor reports and other contractual deliverables are consolidated and submitted on time.
- Up-to-date consolidated project monitoring provides clear visibility on implementation progress, expenditure, risks and upcoming milestones.
- Pooled fund allocations are effectively managed and monitored from allocation through implementation and close-out.
- Implementing partnerships are effectively established and followed up, with timely identification and resolution of implementation and compliance issues.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- Excellent academic qualifications, including Master's degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. project management, development, humanitarian studies, international relations, research methods, social sciences).
- At least 10 years of experience in the development or humanitarian sector; experience in field-based roles and across multiple geographies an asset.
- Familiarity with needs assessments and analysis, applied research in humanitarian or development settings.
- Familiarity with the humanitarian system and global humanitarian policy frameworks, in particular the Grand Bargain, the HPC and the JIAF.
- Demonstrated experience directly managing and implementing humanitarian projects, preferably including experience at country/field level. Experience with complex, multi-country and/or multi-partner projects is a strong asset;
- Demonstrated experience managing institutional donor grants throughout the project cycle, including implementation follow-up, donor reporting and contractual compliance;
- Strong understanding of institutional donor requirements; prior experience with ECHO, Sida, SDC, GAC and/or comparable institutional donors is highly desirable;
- Demonstrated experience working with implementing partners, including partnership set-up, implementation follow-up and reporting; example leading complex consortia a strong asset.
- Excellent organisational, coordination and planning skills, including the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines and coordinate effectively across teams, countries and functions;
- Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting.
- Strong interpersonal skills, including good external engagement and coordination skills.
- Willingness and ability for short term deployments, including to complex and challenging security environments.
- Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility.
- Fluency in English and French required, given the regional remit of the position; Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese or Ukrainian an asset.
- Ability to operate InDesign is a plus.

## COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

For this position, gross salary between **5,892 CHF and 6,221** CHF monthly (before income tax). NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education and experience of staff. A contribution to medical insurance of 489 CHF per month is already included in the salary figure.

- Insurance covering professional and non-professional accidents throughout the period of employment with IMPACT
- Health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance in case of field visits/temporary deployments
- Enrolment in IMPACT Initiatives Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.
- Applicants must hold a valid work permit for Switzerland or be EU/EFTA citizens
- Up to 40% of remote work on a weekly basis

jobs.title: Infrastructure / Irrigation Engineer
jobs.description:
**Job Purpose:**

Under the supervision of the Livelihood Project Manager, t he Infrastructure Engineer leads all civil, structural and electrical works on the livelihood facilities in MMC, Jere and Mafa LGAs. That covers buildings, pump houses, ponds' civil works, boreholes, solar power, fencing, drainage and storage. The engineer makes sure every structure is safe, durable and protected against floods, and that it is handed over with the documents needed to maintain it.

**Key Responsibilities :**

1. Infrastructure condition assessments

- Assess the structural, civil and electrical condition of every facility: buildings, roofs, foundations, pond embankments, concrete works, boreholes, tanks, fencing, drainage and power systems.
- Check site risks, including flood exposure (as in 2024), erosion, access in the rainy season, theft and fire. Recommend engineering measures to reduce them.
- Confirm site boundaries and access routes against the ownership and tenure audit, together with the Social Cohesion Officer.
- Produce an assessment report for each facility, with photos, condition ratings, a prioritised list of works, BoQs and cost estimates.

2\. Design and documentation
- Prepare drawings, specifications and BoQs for repairs and minor works: pump houses, sumps, stores, foundations for machinery, fencing, drainage, flood protection and roof repairs.
- Design solar power and electrical installations for the Mafa tailoring hub, the feed mill and the irrigation pumps, in coordination with the Agricultural Engineer. Include safe wiring, earthing, surge protection and secure panel mounting.
- Design borehole rehabilitation, including tests of yield and water quality where needed.
- Apply accessible design (ramps, safe access) and gender-sensitive features (lighting, separate toilets) where relevant.
- Get technical approval from the Ministry of Water Resources (boreholes) and the relevant government works departments.

3\. Procurement and contract management
- Prepare technical tender documents and evaluation criteria for civil and electrical works.
- Sit on technical evaluation panels; check contractors' capacity and past work.
- Review contractor work plans, method statements and health and safety plans before work starts.

4\. Construction supervision and quality control
- Supervise works on site regularly. Check materials, setting out, concrete mixes and curing, reinforcement, masonry, roofing and electrical installations against drawings and specifications.
- Keep site diaries, measure completed works, approve interim payment certificates and manage variations within approved limits.
- Enforce health, safety and environmental standards: personal protective equipment, safe excavation, electrical safety, waste disposal, and no child labour.
- Make sure contractors hire local labour where possible, including women and youth, and that their workers sign and respect the Code of Conduct.
- Escalate delays, defects, cost overruns or community concerns to the Project Manager immediately.

5\. Completion, certification and handover of works
- Carry out completion inspections with the government counterpart and the facility committee. Issue snag lists and verify that defects are corrected.
- Issue structural and electrical safety certificates. Coordinate joint commissioning with the Agricultural Engineer where works meet.
- Collect as-built drawings, warranties, borehole logs and electrical diagrams for every site.
- Manage the defects liability period and contractor retention.

6\. Maintenance planning and asset records
- Prepare preventive maintenance schedules for buildings, ponds, boreholes, fencing, drainage and solar systems, timed to the seasons (for example, repairs before the rainy season).
- With the Asset Management and Logistics Officer, enter every structure and installation into the asset register, with specifications, useful life and condition rating.
- Train facility committees and operators in basic inspection, cleaning (for example solar panels), minor repairs and when to call a technician.
- Provide maintenance and replacement cost estimates to the Business Development Officer, for the asset renewal reserves.

7\. Reporting
- Submit weekly site progress reports with photos, and monthly engineering reports.
- Take part in quarterly joint monitoring visits and the annual asset verification. Prepare the infrastructure part of handover inventories.

Cross-cutting duties
- Design for low running costs, durability, climate resilience and community management.
- Apply do-no-harm: consult landowners and communities before any works that affect boundaries, access or shared resources.
- Follow PSEA, safeguarding, anti-fraud and security procedures.
- Carry out any other reasonable duties related to the project, as assigned by the Project Manager.

## Qualifications, experience and competencies

### Education and registration

- **Essential:** a B.Eng or B.Sc in Civil Engineering (Structural or Water Resources option preferred), or Building Engineering.
- **Desirable:** an M.Eng or M.Sc in Civil, Structural or Water Resources Engineering.

### Experience

**Essential**

- At least 5 years of experience designing and supervising civil works, including at least 3 years on rural or humanitarian infrastructure.
- Proven experience preparing BoQs, drawings, specifications and tender documents, and managing contractors through to completion and defects liability.
- Experience supervising concrete, masonry, roofing, earthworks and fencing to quality standards.
- Experience with borehole rehabilitation or water supply infrastructure.
- Experience with NGOs, UN agencies or government programmes in North-East Nigeria or a similar setting.

**Desirable**

- Experience with solar power systems for productive use (pumping, small industry).
- Experience with flood-resilient design and drainage.
- Experience with infrastructure for agriculture, aquaculture or agro-processing.
- Experience handing infrastructure over to communities, and with maintenance planning.

### Skills and competencies

- Strong technical design skills; proficient in AutoCAD and quantity surveying, and in project scheduling tools.
- Rigorous quality control and attention to safety on site.
- Integrity in procurement, measurement and certification of works.
- Able to explain technical issues simply to communities, government officials and non-technical staff.
- Able to plan and manage several sites at the same time.
- Commitment to safeguarding, PSEA, inclusion and humanitarian principles.

Proficient in MS Office or Google Workspace
- **Languages**
- Proficiency in English (written and spoken)
- Knowledge and fluency in English and local languages (Hausa and Kanuri) will be an asset.

jobs.title: VSLA Officer - MMC and Jere
jobs.description:
**JOB PURPOSE:**

Under the supervision of the Livelihood Project Manager, the VSLA Officer sets up and strengthens Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) among the members and users of the livelihood facilities in MMC, Jere and Mafa LGAs. The aim is that tailors, fish farmers, irrigating farmers and feed mill operators can save, borrow and reinvest without depending on the project.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Mapping and mobilisation**

- Map existing VSLAs, cooperatives' savings practices and financial service providers around each facility.
- Decide, with the Business Development Officer, where to strengthen existing groups and where to form new ones.
- Mobilise facility members and users through information sessions. Explain that VSLAs are voluntary, self-managed and self-financed, and that the project gives no grants or loan capital to them.
- Make sure women, youth, persons with disabilities, IDPs and returnees can join, and that membership is self-selected.

**2. Group formation and training**

- Form or reactivate VSLAs following a recognised methodology.
- Train each group in the core modules: groups, leadership and elections; developing policies and rules; developing the constitution; the first savings meeting; the first loan meeting and loan repayment; and share-out and graduation.
- Support each group to elect its management committee (Chair, Secretary, Box Keeper, two Money Counters, key holders), agree its constitution, and set share values, loan terms, interest and social fund contributions.
- Arrange the supply of savings kits: lockable cash box, passbooks, stamps and ink, ledger and calculator.

**3. Supervision and coaching**

- Visit each group regularly: weekly during the intensive phase (about the first 12 weeks), then every two weeks or monthly as the group matures.
- Check meeting procedures, record keeping, cash box security, loan management and transparency.
- Coach groups to fix weaknesses such as late repayments, record errors or poor attendance.
- Support the first share-out and the decision to start a new cycle.

**4. Linking savings to the enterprises**

- Help members plan loans for productive uses linked to their enterprise and cycle, such as inputs before a production or harvest cycle, or materials for an order.
- Deliver short financial literacy sessions on household budgeting, savings goals, managing debt and separating household money from enterprise money.
- Coordinate with the Business Development Officer so VSLA savings complement each cooperative's own funds and asset renewal reserve, and do not mix with them.

**5. Linkages to formal financial services**

- Identify banks, microfinance institutions and mobile money providers that offer suitable, affordable products.
- Help mature groups open group savings accounts and use mobile money to reduce cash risk, where appropriate.
- Prepare credit-ready members and groups for linkage to microfinance where it fits, and explain loan terms and risks clearly.

**6. Community-based trainers**

- Identify and train community-based trainers, mainly women and youth, to support groups and form new ones after the project ends.
- Certify trainers who meet the standard, and agree a fee-for-service or volunteer arrangement with groups.

**7. Monitoring and reporting**

- Collect monthly performance data for each group: membership by sex and age, attendance, savings, loans outstanding, repayment rate, social fund balance and share-out value.
- Use a standard VSLA management information system (MIS) or a digital tool agreed with the MEAL Officer.
- Submit monthly reports and flag groups at risk.
- Contribute to the baseline and endline, success stories and lessons learned.

**Cross-cutting duties**

- Protect members' money: never handle or keep group funds, never act as key holder, and report any suspected misuse.
- Make sure group rules do not exclude or burden the most vulnerable members, and watch for risks to women, such as household tension over savings or loans.
- Follow PSEA, safeguarding, confidentiality and security procedures.
- Carry out any other reasonable duties related to the project, as assigned by the Project Manager

**Qualifications, experience and competencies**

**Education:**

- Essential: a university degree (B.Sc or HND) in Economics, Accounting, Banking and Finance, Business Administration, Cooperative Studies, Agricultural Economics, Social Sciences or a related field.
- **Desirable:** certified training in a recognized VSLA methodology, and in financial literacy or microfinance.

**Experience**

- At least 3 years of experience forming, training and supervising VSLAs or similar savings groups, including at least one full cycle through to share-out.
- Experience training adults with low literacy in savings, loans and record keeping.
- Experience working with NGOs, UN agencies or government programmes in North-East Nigeria.

**Desirable**

- Experience linking savings groups to banks, microfinance institutions or mobile money.
- Experience using a VSLA MIS or mobile data collection tools such as Kobo Toolbox or ODK.
- Experience with livelihoods programms for farmers, fish farmers or artisans.
- Experience training community-based trainers.

**Skills and competencies**

- Strong numeracy and accuracy with financial records.
- Excellent facilitation and training skills; patient and respectful with community members.
- Honest and transparent, with high personal integrity in handling financial matters.
- Able to manage many groups across several locations and keep to a supervision schedule.
- Sensitive to gender and inclusion issues in household finances.
- Commitment to PSEA, safeguarding and humanitarian principles.
- Proficient in MS Office or Google Workspace, especially spreadsheets.

**Languages**

- Essential: fluent Hausa; good written and spoken English.
- Desirable: Kanuri will be an asset.

jobs.title: Türkiye Kurumsal ve Bağışçı İlişkileri Sorumlusu [TR]
jobs.description:
**İşin Özeti**

Pozisyon, derneğin Türkiye’deki kurumlar ve bağışçılarla ilişkilerini geliştirmek ve yönetmek, iş birliği ve ortaklık fırsatları oluşturmak, bağışçı ilişkilerini güçlendirmek, destek ve bağış fırsatları ile proje tekliflerini takip etmekten sorumludur. Ayrıca resmî toplantı ve ziyaretlerin koordine edilmesi, faaliyetlerin kayıt altına alınması ve dönemsel raporların hazırlanmasını kapsar.

**Eğitim ve Nitelik Gereklilikleri**

İşletme, Halkla İlişkiler, Siyaset Bilimi ve Kamu Yönetimi veya ilgili alanlarda lisans mezunu olmak.

Türkçeyi profesyonel düzeyde kullanabilmek.

**Gerekli Yetkinlikler**

- Etkili iletişim becerisi
- Öncelik belirleme ve zaman yönetimi becerisi
- Müzakere, ikna ve problem çözme becerisi
- Karar verme ve sorumluluk alma becerisi
- Organizasyon, koordinasyon ve takip becerisi
- İnsanlarla etkili iletişim kurma ve sunum yapma becerisi
- Rapor hazırlama ve resmî yazışma becerisi
- Kurumsal temsil ve resmî iletişim becerisi
- Uzaktan çalışma becerisi
- Raporlama becerisi
- Bilgisayar ve ofis programlarını kullanma becerisi:
- Outlook
- Teams
- Word
- Excel
- PowerPoint
- OneDrive

**Görev ve Sorumluluklar**

- Derneğin Türkiye'deki kurumsal ilişkilerini; kamu kurumları, belediyeler, yerel kuruluşlar, sivil toplum kuruluşları, şirketler, iş insanları, vakıflar ve derneğin faaliyet alanıyla ilgili bağışçı kurumlarla geliştirmek ve yönetmek.
- Derneği, belirlenen yetki ve görevlendirmeler doğrultusunda ilgili toplantı, görüşme ve etkinliklerde temsil etmek; derneğin Türk kurumları nezdindeki kurumsal varlığını ve ilişkilerini güçlendirmek.
- Türk kurumlarıyla iş birliği ve ortaklık fırsatlarını geliştirmek; derneğin hedeflerine ve kaynaklarının güçlendirilmesine katkı sağlayacak ortak yardım kampanyaları ve kurumsal sosyal sorumluluk projeleri belirlemek.
- Türkiye'deki potansiyel bağışçıları ve hibe sağlayan kurumları araştırmak, mevcut destek ve hibe fırsatlarını değerlendirmek; doğrudan yöneticisiyle koordinasyon içinde yeni bağışçıların kazanılmasına yönelik çalışmaları planlamak ve takip etmek.
- İlgili Türk kurumları ile mevcut ve potansiyel bağışçılara ilişkin iletişim bilgilerini, ilişki durumunu, iş birliği ve hibe fırsatlarını ve takip süreçlerinin güncel durumunu içeren veri tabanını oluşturmak ve güncel tutmak.
- Bağışçılarla ilişkileri geliştirmek ve yönetmek; düzenli iletişimi sürdürmek, bağışçıların derneğe olan güvenini ve desteğinin devamlılığını güçlendirmek, talep ve sorularını takip etmek.
- Türk kurumları ve bağışçılarla yapılacak kurumsal toplantı ve ziyaretleri planlamak ve koordine etmek; gerekli hazırlıkları yapmak, toplantı çıktılarını kayıt altına almak ve üzerinde mutabık kalınan işlemleri tamamlanıncaya kadar takip etmek.
- Bağışçı kurumlara sunulan proje, hibe ve bağış tekliflerini takip etmek; geri dönüş ve karar süreçlerini izlemek, doğrudan yöneticisi ve ilgili birimlerle koordinasyon içinde destek fırsatlarını somut iş birliklerine veya katkılara dönüştürmeye yönelik çalışmalar yürütmek.
- Türk kurumları ve bağışçılarla yürütülen resmî yazışmaları takip etmek; derneğin yürürlükteki prosedürleri doğrultusunda kayıt altına almak ve arşivlemek.
- Kurumsal ilişkiler ve hibe faaliyetlerine ilişkin haftalık ve dönemsel raporlar hazırlamak; elde edilen sonuçları, karşılaşılan zorlukları ve önerileri raporlamak.
- Dış ilişkiler ve finansman ihtiyaçlarının belirlenmesi, toplantıların hazırlanması ve proje sunumları ile hibe tekliflerinin oluşturulması için gerekli bilgi ve belgelerin temini amacıyla derneğin ilgili birimleriyle koordinasyon sağlamak.
- Türk kurumları ve bağışçılarla ilişkilerde resmî protokol ve teamüllere uygun hareket etmek; derneğin kurumsal imajının, güvenilirliğinin ve ilişkilerinin güçlendirilmesine katkı sağlamak.
- İnsan Kaynakları Departmanı ile iş birliği içinde temel idari görevleri yürütmek. Bu kapsamda görev tanımlarının hazırlanması ve düzenli olarak güncellenmesi, performans değerlendirme süreçleri, kapasite geliştirme planları, devam takibi, departman/birim içindeki işe alım süreçleri ve çalışanlarla ilgili konularda İnsan Kaynakları Departmanı ile koordinasyon sağlanması yer alır. Ayrıca ekibin ilgili prosedürlere uyumunu teşvik etmek.

**Çocuk Koruma Politikas**

ATAA Derneği, çocuklara yönelik her türlü istismarı kabul edilemez olarak değerlendirmekte ve faaliyetlerinin tüm alanlarında çocukları zarardan koruma sorumluluğunun bilincinde hareket etmektedir. Dernek, çocuklar için güvenli bir ortam sağlamayı taahhüt eder ve çocuk istismarı ile sömürüsünün her türüne karşı sıfır tolerans yaklaşımını benimser.

**Ayrımcılık, İstismar ve Tacizin Önlenmesi Politikası**

ATAA Derneği, tüm iş başvurusu sahiplerine eşit istihdam fırsatları sunar. Irk, din, köken, yaş, medeni durum, uyruk, engellilik veya askerlik durumu temelinde gerçekleşen her türlü ayrımcılığa, istismara veya cinsel ya da diğer türden tacize tolerans göstermez.

ATAA Derneği çalışanları hiçbir koşulda ayrımcılık, taciz, fiziksel, cinsel veya sözlü istismar, tehdit, sömürü ya da dernek içinde veya dışında başkalarının haklarını ihlal eden herhangi bir davranışta bulunamaz.

jobs.title: Independent Nutrition Expert Consultancy Services
jobs.company: Center for Operational Analysis and Research
jobs.description:
**Scope of Services (SoS)**

**Nature of Services:** Independent Nutrition Expert Consultancy Services

**Place of Performance:** Such location as determined by the Consultant when performing the Services subject to any location-specific requirements expressly agreed in writing for a particular assignment.

**Level of Effort:** Assignment-based and strictly as mutually agreed in writing for specific tasks and deliverables. No minimum number of days/hours, fixed working hours, or continuing level of effort is guaranteed or required.

**Type of Contract:** Services will be provided on a day-rate basis against specific project assignments, deliverables, and estimated levels of effort agreed between COAR and the Consultant.

**Timeframe:** The anticipated term of this consultancy is from 09 November 2026 to 31 December 2027, subject to execution of the applicable agreement. The term establishes the period during which assignments may be agreed; it does not create an obligation to provide or accept assignments, guarantee a minimum workload, or require continuous availability. Any extension shall be subject to mutual written agreement.

**Primary Point of Contact:** COAR's designated Senior Programs Manager, acting as the contact for agreeing assignment requirements, coordinating necessary project inputs, clarifying deliverables, addressing technical queries and reviewing completed outputs against the agreed scope. This role is for assignment coordination and does not confer authority to direct the Consultant's day-to-day working methods or exercise line-management authority over the Consultant.

**Overview:** This Scope of Services (SoS) outlines the independent consultancy services of a Nutrition Expert engaged by the Center for Operational Analysis and Research (COAR). The Consultant will provide independent technical and programmatic expertise to support agreed research, analytical, and advisory outputs relating to nutrition programming in humanitarian, development, and other relevant operational contexts. The Consultant may contribute technical analysis and recommendations across the programme cycle, including needs assessment, programme design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and learning, as relevant to each assignment. Activities may include reviewing specified nutrition assessments, programme documents, monitoring reports, evaluation findings, and response plans; analysing quantitative and qualitative data; assessing nutrition-related needs, programme approaches, and operational challenges; providing technical input on nutrition interventions and programme strategies; and drafting or contributing to research reports, analytical products, guidance notes, and recommendations. Where expressly included in an assignment agreed in writing, the Services may also include conducting primary and secondary research, undertaking stakeholder consultations or interviews, reviewing programme approaches and partner documentation, and providing technical input on monitoring frameworks, indicators, and the interpretation of nutrition-related findings.

**Nature of the consultancy:** This is an independent, non-exclusive, project-based consultancy engagement and not a position of employment with COAR. Services will be commissioned through specific assignments agreed in writing between COAR and the Consultant, setting out the relevant scope, deliverables, estimated level of effort, timeframe and applicable day rate.

COAR does not guarantee any minimum number of assignments or consultancy days, and the Consultant will remain free to accept or decline proposed assignments and to provide services to other clients, subject to confidentiality, conflicts of interest and the timely delivery of any assignment accepted.

The Consultant will determine independently the professional approach, methods, sequencing, working time and place of performance of the Services, subject to agreed deliverables, deadlines, applicable legal, contractual, client, security, safeguarding, confidentiality, data-protection, and other project-specific requirements, and reasonable project coordination. The Consultant will ordinarily use their own equipment and working facilities and will be responsible for their own tax, social insurance and other statutory obligations arising from the consultancy. The consultancy does not carry employee benefits.

The Consultant will coordinate their own activities and agreed project inputs but will not occupy a position within COAR’s organisational structure, exercise employment or line-management authority over COAR personnel, or have authority to bind COAR, except where expressly authorised in writing for a defined project purpose.

COAR may specify the scope, required outputs, deadlines, quality standards, project requirements, and information required for an agreed assignment, but will not direct the Consultant as to the manner or means of performing the Services.

The Consultant will not be required to work fixed hours, maintain continuous availability, attend COAR premises on a regular basis, or participate in COAR’s internal management or personnel processes, except where specific attendance or participation is reasonably necessary for an agreed assignment.

Fees will be payable only for Services performed under an agreed assignment and against submission of appropriate invoices. No minimum volume of work or continuing retainer is guaranteed.

**About COAR:** COAR is an independent social enterprise that directly supports practitioners, policymakers, and donors by facilitating humanitarian and development interventions in complex, fragile, and high-risk environments.

**Objectives**

- To provide independent technical and programmatic expertise in nutrition, drawing on relevant professional experience and specialist knowledge, for the specific subject matter and outputs defined in each assignment.
- To contribute to the preparation, review, and, where specifically agreed, finalisation of research and analytical deliverables, including quantitative and qualitative data analysis, primary and secondary research, programme assessments, and technical reporting related to nutrition.
- To analyse nutrition-related needs, interventions, programme approaches, implementation challenges, and operational considerations in humanitarian and development contexts, as relevant to the agreed assignment.
- To review specified nutrition assessments, programme documents, monitoring reports, evaluation findings, response plans, and other relevant technical materials, providing evidence-based observations and recommendations.
- To provide technical input into nutrition programme design, implementation approaches, monitoring and evaluation frameworks, indicators, and learning products, where relevant to the Consultant's expertise and the agreed scope.
- To conduct agreed primary and secondary research, including stakeholder consultations and interviews where required, within the applicable level of effort and project requirements.
- To prepare or review specified reports, analytical products, contextual assessments, technical notes, articles, guidance materials, or other outputs where the deliverables and delivery schedule have been agreed in writing. Where an assignment includes recurring products, the parties shall agree in advance on the number or frequency of products, expected level of effort, and applicable fees.
- To undertake additional project-specific technical work only where separately agreed in writing, including the relevant scope, deliverables, estimated effort, schedule, and fees.

**Required Professional Experience and Expertise**

*The Consultant engaged for an assignment should possess professional expertise relevant to the Services to be commissioned, including, as applicable:*

- A minimum of five years of relevant professional experience in nutrition, nutrition programming, nutrition research, public health nutrition, or a closely related field at national and/or international level.
- Demonstrated knowledge of relevant nutrition concepts, approaches, and interventions, particularly in humanitarian and development settings, as appropriate to the assignment.
- Experience in nutrition-related programme design, implementation, assessment, monitoring, evaluation, research, or technical analysis, depending on the requirements of the assignment.
- Ability to review and interpret quantitative and qualitative data and relevant technical documentation, and to translate findings into clear, evidence-based analysis and practical recommendations.
- Familiarity with relevant nutrition assessment approaches, indicators, monitoring frameworks, evaluation methodologies, and technical guidance, as applicable to the assignment.
- Understanding of the operational, institutional, and contextual factors that influence the design, delivery, and effectiveness of nutrition programmes.
- Fluency in oral and written English.
- Ability to communicate professionally and organise the work required to complete accepted assignments.
- Demonstrated ability to work to agreed deadlines and liaise effectively with donor representatives, partner organisations, technical specialists, and other stakeholders where reasonably necessary for agreed project activities and subject to the applicable level of effort.
- Demonstrated ability to provide services independently while coordinating effectively with COAR colleagues and relevant stakeholders where reasonably necessary for agreed project activities.
- Ability to plan and prioritise work across assignments the Consultant has accepted and to deliver the agreed outputs within applicable deadlines.
- Ability to produce accurate, well-organised, analytical, and appropriately detailed professional outputs.
- Strong presentation, reporting, analytical, and communication skills.
- Experience in Myanmar is a plus;
- Being located in the Asia time zone is a plus but not required.
- High level of professionalism, discretion, and commitment to confidentiality and where applicable, the Consultant shall comply with the safeguarding, confidentiality, data-protection, information-security, health-and-safety and client-mandated requirements which COAR identifies in writing as applicable to external service providers. For the avoidance of doubt, COAR’s general employee handbook, working-hours, attendance, leave, appraisal, disciplinary and grievance procedures shall not apply.
