jobs.title: Technical Advisor - Law Enforcement and Wildlife Crime Prevention.
jobs.description:
**Reporting to:** Technical Director.
**Working Relationships:** Senior Consultant in Protected Area Management, Marine Landscape Coordinator, WCS Gabon technical teams, WCS park managers, ANPN, MINEF, DGPA, Ministry of the Sea, and other relevant government agencies.
**Work Location:** Libreville, with frequent field assignments in national parks, landscapes, and project sites where WCS operates in Gabon.

**Position Type:** Full time

**Overview of the Program in Gabon:**

WCS’s history in Gabon began in 1985 with the first national census of forest elephants, followed by a comprehensive assessment of conservation priorities. This work contributed to the creation of the network of 13 national parks in 2002 and subsequently to the development of the network of marine protected areas. In October 2025, WCS and the National Agency for National Parks (ANPN) signed a partnership agreement establishing a roadmap to prepare for long-term collaborative management partnerships for several parks. This roadmap includes Priority Support Projects (PSPs) designed to address urgent operational needs, strengthen management systems, and lay the technical, institutional, operational, and financial groundwork for future Collaborative Management Partnerships (CMPs). Law enforcement and wildlife crime prevention efforts are further supported by several projects and funding sources within the WCS Gabon portfolio, notably the INL project to combat wildlife trafficking and the NaturAfrica project to support protected area management. The objective is to mobilize this support within a common programmatic framework by strengthening systems, capacities, and tools that can be used sustainably by national authorities and park managers, including in the preparation of future CMPs.

**Job Summary**

WCS is seeking a LEM/CWT ((Law Enforcement Management/ Counter Wildlife Trafficking) Technical Advisor to strengthen protection, monitoring, and law enforcement in terrestrial and marine protected areas supported by its program, in support of the relevant government agencies and in accordance with their sovereign mandates.

As WCS’s technical lead in this field, he or she will support operational mechanisms and supervise specialized teams. Park managers retain operational control of the sites; the Senior Protected Area Management Consultant consolidates cross-cutting contributions under the supervision of the technical directorate.

He or she coordinates support from various projects to build shared and sustainable systems and capacities, and contributes to the development of new projects and funding.

At the national level, he or she monitors and supports developments in legal and institutional frameworks, particularly with regard to the CMPs and the Water and Forestry Paramilitary Corps. For targeted parks, he or she prepares LEM/CWT contributions to WCS’s internal commitment documents and to the transition to the CMPs.

**Job Objectives**

- Develop an LEM/CWT framework tailored to terrestrial and marine contexts, contributing to its legal and institutional evolution through technical provisions.
- Strengthen the capacities of partner government agencies, WCS teams, and park managers according to their roles and needs.
- Develop interoperable information and operational monitoring systems to support planning and decision-making.
- Improve the effectiveness of wildlife protection and anti-poaching measures at priority sites.
- Prepare the LEM/CWT component of WCS’s commitments and future CMPs, with clearly defined responsibilities, capacities, and financial needs.

**Key Responsibilities**

**A) LEM/CWT Technical Support for Priority Sites and the PSP/CMP Process**

- Assess, together with Director Conservators, WCS park managers, and relevant government agencies, LEM/CWT threats, capacities, and needs; define priorities and roadmaps for monitoring and anti-poaching programs.
- Enhance intelligence-led patrols, information collection and analysis, case management, and legal follow-up, with inter-institutional and, where relevant, cross-border coordination.
- Plan the equipment, infrastructure, logistics, and maintenance required for operations: mobility, communications, command posts and operations rooms, drones, and geospatial tools. Deploy interoperable systems, including SMART, EarthRanger, and—in marine environments—Skylight/Global Fishing Watch, in conjunction with relevant national systems.
- In northeastern Gabon, provide support in particular to the CWT coordination center in Makokou and the LEM/CWT units in Ivindo, Minkébé, and the associated landscape. Along the coast, support land, coastal, and maritime surveillance operations and, in Mayumba, the cooperation mechanisms of the Mayumba-Conkouati Transboundary Park.
- For parks participating in the PSP/CMP, prepare LEM/CWT contributions in collaboration with the senior consultant, park managers, regional WCS experts, and relevant authorities: risks, responsibilities, and chains of command; standards; investment needs and recurring costs; transition conditions; and points requiring resolution. These contributions inform the operational plans, business plans, and commitment proposals according to a shared timeline; the Technical Committee addresses review comments. Commitment decisions and institutional approvals are the responsibility of WCS and the relevant authorities, respectively.

**B) LEM/CWT Structural Support at the National Level, Coordination, and Knowledge Sharing**

- Organize technical reviews and exchanges between sites and with the ANPN operations center; document best practices, limitations, and cost models to identify solutions to be harmonized or scaled up nationwide.
- With the support of legal experts, competent authorities, and partners, monitor current and proposed legal and institutional frameworks; analyze their impact on the mandates, status of ecoguards and rangers, responsibilities, coordination, and governance of protected areas.
- Based on challenges documented in the field, propose improvements to the future LEM/CWT framework: rationale, options, feasibility, costs, and operational impacts. Review these with legal experts as needed and finalize them with the senior consultant for cross-cutting issues before submitting them to the authorized authorities.
- Support the updating and harmonization of LEM/CWT methods, tools, and standards used by WCS and its partners, by capitalizing on field experiences and integrating, where relevant, innovative approaches and new technologies: operational concepts, SOPs, emergency protocols, data collection and analysis systems, monitoring and decision-support tools, operations room architecture, training programs, and post-training follow-up mechanisms.
- Coordinate WCS Gabon’s LEM/CWT portfolio: supervise technical staff, consultants, and trainers; contribute to planning, budgeting, and procurement in collaboration with the Program and Finance teams, as well as to monitoring results, reporting, and funding proposals.
- Assess skills needs by function and implement the LEM/CWT component of the overall capacity-building plan consolidated by the senior consultant: training, coaching, practical exercises, and internal knowledge transfer. Integrate human rights, crime scene management, and legal procedures; evaluate learning outcomes and their application. Fleet managers organize the implementation of these practices within their teams.

**Expected Results and Outputs for This Support**

- **Internal engagement and preparation of CMPs:** LEM/CWT contribution by fleet covering the elements described in Section A, in accordance with the content and review schedule agreed upon with the Technical Directorate and the senior consultant. Internal analyses are reused and updated—where relevant—in discussions with the ANPN regarding PSPs and CMPs.
- **Capacity building:** initial assessment, training or coaching program and materials, review of skills acquired and applied, remaining needs, and follow-up actions, based on criteria agreed upon at the outset.
- **Legal and institutional frameworks:** record of current and proposed changes, analysis of implications, monitoring of system and procedure adjustments, and proposal notes for the future framework where relevant.
- **Operational support and harmonization:** site-specific roadmaps, updated guidelines and tools, and summaries of technical reviews and lessons learned.

**Qualifications Requirements:**

**a) LEM/CWT expertise and protection operations**

- Master’s degree (or equivalent) in conservation, natural resource management, security, criminology, law, public administration, or a related field; or demonstrated equivalent professional experience.
- Significant experience in technical management or technical assistance for law enforcement operations, protected area conservation, or combating wildlife/environmental crime; experience in Central Africa is a significant asset.
- A good understanding of chains of command, operational planning, intelligence-led patrols, case management procedures, judicial follow-up, and interagency coordination.
- Experience coordinating multi-agency operations is an advantage.

**b) Information Systems and Operational Technologies**

- Proficiency or solid experience with SMART and/or comparable tools; experience with EarthRanger, GIS, GPS, and communication systems is highly valued.
- Ability to transform operational data into analyses, priorities, deployment plans, and recommendations that can be used by field leaders and decision-makers.

**c) Institutional Advisory Services, Planning, and Funding**

- Ability to analyze organizational structures, responsibilities, staffing needs, and operational costs, and to translate these analyses into procedures, roadmaps, budgets, and realistic scenarios.
- Experience advising public administrations; ability to analyze the operational implications of legal and institutional changes in collaboration with legal experts and to propose field-based improvements.
- Experience in preparing operational and financial plans for protected areas, business plans, or comparable frameworks is desirable, along with the ability to contribute to the definition of governance mechanisms and institutional interfaces.

**d) Management, Communication, and Languages**

- Ability to provide technical leadership to multidisciplinary teams, coordinate multiple partners, and simultaneously manage national, field, and project priorities.
- Excellent writing, analytical, synthesis, facilitation, and interpersonal communication skills.
- Fluency in French; a working knowledge of English is a plus.
- Ability to undertake frequent field assignments and to work in field conditions that may be isolated or demanding.

jobs.title: Livelihood Project Activity Manager_Borno State
jobs.description:
**JOB PURPOSE:**

The incumbent will be responsible for the overall management, coordination, and monitoring of Livelihood activities in Borno state. Under the supervision of the FSL Programme Manager, the Livelihood Project Manager leads delivery of the 6-month consolidation phase that turns ten constructed livelihood facilities in MMC, Jere and Mafa LGAs into community-run enterprises with clear ownership, governance and asset management.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Project planning and delivery (20%)

- Lead the inception phase (Months 1): technical assessments, the ownership and tenure audit, conflict analysis and baseline. Turn their results into a costed operational plan for each facility.
- Own the detailed workplan, procurement plan and spending plan, and keep them aligned with the WFP Field Level Agreement (FLA).
- Steer each facility through the five-stage pathway (Assess, Organise, Rehabilitate and equip, operate with support, Consolidate and hand over). Approve each facility's move to the next stage against the agreed exit criteria.
- Lead monthly team reviews; identify delays early and adjust plans.

Technical oversight of facility operationalisation (20%)

- Make sure the technical officers deliver on schedule and to specification:
- Approve the business plan, pricing, cost-recovery and revenue-sharing model for each of the ten enterprises.
- Make sure the facilities supply each other as planned, for example feed from the Mafa mill to all three fish farms and greenhouse seedlings to the irrigation farms.

Ownership, governance and social cohesion (15%)

- Provide senior leadership on landowner negotiations and the Tripartite Facility Management Agreements, working with the Governance and Social Cohesion Officer and the legal adviser.
- Secure the signature of every agreement by the lead MDA or LGA, the community cooperative and the landowning family or traditional institution.
- Serve as secretariat to the State Asset Oversight Committee and attend the LGA Facility Oversight Committees in MMC, Jere and Mafa.
- Champion the Government–Community Compacts and the landowner recognition events. Personally step in on escalated disputes over land, membership or benefits.
- Make sure committee elections, constitutions and safeguards against elite capture are applied consistently.

Asset management (10%)

- Make sure every facility has an up-to-date asset register, tagging, maintenance schedule, spares register and a funded asset renewal reserve.
- Approve major repairs and the declining co-financing of repairs during transition.
- Lead the annual joint asset verification and sign the handover inventories with government and community counterparts.

Partnership and stakeholder management (10%)

- Serve as the main operational counterpart to WFP. Prepare for and host joint monitoring visits and quarterly reviews.
- Build working relationships with lead State MDAs (Agriculture, Water Resources, fisheries, Women Affairs, Lands, Cooperatives), the three LGA Councils, Borno State ADP/FADAMA, traditional rulers and private-sector partners.
- Represent the project in the Food Security Sector and relevant working groups.

Team leadership and people management (10%)

- Recruit, induct, supervise and appraise the project team of 21, with a target of at least 40% female.
- Set clear objectives for each staff member, linked to the handover readiness scorecard.
- Coach staff and promote teamwork across technical, governance and community roles.
- Oversee short-term specialists: legal adviser, feed mill engineer, pump engineer, mediation facilitator, digital solutions provider and endline evaluator.

Finance, procurement and compliance (10%)

- Manage the project budget. Track spending monthly against the plan and flag any variance above 10% to the line manager.
- Make sure all procurement (pumps, feed mill, tailoring equipment, pond materials) follows the organisation's and WFP's rules, with warranties, after-sales service and value for money.
- Approve payments within delegated authority and oversee the tapering transitional stipends for facility operators.
- Make sure the project is ready for audits and keeps complete supporting documentation.

MEAL, reporting and learning (5%)

- Make sure the MEAL system tracks facility functionality, enterprise performance, asset condition, governance and social cohesion indicators.
- Submit accurate, timely narrative and financial reports to WFP and internal management.
- Use monitoring data to adapt the approach, and document lessons and good practice for future WFP resilience programming.

Cross-cutting duties

- Apply do-no-harm and conflict sensitivity in every decision on land, membership and benefits.
- Uphold protection, gender, disability inclusion and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) standards. Make sure the Feedback and Complaints Response Mechanism (FCRM) works.
- Model and enforce PSEA and safeguarding; report any concern immediately through the proper channels.
- Follow security procedures for all movement, especially to Mafa, and keep staff safety first.

*Carry out any other reasonable duties related to the project, as assigned by the line manager.*

## Education & Professional Requirements:

**Education:**

- **Essential:** a university degree in Agricultural Economics, Agriculture, Development Studies, Business Administration, Economics, Sciences, Social Sciences or a related field.
- **Desirable:** a Master's degree in one of these fields.

## Professional experience

- At least 5 years of experience in food security or resilience programmes, including at least 3 years in senior supervisory roles.
- Proven experience delivering projects activities including supervision of procurement and contractors.
- Experience building community-based enterprises or cooperatives, including business planning and cost-recovery systems.
- Experience working with State and LGA government counterparts and traditional institutions in North-East Nigeria.

## Personal requirements

- Ability to lead and motivate a mixed technical and community team under pressure.
- Negotiation, mediation and stakeholder management skills, including on sensitive land and benefit-sharing issues.
- Sound judgement on enterprise viability, pricing and financial sustainability.
- Clear report writing and presentation skills in English.
- Commitment to gender equality, inclusion, AAP, PSEA and humanitarian principles.
- Proficient in MS Office or Google Workspace; able to use data and dashboards for decisions.

## Languages

- **Essential:** fluent written and spoken English; good spoken Hausa.
- Knowledge and fluency in English and local languages (Hausa and Kanuri).

jobs.title: مساعد/ة إداري/ة (Admin Assistant)
jobs.description:
## إعلان وظيفة: مساعد/ة إداري/ة (Admin Assistant)

**المنظمة:** ماري للبحوث والتنمية (MRD)
**المسمى الوظيفي:** مساعد/ة إداري/ة – Admin Assistant
**مكان العمل:** دمشق، سوريا
**نوع الدوام:** دوام كامل

### نبذة عن المنظمة

ماري للبحوث والتنمية (MRD) هي منظمة غير ربحية مرخصة تعمل على دعم السلام والتنمية وتعزيز قدرات المجتمع المدني، من خلال تنفيذ برامج ومشاريع في مجالات الحماية، والصحة والدعم النفسي والاجتماعي، وسبل العيش، والأمن الغذائي، والمياه والإصحاح، وبناء السلام، والحوار المدني، وبناء قدرات منظمات المجتمع المدني.

تعلن MRD عن رغبتها في توظيف **مساعد/ة إداري/ة (Admin Assistant)** للانضمام إلى فريقها في مكتب دمشق، والمساهمة في ضمان سير العمليات اليومية بكفاءة، من خلال تقديم الدعم الإداري واللوجستي، ومتابعة المشتريات والمخزون والأصول، وتنسيق الخدمات والاحتياجات التشغيلية للمكتب والمشاريع.

### الهدف من الوظيفة

تتمثل الغاية من الوظيفة في دعم تنفيذ العمليات الإدارية واللوجستية اليومية لمكتب MRD في دمشق، وضمان توفير المستلزمات والخدمات المطلوبة في الوقت المناسب، والمساهمة في تطبيق إجراءات المشتريات وإدارة الأصول والمخزون وحفظ الوثائق التشغيلية وفقاً لسياسات المنظمة ومتطلبات الجهات المانحة.

سيعمل شاغل/ة الوظيفة بالتنسيق مع فرق البرامج والمالية والإدارة والموردين، بما يضمن كفاءة استخدام الموارد، ودقة التوثيق، والالتزام بإجراءات الشفافية والمساءلة.

### المهام والمسؤوليات الرئيسية

#### أولاً: المهام الإدارية واللوجستية

- متابعة الاحتياجات التشغيلية اليومية لمكتب دمشق، والعمل على تأمين المستلزمات والخدمات الضرورية لضمان استمرارية العمل.
- متابعة احتياجات المكتب من القرطاسية والمواد المكتبية والمستلزمات التشغيلية، وضمان توفرها وفقاً للاحتياجات الفعلية.
- تنظيم ومتابعة المخزون، وتحديث سجلات الاستلام والصرف والأرصدة بصورة دورية.
- متابعة الأصول والموجودات والمعدات المكتبية، وتحديث سجلاتها، والمساهمة في عمليات الجرد الدوري.
- تنسيق خدمات الصيانة والإصلاح والنظافة والاتصالات وغيرها من الخدمات اللازمة لتشغيل المكتب.
- متابعة احتياجات الاجتماعات والتدريبات والفعاليات والزيارات الميدانية، والتأكد من توفر الترتيبات اللوجستية المطلوبة.
- تنسيق حجوزات النقل والإقامة والخدمات اللوجستية المرتبطة بأنشطة المنظمة، وفق الإجراءات المعتمدة.
- متابعة طلبات الخدمات والمستلزمات الواردة من فرق البرامج والمشاريع، وتنسيق الاستجابة لها ضمن الأولويات والموارد المتاحة.
- تنظيم وأرشفة الوثائق الإدارية والتشغيلية وتسهيل الوصول إليها عند الحاجة.
- المساهمة في تحسين تنظيم العمليات اليومية وتحديد الاحتياجات التشغيلية المتكررة واقتراح الحلول المناسبة.

#### ثانياً: المشتريات والتعامل مع الموردين

- استلام طلبات الشراء من الأقسام المعنية ومراجعة اكتمال المعلومات والمواصفات المطلوبة قبل إحالتها للإجراءات المعتمدة.
- جمع عروض الأسعار من الموردين، وإعداد جداول المقارنة الأولية، وتوثيق العروض والخيارات المتاحة.
- التواصل مع الموردين ومقدمي الخدمات ومتابعة الأسعار والتوافر ومواعيد التسليم.
- متابعة إجراءات الشراء والتوريد وفق سياسات MRD، وحدود الصلاحيات، ومتطلبات الجهات المانحة.
- التنسيق لاستلام المواد والخدمات والتحقق من مطابقتها للطلبات والمواصفات المعتمدة، وتوثيق أي نقص أو تلف أو اختلاف.
- جمع وحفظ وثائق المشتريات، بما في ذلك طلبات الشراء وعروض الأسعار والموافقات وأوامر الشراء ومحاضر الاستلام والفواتير.
- متابعة حالة طلبات الشراء المفتوحة والتوريدات المتأخرة، وإبلاغ المسؤول المباشر بأي تحديات قد تؤثر على سير العمل.
- ضمان توثيق إجراءات الشراء بصورة منظمة وقابلة للمراجعة والتدقيق.
- الالتزام بمبادئ الشفافية وتكافؤ الفرص وتجنب تضارب المصالح عند التعامل مع الموردين.

#### ثالثاً: الدعم التشغيلي والمالي

- جمع وتنظيم الوثائق الداعمة للمصروفات التشغيلية والمشتريات، والتأكد من اكتمالها قبل إحالتها إلى قسم المالية.
- متابعة الفواتير والإيصالات ومحاضر الاستلام والوثائق ذات الصلة بالمدفوعات التشغيلية.
- التنسيق مع قسم المالية بشأن استكمال الوثائق المطلوبة لمعالجة المدفوعات وتسوية المصروفات.
- المساعدة في إعداد جداول متابعة المشتريات والمصروفات التشغيلية والمخزون والأصول.
- إدخال البيانات التشغيلية وتحديث سجلات المتابعة باستخدام برامج Microsoft Office، وخاصة Excel.
- متابعة المستندات الإدارية والمالية المرتبطة بالموردين والخدمات التشغيلية، وضمان أرشفتها بطريقة منظمة.
- الالتزام بالفصل بين المهام التشغيلية والمالية وفق الصلاحيات المعتمدة، وعدم تنفيذ أو اعتماد أي عملية خارج نطاق المسؤوليات الممنوحة للوظيفة.

#### رابعاً: التنسيق والامتثال وإعداد التقارير

- التنسيق المستمر مع فرق البرامج والمالية والإدارة لتحديد الاحتياجات التشغيلية ومتابعة تنفيذها.
- إعداد تحديثات دورية للمسؤول المباشر حول حالة المشتريات والمخزون والأصول والاحتياجات التشغيلية.
- الإبلاغ عن أي تأخير أو نقص في المستلزمات أو مشكلات في الخدمات أو الموردين قد تؤثر على تنفيذ الأنشطة.
- المساهمة في إعداد تقارير العمليات الدورية وتوفير البيانات والوثائق اللازمة للمراجعة الداخلية أو متطلبات الجهات المانحة.
- الالتزام بسياسات وإجراءات المنظمة المتعلقة بالمشتريات واللوجستيات وإدارة الأصول والسلامة والأمن.
- الحفاظ على سرية المعلومات والوثائق التشغيلية والمالية، والتعامل مع جميع السجلات بمهنية ومسؤولية.
- تنفيذ أي مهام إدارية أو تشغيلية أخرى ذات صلة بطبيعة الوظيفة، ضمن نطاق الصلاحيات وتوجيهات المسؤول المباشر.

### المؤهلات والخبرات المطلوبة

- شهادة جامعية أو معهد متوسط في إدارة الأعمال، أو الإدارة اللوجستية، أو إدارة العمليات، أو المحاسبة، أو أي تخصص ذي صلة.
- خبرة عملية لا تقل عن سنة واحدة في مجال الإدارة أو اللوجستيات أو المشتريات أو الدعم التشغيلي، ويفضل ضمن المنظمات غير الحكومية أو منظمات المجتمع المدني.
- معرفة جيدة بإجراءات المشتريات، وجمع عروض الأسعار، وإدارة المخزون والأصول، وحفظ الوثائق التشغيلية.
- مهارات جيدة في استخدام برامج Microsoft Office، وخاصة Excel لإعداد جداول المتابعة وتنظيم البيانات.
- القدرة على تنظيم الوثائق والسجلات ومتابعة الطلبات والمشتريات بدقة.
- مهارات جيدة في التواصل والتنسيق والتعامل المهني مع الموردين ومقدمي الخدمات.
- القدرة على ترتيب الأولويات وإدارة عدة مهام في الوقت نفسه والالتزام بالمواعيد النهائية.
- القدرة على العمل ضمن فريق والتعاون مع الأقسام المختلفة.
- النزاهة والشفافية والالتزام بالسرية المهنية وتجنب تضارب المصالح.
- القدرة على العمل في بيئة ديناميكية والاستجابة للاحتياجات التشغيلية العاجلة.

### المهارات الإضافية المفضلة

- خبرة سابقة في إدارة العمليات أو المشتريات ضمن المشاريع الممولة من الجهات المانحة.
- معرفة بمتطلبات توثيق المشتريات وإجراءات التدقيق المالي والتشغيلي.
- خبرة في إعداد جداول مقارنة عروض الأسعار وسجلات المخزون والأصول.
- إجادة اللغة الإنجليزية، وخاصة في قراءة المراسلات والمواصفات والوثائق التشغيلية، تعتبر ميزة إضافية.

### الراتب ومكان العمل

- **الراتب الشهري: 535 دولاراً أمريكياً.**
- مكان العمل: مكتب MRD في دمشق، سوريا.
- نوع العقد والمدة: يُحددان وفق احتياجات المشروع وإجراءات التوظيف المعتمدة لدى المنظمة.

### تكافؤ الفرص

تلتزم ماري للبحوث والتنمية (MRD) بمبادئ تكافؤ الفرص وعدم التمييز، وتشجع جميع المرشحين المؤهلين على التقدم للوظيفة. كما تتوقع من جميع الموظفين الالتزام بمدونة السلوك والسياسات الداخلية للمنظمة ومبادئ النزاهة والمساءلة والاحترام المهني.

jobs.title: Legal Assistant (Damascus) مساعد قانوني
jobs.description:
**About Mari Research and Development (MRD):**
Mari Research and Development (MRD) is a registered non-profit organization based in Syria and Iraq, dedicated to peacebuilding, civil dialogue, protection, psychosocial support, legal aid, livelihoods, and community resilience. MRD works closely with local communities and international partners to empower vulnerable populations, including survivors of detention and torture, families of the missing, women, and youth.

**Job Title:** Legal Assistant
**Location:** Damascus
**Reports to:** Legal Field Advisor

## **Position Purpose**

The Legal Assistant delivers direct legal information, counseling, and referrals to beneficiaries, with a focus on access to civil documentation and legal rights.

## **Key Responsibilities**

- Conduct client intake and provide legal information.
- Support applications for civil documentation and follow-up.
- Deliver community awareness sessions on legal rights.
- Maintain confidential case files and records.
- Refer cases to external actors as appropriate.

## **Qualifications**

- University degree in Law or related field.
- Practicing lawyer with at least 5 years of experience.
- Knowledge of civil documentation processes in Syria.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
- Arabic required.

jobs.title: Finance Manager RDC
jobs.description:
**Lieu : Goma ou Kinshasa au choix / République Démocratique du Congo**
**Date souhaitée de démarrage : début janvier 2027**
**Durée de contrat : 24 mois**

Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI) est une association de solidarité internationale indépendante et impartiale, qui intervient dans les situations de pauvreté et d’exclusion, de conflits et de catastrophes. Œuvrant aux côtés des personnes handicapées et vulnérabilisées, elle agit et témoigne pour répondre à leurs besoins essentiels et améliorer leurs conditions de vie. Elle s’engage à promouvoir le respect de leur dignité et de leurs droits fondamentaux.

Depuis sa création en 1982, HI a mis en place des programmes de développement dans plus de 55 pays et intervient dans de nombreuses situations d’urgence. Aujourd'hui, nous avons un budget d'environ 200 millions d'euros, avec 4000 employés dans le monde.

Chez Handicap International, nous croyons fermement en l'importance de l'inclusion et de la diversité au sein de notre structure. C'est pourquoi nous sommes engagés dans une politique handicap afin de favoriser l'accueil et l'intégration de personnes en situation de handicap.

Merci d’indiquer si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement particulier, y compris pour participer aux 1ers entretiens. Retrouvez plus d’informations sur l’association : .

## **CONTEXTE**

HI intervient en RDC depuis 1995 et met aujourd’hui en œuvre un portefeuille diversifié de projets humanitaires et de développement, avec une présence importante à Kinshasa et dans l’Est du pays.

À Kinshasa et dans l’Ouest, le programme intervient notamment dans le renforcement du système de santé, la réadaptation, la santé maternelle et infantile, le Nurturing Care et l’inclusion, avec le lancement à partir de 2027 d’un important programme pluriannuel financé par la coopération belge.

Dans l’Est, HI est présent à Goma/Mweso, Beni et Uvira, avec des interventions au Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu et en Ituri. Le portefeuille couvre notamment la réadaptation, la santé mentale et le soutien psychosocial, la protection, l’inclusion humanitaire, la réponse aux urgences et aux épidémies ainsi que l’éducation aux risques liés aux engins explosifs.

À travers Atlas Logistique, HI développe également d’importantes activités de services logistiques mutualisés : stockage, transport, chaîne du froid et appui aux acteurs humanitaires.

Le programme évolue dans un contexte sécuritaire, administratif et opérationnel particulièrement complexe, marqué par le conflit dans l’Est, les déplacements de population, les contraintes d’accès et la nécessité de pouvoir rapidement adapter et déployer les opérations.

## **VOTRE MISSION**

**Le/la Finance Manager est responsable de l’animation des équipes financières, du respect des standards de l’organisation et des règles locales dans le domaine financier, de la stratégie et du pilotage financier, et enfin de la gestion financière opérationnelle sur son périmètre.**

**Evolution du Volume Financier**

Le programme RDC a connu une croissance et une diversification importantes de son portefeuille au cours des dernières années, avec plusieurs financements humanitaires et de développement de volumes significatifs.

Les équipes sont réparties entre Kinshasa et plusieurs bases .

Cette organisation multi-bases implique une gestion financière fortement décentralisée, tout en nécessitant un pilotage, une consolidation et des mécanismes de contrôle robustes au niveau national.

Le Finance Manager RDC assure le pilotage global de la fonction Finance et la consolidation financière du programme.

**Bailleurs et partenaires externes principaux**

Le portefeuille du programme repose sur une diversité de bailleurs institutionnels.

HI intervient régulièrement au sein de consortiums et en partenariat avec des ONG internationales et nationales, ce qui implique une gestion importante des conventions de partenariat, du suivi financier des partenaires et des obligations de reporting auprès des leads et bailleurs.

## **SPECIFICITES DU POSTE**

Le poste peut être basé à Kinshasa ou Goma, avec des déplacements réguliers entre les différentes bases du programme et ponctuellement dans les zones d’intervention.

À Kinshasa, le poste est ouvert en famille/couple.

À Goma, le poste est non accompagné (sans famille/couple).

## Exigences

Vos compétences pour réussir :

- Expérience confirmée en management financier au sein d’un programme complexe, multi-bases et multi-bailleurs.
- Forte capacité de pilotage financier stratégique : analyse financière, anticipation des risques et formulation de recommandations à la Direction Programme
- Expérience avérée dans la structuration et le renforcement d’un département Finance, avec une capacité à clarifier les rôles, déléguer et renforcer les mécanismes de pilotage et de contrôle.
- Forte capacité de renforcement des compétences : coaching, accompagnement des managers et équipes Finance, transfert de compétences et développement de leur autonomie.
- Leadership collaboratif, avec une forte capacité d’écoute, de dialogue et de remise en question, permettant de comprendre les contraintes des différentes équipes et de rechercher des solutions collectivement.
- Bonne gestion de la pression et des priorités, avec la capacité à maintenir une prise de décision structurée dans les périodes de forte charge, de clôture, d’audit ou d’urgence opérationnelle.
- Capacité à manager des équipes à distance et à construire une organisation efficace entre le niveau national, les responsables Finance de zone et les équipes des bases.
- Maîtrise professionnelle du français et de l'anglais

## Avantages

Chez HI, les conditions de départ sont à la hauteur de votre engagement et adaptées au contexte de votre mission. Une attention particulière est portée aux questions de santé et à votre situation personnelle :

- **Contrat International de 24 mois**
- **Prise de poste début janvier 2027**
- Le contrat international permet une couverture sociale adaptée aux besoins de chacun :
- Assurance chômage prélevée uniquement pour les ressortissants de l’UE
- Assurance retraite
- Couverture santé, rapatriement, prévoyance prises en charge par HI et par l’employé
- **Salaire** : à partir de 2 757€ brut/mois selon expérience professionnelle
- **Perdiem** :
- Goma : 684€ net/ mois – versé en monnaie locale sur le terrain
- Kinshasa : 1 150€ net/mois – versé en monnaie locale sur le terrain
- **Hardship :**
- Goma : 500€ net/ mois
- Kinshasa 0 € net/mois
- **Poste :**
- Goma : **non accompagné**
- Kinshasa : famille
- **Congés payés** : 25 jours par an ;
- **R&R** : 5 jours tous les 8 semaines

Prise en charge des frais de transport, de visas et de transport de vos effets personnels (dès 12 mois)

- A partir de 12 mois de mission une allocation enfant de 100 € versée à partir de 2 enfants à charge

jobs.title: Request for Proposal WAZZII Platform Feature Development and Service Design
jobs.description:
## **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media and technology girls choose, use and trust. Across Africa and South Asia, our youth brands — including Wazzii and Tuki in Kenya, Big Sis in South Africa, Chhaa Jaa and Bol Behen in India, and Yegna in Ethiopia — reach millions of adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) with content and digital tools that support the decisions shaping their lives, from sexual and reproductive health (SRH) to wellbeing, education and work. Our approach is girl-centred by design: girls co-create our products, our evidence teams measure what actually changes for them, and our safeguarding architecture treats their safety as a design constraint, never an afterthought.

Girl Effect has spent a decade building conversational products for young people, and several years deliberately and publicly charting what responsible technology for girls looks like.

## **What is WAZZII**

Today. WAZZII is Girl Effect’s WhatsApp-based chatbot for AGYW in Kenya, offering confidential SRH information, signposting and human help desk support in English and Sheng. It draws on a decade-deep corpus of more than 50 million questions young people have asked our chatbots — one of the richest datasets in existence on what girls actually want to know. Human help desk operators, working on the RapidPro help desk, remain central to the experience.

The next evolution of its design. Over the coming two years, WAZZII will evolve from a conversational companion into a trusted service-navigation platform: girls will move from a conversation to finding a real, vetted, youth-friendly provider nearby; prepare for the visit with confidence; access services using codes issued in the chat; and be supported to continue afterwards — with verified loops confirming a girl was actually served. Tens of thousands of girls are expected to use these capabilities directly, and the learning will shape Girl Effect’s chatbot portfolio globally. This tender selects the partner for the service design and platform engineering behind that evolution.

## **The Girl Effect Tech Stack**

Girl Effect has built an ecosystem of technologies which underpin its user-facing solutions. By using the existing tech stack, we ensure our in-country teams can focus their time and budget on delivering impact. The stack consists of:

- RapidPro: Low-code chatbot building platform through which we connect to instant messaging platforms, build out user engagement pathways including informational content, quizzes and surveys, and connect to other tools via API. Hosted on partner org’s multi-tenant AWS infrastructure

**Wagtail: Python-based CMS, used to build our user-facing websites. Connects to RapidPro via API to provide structured content such as service directories. Self-hosted on AWSIntelligence Module: GE’s self-built tool to manage connectivity with LLMs. Connects via API to RapidPro to build user-facing GenAI workflows.Self-hosted on AzureAPIs: Manage connections between the different tools in the system. Self-hosted on AWS**

We are open to suggestions of changes that could be made to the stack which would provide tangible benefits to our programmatic output, whether through improved functionality or cost efficiencies.

**Objective**

To appoint an experienced technology and service-design partner to design, build, test, deploy and support the next phase of WAZZII as a safe, accessible and measurable service-navigation platform for adolescent girls and young women in Kenya.

The engagement will follow a **service-design-led approach**, with user needs, safeguarding requirements and tested service journeys informing the final technical build.

## **What You will do**

Girl Effect is seeking an experienced partner to deliver WAZZII’s next evolution through a human-centred design approach: service design leads, and engineering follows. The partner’s senior service designer works with girls, operators and the Girl Effect team to understand needs, shape journeys and define the feature requirements — and the build then delivers against those requirements. The partner will build on WAZZII’s existing stack and be onboarded to current systems and documentation at inception. AI functionality is not in scope of this TOR.

Service design. Key activities include:

- Co-creation workshops with young people — multiple rounds across the engagement, designed and facilitated with Girl Effect — shaping the finder, the redemption moment, visit preparation and continuation support around how girls actually live, move and pay
- Design sprints with the Girl Effect team — per feature cluster, turning co-creation insight and programme requirements into tested, buildable designs before engineering begins
- End-to-end journey mapping — from first conversation to provider visit to continuation, kept current as the build evolves
- Escalation flow design — with Girl Effect’s safeguarding team, so every journey has a safe, human path out
- Service blueprint for the redemption moment — the seconds at the pharmacy counter where the whole service succeeds or fails for a girl
- Feature requirements definition — workflow maps and functional requirement packs per feature cluster — the outputs that define what gets built, for this engagement and for future platform capabilities
- Design QA — on every girl-facing feature, including accessibility and low-bandwidth performance

Feature development. Many of the features likely to be built as part of these requirements include, but are not limited to:

- Code redemption system — girls receive single-use codes in the chat that unlock services at participating pharmacies and clinics. The partner builds the full lifecycle: secure code generation, delivery in-chat, validation at the counter, and reconciliation — with anti-fraud controls (single-use enforcement, expiry, anomaly detection) and reliable performance on low-end devices and patchy connectivity
- Provider dashboard — a simple web dashboard for participating pharmacies and clinics: validate a girl’s code in seconds at the counter, track stock of supported products, view redemption history and reconciliation status, and access basic reporting. Designed for busy counter staff with minimal training, on the devices providers actually have
- Geolocation & provider finder — a girl shares her area in the chat and receives the nearest vetted youth-friendly providers — services offered, opening hours, indicative pricing, and simple directions. Provider records are managed by Girl Effect through an admin interface; the directory exposes open APIs so future partner services can be surfaced
- Structured chat journeys — new structured flows in Sheng and English — method exploration, visit preparation, follow-up scheduling — authored by Girl Effect, implemented and instrumented by the partner so every journey step is measurable
- Cost comparison tool — a lightweight in-chat calculator letting girls compare the costs of methods and services across provider types, supporting informed choice before a visit
- Help desk enhancements — workflow improvements on the existing RapidPro help desk — routing, tagging, queue management and reporting for operators.
- Code generation tools — bulk and offline code generation for on-ground activations and community events, with attribution so redemptions can be traced back to the channel that issued them
- Quality, security & operations — QA throughout; security audit and penetration test before any girl-facing launch; hosting and infrastructure; maintenance and bug-fix support through the engagement

## **Scope Confirmation and Change Control**

The feature descriptions above represent the anticipated scope. The final feature requirements will be confirmed through the inception and service-design stages.

To control scope and cost:

- Each feature cluster must have an approved requirements pack and acceptance criteria before development begins.
- No material change to the agreed scope, cost or timeline may proceed without written approval from Girl Effect.
- Proposed changes must document the rationale, impact on costs, timeline, security, dependencies and other deliverables.
- Work completed without the required written approval may not be eligible for payment.
- Girl Effect may prioritise, defer or remove features based on user evidence, technical feasibility, available budget or programme priorities.
- Girl Effect may commission optional or future features through separately approved work orders or contract amendments.

## **Deliverables**

**Service design**

Deliverable Description

Co-creation workshop rounds A minimum of three rounds with young people across the engagement, each with documented outputs feeding directly into design decisions

Design sprint outputs Sprint per feature cluster with the Girl Effect team: tested prototypes, decisions log, and buildable specifications

Journey maps End-to-end maps maintained across the engagement

Escalation flow designs Safeguarding-approved designs for every journey

Redemption service blueprint Counter-moment blueprint validated with providers and girls

Feature requirements packs Workflow maps and functional requirements defining each feature cluster before build

Design QA reports Per release, covering accessibility and low-bandwidth performance

**Development features**

*The final feature set is confirmed through the service design process; the deliverables below reflect the features currently anticipated.*

Deliverable Description

Code redemption system live End-to-end generation, delivery, validation and reconciliation in production, with anti-fraud controls and monitoring

Provider dashboard live Deployed to participating facilities with onboarding materials and admin tooling

Provider finder live Geo-located directory in the chat experience, with the admin interface and open APIs documented

Structured chat journeys live Agreed RapidPro Flow journeys set implemented, instrumented and released

Cost comparison tool live In-chat calculator released

Help desk enhancements live RapidPro workflow improvements deployed to the operator team

Code generation tools live Bulk/offline generation with channel attribution, in the hands of the on- ground team

Security & launch readiness Security audit and penetration test passed; QA reports; release briefs to operators and content team per deployment

Operations Hosting live; maintenance and bug-fix support; documentation and handover materials

## **Technical and Operational Requirements**

The proposed solution should:

- Be secure, scalable, maintainable and suitable for future expansion.
- Work effectively on low-end devices and under limited connectivity conditions.
- Apply privacy-by-design and data-minimisation principles.
- Use documented and supportable technologies.
- Integrate with Girl Effect’s approved systems and interfaces.
- Provide appropriate audit logs, access controls and administrative permissions.
- Support secure backup, restoration and business-continuity arrangements.
- Avoid unnecessary collection or exposure of personal and sensitive information.
- Meet agreed accessibility and usability standards.
- Provide clear operational monitoring and error reporting.
- Avoid unreasonable dependency on proprietary tools or a single supplier.

Bidders must identify all third-party software, services, licences and recurring costs required for the proposed solution.

## **Project Management and Working Arrangements**

The engagement will be managed by Girl Effect’s Product and Delivery Lead.

The successful partner will:

- Work through two-week delivery sprints.
- Use Girl Effect’s agreed Jira or programme management environment.
- Participate in weekly delivery meetings.
- Maintain an updated delivery plan, risk register, issues log and decisions log.
- Provide concise sprint and monthly progress reports.
- Demonstrate completed work at agreed sprint reviews.
- Escalate material delays, dependencies, security risks and safeguarding concerns promptly.
- Ensure that each production release is supported by appropriate technical and operational documentation.

## **Who You Are**

- Relevant experience delivering large-scale digital platforms, chatbot services, dashboards, system integrations or comparable solutions.
- Strong service design and participatory design capability.
- Experience designing digital services for young people or users in sensitive contexts.
- Experience with WhatsApp, RapidPro or comparable conversational platforms.
- Strong software engineering, quality assurance, security and deployment practices.
- Ability to integrate with and improve an existing technology environment.
- Capacity to provide implementation and post-launch support in Kenya.
- Appropriate safeguarding, data-protection and information-security controls.
- Financial and operational capacity to deliver the assignment.

## **Proposal Submission Requirements**

Bidders must submit separate technical and financial proposals (Max 10 pages).

### **Technical Proposal**

The technical proposal should include:

- Understanding of the assignment and proposed solution.
- Service-design and participatory-research approach.
- Proposed technical architecture and integration approach.
- Delivery methodology, workplan, sprint structure and key milestones.
- Quality-assurance, testing and release-management approach.
- Safeguarding, data-protection and security approach.
- Hosting, maintenance and support model.
- Proposed project team, roles, CVs and level of effort.
- Relevant organisational experience and at least three comparable assignments.
- At least three client references.
- Key assumptions, dependencies, risks and exclusions

### **Financial Proposal**

The financial proposal must be submitted in **USD** and include:

- A fixed price by deliverable and implementation phase.
- Personnel roles, professional rates and level of effort.
- Hosting, infrastructure and recurring costs.
- Third-party licence and service costs.
- Maintenance and support costs.
- Applicable taxes shown separately.
- Proposed reimbursable expenses shown separately.
- Optional feature or enhancement rates, where relevant.
- Clear assumptions, dependencies, exclusions and pricing conditions.

## **Evaluation**

Proposals will be evaluated in the following order:

- Pre-screening;
- Technical evaluation;
- Pitch, demonstration or clarification stage, where required; and
- Financial evaluation.

Evaluation Criterion

- Relevant organisational experience and comparable platform delivery 15%
- Service-design and participatory-design capability 15%
- Quality and feasibility of the technical approach 20%
- Security, data protection, safeguarding and quality assurance 10%
- Proposed team, delivery plan and Kenya support model 10%

Technical Total 70%

- Financial proposal and overall value for money 30%

Total 100%

Girl Effect may:

- Request written clarifications;
- Invite shortlisted bidders to a pitch or technical demonstration;
- Conduct reference checks and due diligence;
- Request a best-and-final offer; or
- Negotiate the final scope, work plan and commercial proposal with the preferred bidder.

The lowest-priced proposal will not necessarily be selected.

## **Project Timelines**

- Terms of reference published: **29th October 2026**
- Questions/Clarification Deadline: **4th November 2026**
- Consolidated FAQ shared with all prospective bidders: **6th November 2026**
- Deadline for proposal submission: **13th November 2026**
- Inception: onboarding to existing stack; interfaces defined; design sprint 1 and co-creation round 1- Months 1–2 post-contract
- Build releases (redemption system, dashboard, finder first)- Months 2–6
- Co-creation rounds 2–3; design sprints per feature cluster- Months 2–5
- Security audit and launch readiness-Month 6
- Operations, maintenance and iteration- Month 7 onward

*Timings are indicative and will be finalised at contracting; deliverable acceptance, not elapsed time, triggers payment milestones.*

### **Clarification Process**

Bidders may submit clarification questions to suppliers@girleffect.org by **4th November 2026**

The email subject should state:

**Clarification Question – WAZZII Platform Tender**

To ensure a fair and transparent open-tender process:

- Girl Effect will not provide substantive answers to all bidders.
- All relevant questions and responses will be compiled into a consolidated FAQ.
- The FAQ will not identify the organisation that submitted each question.
- The consolidated FAQ will be shared with all prospective bidders through the same publication or communication channels used for the RFP.
- Bidders are responsible for reviewing the FAQ and any formal tender updates before submitting their proposals.
- Verbal information or guidance will not amend the RFP unless confirmed by Girl Effect in writing.

Girl Effect may decline to answer questions received after the clarification deadline.

### **General and Commercial Terms**

- **Contracting:** The successful bidder will sign Girl Effect’s standard services agreement, statement of work and applicable data-processing and information-security documentation.
- **Payment**: Payments will be linked to the satisfactory completion and written acceptance of agreed deliverables. Girl Effect may withhold payment for incomplete, defective or unapproved work.
- **Pricing: T**he agreed implementation pricing will remain fixed unless a change is approved through the formal written change-control process.
- **Expenses:** Only reasonable expenses approved in writing in advance will be reimbursable. Reimbursable expenses must be supported by appropriate documentation.
- **Intellectual Property:** Girl Effect will own all foreground intellectual property, deliverables, source code, configurations, designs and documentation created specifically under the engagement, subject to agreed treatment of pre-existing tools and third-party materials.
- **Source Code and Access:** The partner must maintain current source code and documentation in repositories approved by Girl Effect and provide Girl Effect with appropriate administrative access throughout the engagement.
- **Open-Source and Third-Party Components:** All open-source and third-party components must be disclosed, appropriately licensed, maintained and approved for use.
- **Confidentiality and Data Protection:** The partner must protect Girl Effect’s confidential information and personal data and comply with applicable data-protection requirements.
- **Safeguarding and Conduct:** Appointment is subject to satisfactory due diligence, reference, safeguarding, information-security and compliance checks. The successful bidder must comply with Girl Effect’s code of conduct, safeguarding and anti-fraud requirements.
- **Subcontracting:** No material part of the assignment may be subcontracted without Girl Effect’s prior written approval. The lead bidder remains responsible for all subcontracted work.
- **Warranties and Defects:** Bidders should propose a warranty period during which defects in accepted deliverables will be corrected at no additional cost.
- **Conflicts of Interest:** Bidders must disclose any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest.
- **Tender Costs:** Girl Effect will not reimburse costs incurred in preparing or submitting a proposal or participating in clarification, pitch or negotiation stages.
- **Right to Award:** Girl Effect may clarify, negotiate, amend, suspend or cancel the procurement; reject any or all proposals; award the full or partial scope; award in phases; or make no award.
- **No Commitment:** Publication of this RFP does not constitute a commitment to enter into a contract.
- **Equal Opportunity:** Girl Effect welcomes submissions from qualified organisations that meet the stated regulatory, technical and service requirements.
- **Proposal Validity:** Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

jobs.title: MEAL Manager (National Position) -Re Advertised
jobs.description:
Near East Foundation (NEF)

**Title:** Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning Manager (National Position)

**Reports to:** Country Director

**Location:** Damascus, Syria

**Travel:** Up to 25% within Syria

**The Near East Foundation (NEF)** is seeking candidates for a **MEAL**[**\[1\]**](https://reliefweb.int/#_msocom_1) **Manager** to be based in Damascus, Syria. NEF is a non-profit international development organization that has supported livelihoods recovery and community-based economic development in the Middle East, Africa, and Caucasus since 1915. NEF draws on local teams, experience, and partnerships in these regions to create community-led solutions to reduce poverty, create economic opportunity, and empower conflict and crisis-affected groups to improve their outlook and wellbeing. Working through a network of country offices and local partners, NEF has operations in ten countries: Armenia, Lebanon, Iraq, Mali, Morocco, Palestine, Sudan, South Sudan, and Syria. HQ offices are based between Syracuse, NY, Washington, DC, London, UK, and Brussels, Belgium. Our programs are organized around three pillars: Inclusive Economic Development, Climate-resilient Development, and Stabilization and Peacebuilding.

**Position Description**

The MEAL Manager is a member of the NEF Syria team, reporting to the Syria Director. The purpose of the MEAL Manager is to ensure all MEAL responsibilities are performed to the highest standards and according to donor and NEF guidelines. The post-holder also assumes communication and visibility responsibilities for the Syria operation.

**Responsibilities**

- **Proposal Development and MEAL Planning:**
- Participate in the development of project proposals, including designing logframes, selecting and defining indicators, and developing MEAL plans.
- Design and update the project logframes and MEAL plans in collaboration with relevant team members.
- **MEAL System Implementation and Oversight:**
- Ensure an appropriate MEAL system is in place, functioning effectively, and periodically reviewed to adapt to changing program and operating contexts.
- Manage and report on the implementation of project MEAL plans, including regular progress tracking and reporting to the Director.
- Coordinate closely with program team counterparts and ensure data is available in a timely and easily digestible format (e.g. dashboard creation) to facilitate data-informed and robust adaptive management processes
- **Data Management and Analysis:**
- Operationalize NEF MEAL procedures and tools, including data collection, storage, analysis, and reporting (using KOBO, and other relevant tools).
- Ensure the quality and accuracy of data collected and stored, overseeing data cleaning and validation, and conducting statistical analysis using tools such as SPSS and Excel.
- Ensure appropriate data protection, confidentiality, access, and secure storage practices are applied across MEAL systems and datasets.
- Analyze performance against indicators and targets, flag significant deviations, and work with program teams to identify appropriate corrective or adaptive actions.
- Conduct qualitative and quantitative data analysis to provide comprehensive insights into project performance.
- Facilitate various types of assessments, including impact, outcome, and process evaluations, in coordination with the HQ MEAL team.
- **Data Quality Assurance:**
- Lead and oversee internal Data Quality Assessments (DQAs), with support from the Data Analyst and relevant program teams, to ensure the validity, reliability, completeness, and consistency of program data. This includes:
1. Conducting ongoing analysis of MEAL databases or trackers to identify data quality strengths, gaps, and inconsistencies.
2. Supporting the development, implementation, and supervision of procedures to improve data quality and reporting.
3. Ensuring identified data quality issues are documented, addressed, and followed up with relevant program and MEAL staff.
4. Collecting and verifying, where applicable, supportive documentation to ensure consistency and accuracy in data management.
- **Training and Capacity Building:**
- Train, support, and supervise MEAL staff, volunteers, and field agents on data collection, surveys, and project monitoring.
- Where relevant, conduct capacity-building training for partner organizations and team members, including institutional needs assessments and socio-economic assessments.
- **Accountability and Feedback Mechanisms:**
- Ensure accountability and feedback mechanisms are applied consistently across all projects, locations, and partners, including appropriate recording, referral, response, follow-up, and closure of feedback and complaints, in line with ethical, confidentiality, and transparency standards.
- **Learning and Documentation:**
- Facilitate periodic learning sessions, reflection workshops or post-action reviews with project teams to identify lessons learned and best practices.
- Contribute to project learning and adaptive management by documenting and sharing findings, lessons learned, learning papers, case studies, and beneficiary profiles.
- Develop and disseminate communication and visibility materials (e.g., project overviews, fact sheets).
- **Evaluation and Reporting:**
- Facilitate mid-term, final, and other ad hoc evaluations in coordination with the HQ MEAL team and regional office.
- Contribute to and lead on projects' narrative reporting requirements, ensuring quality, data accuracy, and analysis.
- Review and finalize MEAL reports (e.g., semiannual, endline) and provide feedback on project strategies to enhance performance and sustainability.
- **Collaboration and Coordination:**
- Participate in monthly country coordination calls organized by HQ-based Program Officers.
- Collaborate with the broader Syria team to ensure alignment on data collection, and MEAL system implementation.
- Coordinate with the HQ MEAL Team backstop on technical guidance, MEAL standards and tools, organizational data requirements, learning priorities, and regional or global MEAL initiatives.
- Participate and contribute to donor meetings as required.
- **Field Monitoring and Support:**
- Conduct and oversee regular field monitoring follow-up activities, including focus group discussions with NEF beneficiaries.
- Support partner capacity assessments and build capacity where necessary.
- **Additional Duties:**
- Prepare field visits for NEF and external visitors, including photographers, journalists, or media if relevant.
- Perform other duties as required and requested by the direct line manager or technical supervisor.

**Position Criteria**

- Strategic thinking, including identification of MEAL system weaknesses and initiative to address problem(s);
- Excellent organizational skills, accuracy and attention to detail;
- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment and meet deadlines;
- Ability to operate both independently and collaboratively as required.

**Qualifications**

- Bachelor's degree in social sciences, humanities, quantitative/qualitative research methods, or a related field;
- At least Seven years of relevant professional experience in data collection, preferably with a national or international NGO, or other civil society organization;
- Fluent in written and spoken Arabic and English;
- Proficient in MS Office applications, particularly Word and Excel;
- Experience using digital data collection applications (e.g., KoboCollect, Akvo) is an asset;
- Plays an effective role within a team, able to communicate, develop, and maintain effective working relationships within a dynamic team environment.

jobs.title: Country WASH & Infrastructure Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Overall purpose of the role**

Under the direct supervision of the Head of Programme, the Country WASH & Infrastructure Coordinator provides technical leadership, strategic guidance and quality assurance for DRC Sudan's WASH and WASH infrastructure portfolio, covering emergency, nexus and long-term WASH, water resources, sanitation and hygiene, climate resilience and preparedness, and WASH in institutions. The role also supports programme development and positioning, working with DRC technical and area teams, global advisors, and partners and authorities.

**Responsibilities**

The post holder acts as DRC Sudan's national technical advisor for WASH and WASH infrastructure, working closely with Area Managers and technical teams to ensure timely, high-quality implementation. Area Managers retain operational management and delivery; the Coordinator sets technical standards, provides oversight and quality assurance, and supports planning, proposals and technical documents (e.g. designs, BoQs, tools, SoPs). To achieve the overall and specific position's objectives, the job holder's tasks and responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

***Technical Leadership, Strategy and Programme Quality***

- Provide technical leadership on WASH: develop and update the WASH strategy under the Sudan Country Strategy, and produce standards, guidance, tools and SoPs aligned with Sphere, national codes, Cluster guidance and DRC frameworks.
- Ensure coherent approaches across emergency, protracted-displacement and nexus/long-term WASH, moving from emergency response towards sustainable, climate-resilient services with sound O&M and local ownership.
- Integrate WASH with Protection, Shelter/Site Management, and Economic Recovery, including cholera response.
- Support field teams in needs identification and RNAs; conduct field visits (including Darfur) or remote follow-up where access is constrained, to quality-assure design, construction and implementation.

***Water, Sanitation, Hygiene and Community-Led Approaches***

- Water supply and resources: advise on hydrogeological and source assessments, groundwater and surface water options (e.g. boreholes, hafirs), solar systems, water quality and conflict-sensitive access, promoting IWRM.
- Sanitation: guide safe, inclusive sanitation across the service chain (household, communal, camp and institutional), including excreta management, market-based sanitation, solid waste and vector control.
- Hygiene and behaviour change: promote evidence-based hygiene promotion and social and behaviour change approaches, including menstrual health, adapted to context and informed by community feedback.
- Community-led WASH: promote community-led approaches (e.g. CLTS, WASH committees, community management of services, local service providers) for ownership, O&M and sustainability.
- WASH in schools and public institutions (incl. health facilities, IPC): standards, designs and sustainable management.

***Climate, Resilience, AA and Preparedness***

- Integrate climate risk, DRR, nature-based solutions and IWRM into WASH strategy and design, promoting climate-resilient infrastructure (e.g. solar, flood-proofing).
- Lead WASH preparedness and anticipatory action: contingency planning, early warning and trigger-based action for floods, drought and cholera, prepositioning of supplies and surge readiness, with the WASH Cluster and authorities.

***Infrastructure, Engineering Review and Procurement***

- Lead the technical review and clearance of WASH designs, drawings, BoQs, specifications and cost estimates (water, sanitation, schools and public institutions), ensuring feasibility, cost-effectiveness and compliance with standards.
- Guide tendering, contracting, supervision, quality control, handover and O&M, including rehabilitation of damaged systems.
- Support Area WASH Managers and Supply Chain in procurement and pipeline planning, including market-based approaches.

jobs.description:
**About CRS**

Catholic Relief Services (CRS) is the official international humanitarian agency of the Catholic community in the United States. CRS works in around 100 countries to *save, protect, and transform* lives, serving people in need regardless of race, religion, or nationality. Through trusted local partnerships, CRS delivers relief and development programs in emergency response, disaster risk reduction, health, agriculture, education, community savings, livelihoods, and peacebuilding.

CRS began working in the Philippines in 1945, making it the longest-running continuous CRS country program in the world. Today, CRS Philippines implements programs in emergency response and recovery, disaster risk reduction, climate resilience, livelihoods, and peace and development. With more than 70 staff across Manila, Cotabato City, Tagbilaran City, Iloilo City, Virac, and Malaybalay City, CRS works closely with church and civil society partners, government agencies, and other organizations to serve vulnerable communities across the country.

The **Innovative Climate Financing - Philippines Carbon Finance Pilot** is an 18-month initiative (April 2026 – September 2027) which seeks to assess and advance the readiness of indigenous peoples’ ancestral domains in Bukidnon and Davao del Norte for participation in high-integrity forest carbon markets while delivering biodiversity, livelihood, and governance co-benefits. It likewise aims to support overall investments readiness by ensuring robust technical requirements are complied with, particularly on establishing the baseline and baseline, and calculation of project removals in line with the industry’s standards. CRS works with the Philippine Eagle Foundation (PEF) as the local implementing partner, the IP organizations, government agencies, and local stakeholders, to support IP governance strengthening, forest restoration, agroforestry and livelihoods skills strengthening, FPIC processes, biodiversity assessments, land and carbon suitability assessments, safeguarding, and the development of investment-ready carbon project opportunities.

On the other hand, the Restoration through Science-based Execution and Established Biodiverse Registry Philippines (RESEEDPH) project is a five year initiative designed to restore degraded forest and agro biodiverse landscapes by combining science-based planning, community participation, and strengthened policy support. Operating in Catanduanes, Bohol, and North Cotabato, the project focuses on climate-adapted species selection, improved seed and nursery systems, and the development of evidence-based restoration models that enhance both ecological health and community livelihoods.

**Job Summary**

The Environmental and Social Safeguards (ESS) Officer supports the implementation, monitoring, documentation, and continuous improvement of the Environmental and Social Safeguards system of the Philippines Carbon Finance Pilot and the RESEED project. The position assists in ensuring compliance with applicable donor and/or investment requirements, CRS policies, national regulations, environmental and social safeguards frameworks, and relevant carbon finance investment standards. Working closely with the Senior ESS Officer and Senior Project Officer for Social Standards, the incumbent will help ensure that environmental and social risks are identified, managed, monitored, and documented throughout project implementation.

## Responsibilities

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

**1. Environmental and Social Safeguards Implementation**

- Support implementation of the project's Environmental and Social Safeguards Frameworks, management plans, protocols, and procedures.
- Assist in environmental and social screening of project activities and interventions.
- Support monitoring of environmental and social risks associated with project implementation.
- Ensure safeguard requirements are integrated into workplans, field activities, and partner implementation processes.
- Monitor compliance with approved safeguard mitigation measures and management plans.

**2. Risk Monitoring, Compliance, and Verification**

- Conduct routine field monitoring and verification visits to assess safeguard compliance.
- Assist in identifying environmental and social risks, issues, and emerging concerns
- Support preparation and updating of risk registers, safeguard trackers, and compliance monitoring tools.
- Follow up implementation of agreed corrective and preventive actions.
- Escalate significant risks and non-compliance issues to the Senior ESS Officer.

**3. Environmental Monitoring and Documentation**

- Support monitoring of environmental safeguards related to reforestation, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem restoration, forest protection, and natural resource management activities.
- Assist in documenting environmental impacts, mitigation measures, field observations, and compliance status.
- Maintain safeguard documentation, monitoring records, and evidence files.
- Coordinate with GIS and technical teams to support environmental monitoring and reporting.

**4. Accountability and Grievance Monitoring**

- Receive, document, track, and monitor safeguard-related concerns, complaints, and grievances.
- Maintain confidential records and databases related to grievances and safeguard issues.
- Support timely referral and resolution of cases in accordance with approved protocols.
- Generate regular summaries and analyses of safeguard-related grievances and trends.

**5. Stakeholder Engagement Support**

- Support community consultations, safeguard orientations, disclosure activities, and engagement processes.
- Document stakeholder consultations, meetings, and safeguard discussions.
- Assist in ensuring project participants understand safeguard commitments, grievance channels, and project responsibilities.
- Coordinate closely with the Senior Project Officer for Social Standards on FPIC, Indigenous Peoples engagement, and social safeguard activities.

**6. Reporting and Knowledge Management**

- Prepare regular safeguard monitoring reports, compliance updates, and field visit reports.
- Support consolidation of environmental and social safeguard data for donor and management reporting.
- Maintain safeguard records, databases, and document repositories.

**7. Partner Capacity Strengthening**

- Support training and coaching of project staff, partners, and community stakeholders on safeguard requirements.
- Assist in delivering orientations on environmental and social safeguards, grievance mechanisms, and risk management procedures.
- Monitor partner compliance and provide technical support as needed.

## Qualifications

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Forestry, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Planning, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Community Development, or a related field.
- Minimum of 3 years of relevant professional experience in environmental safeguards, social safeguards, environmental compliance, risk management, conservation, natural resource management, or related development programs.
- Experience formulating ESS Plan and supporting implementation for donor-funded projects is preferred.
- Experience conducting field monitoring, compliance verification, and stakeholder consultations is highly desirable.
- Experience working with indigenous people's communities and local partners is an advantage.
- Experience working in Mindanao, particularly Bukidnon and Davao del Norte, is highly desirable.
- Willingness and ability to travel regularly to field sites and remote communities.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- Familiarity with environmental and social safeguard principles and risk management approaches.
- Understanding of environmental compliance requirements and mitigation planning.
- Knowledge of grievance management and accountability mechanisms.
- Strong organizational and documentation skills.
- Ability to collect, organize, and analyze field monitoring information.
- Strong report-writing and communication skills.
- Ability to work effectively with diverse stakeholders and communities.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and digital monitoring tools.
- High attention to detail and commitment to accountability and compliance.

**Required Languages**:

- Excellent spoken and written English.
- Working knowledge of Bisaya is highly desirable.

**Travel**: Must be willing to travel up to 50% of the time to Malaybalay, Bukidnon and/or Talaingod, Davao del Norte.

**Key Working Relationships:** TBD

**Agency-wide Competencies (for all CRS Staff)**

These are rooted in the mission, values, and guiding principles of CRS and used by each staff member to fulfill his or her responsibilities and achieve the desired results.

- **Integrity**
- **Continuous Improvement & Innovation**
- **Builds Relationships**
- **Develops Talent**
- **Strategic Mindset**
- **Accountability & Stewardship**
