jobs.title: Environment & Energy Officer - Nakivale Refugee Settlement
jobs.description:
**About HEKS/EPER:**
HEKS/EPER (Swiss Church Aid) is a faith-based international development and humanitarian organization committed to justice, human dignity, and sustainable development. In Uganda and South Sudan, our work focuses on supporting marginalized communities and building resilience through a triple nexus approach that integrates humanitarian response, sustainable development, and peacebuilding. We promote a rights-based, participatory, and conflict-sensitive approach that upholds dignity, inclusion, and accountability to affected populations.

**Standard functions:**

The Environment & Energy Officer will lead the environmental restoration, natural resource management and clean energy components of the project Empowering Youth and Women through Inclusive Skills Development (EWISE) in Nakivale Refugee Settlement. The project aims to improve the self-reliance and inclusive economic participation of vulnerable youth and women in refugee and host communities while enhancing environmental restoration and reducing pressure on natural resources.

The Environment & Energy Officer will coordinate, implement and monitor project interventions on natural resources management, especially watershed management inputs, community and institutional woodlot management, and the integration of gender through Social and Behaviour Change Communication (SBCC) with focused targeting of youth and women. The Officer will also design community-led plastic waste collection and recycling hubs, and will ensure that environmental safeguards, climate adaptation and sustainable energy considerations are integrated across the project.

In addition, the Officer will provide technical support on environment, climate and energy across other projects of the country programme, dedicating approximately 10% of the position's time to technical guidance and promoting consistent application of environmental safeguards and scale-up of sustainable energy approaches across the country programme.

M**ain responsibilities:**

**1. Programme Strategy and Implementation**

- Ensure effective and efficient planning and implementation according to approved budgets, workplan and HEKS/EPER policies.
- Ensure the project adopts the humanitarian–development–peace nexus approach and aligns with the thematic areas of livelihoods, conflict transformation, climate adaptation, and protection.
- Conduct environmental, climate-risk and energy assessments to inform project targeting, design, and implementation and guide the design of interventions on natural resources management at the community and institutional level.
- Design interventions that promote sustainable energy solutions that complement woodlot restoration, such as fuel-efficient stoves, clean-cooking practices and woodlot-based fuelwood management plans, to reduce pressure on natural resources.
- Develop strategies and promote approaches that strengthen integration and inter-linkages of climate-smart agriculture, agroforestry, reforestation, sustainable land management, water conservation, soil and water protection, and biodiversity-friendly practices.
- Provide technical input to project proposals across the country programme, ensuring environment, climate and energy principles are integrated into context analyses, theories of change and results frameworks.

**2. Project Cycle Management (PCM)**

- Coordinate the targeting, selection and engagement of youth and women as change agents, using vulnerability, capacity and gender-inclusion criteria.
- Support the establishment and strengthening of woodlot management committees, including management plans, bylaws, benefit-sharing and conflict-resolution arrangements and gender-balanced leadership.
- Design and deliver specialized training for community members and institutions on woodlot restoration, including nursery management, planting, maintenance, protection, and sustainable harvesting, with integrated modules on gender equality, safeguarding, and conflict sensitivity.
- Conduct sensitization and awareness sessions in institutions on environmental protection, climate change and energy efficiency and strengthen the capacity of school Eco-clubs to mainstream environmental protection in schools.
- Support plastic waste collection and recycling, including establishing community-led recycling hubs and working with the MSD Officer to link collection groups to recyclers and green business opportunities.
- Conduct environmental and social safeguard screening of project sites and activities (including woodlots, nurseries and recycling hubs), develop and monitor mitigation measures, including safe waste handling.
- Work with the MEAL team to track log frame indicators (including tree survival, area restored and waste collected), conduct assessments, and document success stories, case studies and lessons learned; contribute to the internal mid-term and end-term reviews.
- Provide technical assistance and capacity building to schools and community structures on woodlot restoration, watershed management, environmental safeguards and sustainable energy.

**3. Donor Compliance, Reporting and Representation**

- Ensure compliance with donor contract, HEKS/EPER's Field Financial and Administrative Guidelines (FFAG), and national environmental regulations as applicable.
- Prepare high-quality narrative inputs for donor reports, programme briefs and case studies on woodlot restoration, tree survival, sustainable energy and plastic waste recycling, in consultation with the MEAL Officer and Grants and Acquisition Coordinator, ensuring donor visibility requirements are met.
- Represent HEKS/EPER in environment and energy coordination platforms at settlement and district level (OPM, UNHCR, Isingiro District Local Government, CRRF structures) and build partnerships with environment partners and institutions, especially schools and community structures.

**4. Budget Oversight and Financial Accountability**

- Develop project workplans, procurement plans and budget follow-ups (BFUs) to contribute to monthly forecasts and variance analysis. Review and approve procurement requests and expenditure plans within delegated thresholds.

**5. MEAL and Learning**

- Contribute to organisational learning on climate resilience, environmental restoration and energy access.

**6. Team Management and Capacity/Building**

- Ensure age, gender, disability, conflict sensitivity (Do No Harm) and environmental considerations are mainstreamed in all activities.
- Promote team cohesion and ensure staff, partners and trainers adhere to Do No Harm, Protection and HRBA principles and to HEKS/EPER's Gender and Diversity, PSEAH and child safeguarding policies.

**Any other task relevant to this role, assigned by the Supervisor.**

**Minimum requirements**

- Bachelor's degree in environmental science, Natural Resource Management, Forestry, Agroforestry, Climate Change, Renewable Energy, Environmental Engineering, Agriculture or a related field (a master's degree is an added advantage).
- Minimum of 3 years of relevant experience in environmental management, woodlot restoration/agroforestry, watershed management, climate adaptation, sustainable energy or natural resource management in humanitarian and/or development settings.
- Demonstrated experience in environmental and social safeguards, environmental risk assessment, community mobilisation, training and field monitoring.
- Knowledge of tree nursery and woodlot management, fuel-efficient stoves and clean-cooking technologies, solar energy, waste management, plastic recycling or circular-economy approaches.
- Experience working in refugee-hosting contexts and with refugee and host communities, women, youth and persons with disabilities.
- Strong report-writing, data collection and analysis skills; proficiency in MS Office and data tools (Excel, KoboToolbox, PowerPoint; GIS or Power BI preferred).
- Fluency in English; knowledge of Runyankole/Rukiga, Kinyarwanda, Kinyabwisha, Swahili or French is an added advantage.

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
INTERSOS is an independent humanitarian organisation that assists the victims of natural disasters, armed conflicts and exclusion. Its activities are based on the principles of solidarity, justice, human dignity, equality of rights and opportunities, respect for diversity and coexistence, paying special attention to the most vulnerable people.

## **Terms of reference**

**Job Title:** Project Manager

**Code**: SR-60-10330

**Duty station:** Mykolaiv with regular field visits to Kharkiv

**Starting date:** 01/12/2026

**Contract duration:** until 14/07/2028

**Reporting to:** Head of Programme

**Functional supervisor:**

**Supervision of:** CW/PSS Team Leaders, MAMs and GFFO staff

**Type of duty station:** Non-family duty station

## **General context of the project**

The war in Ukraine, which started on the 24th of February 2022, shows no signs of abating, and continues to drive increasing humanitarian needs across the country. Access concerns and humanitarian needs are particularly high in eastern Kharkivska, Sumska oblasts and southern Khersonska oblast, where the conflict is intensifying and critical infrastructure damage prevents civilians from accessing basic services.

Today INTERSOS is present in Odeska, Mykolaivska, Khersonska and Kharkivska Oblasts with bases of operations in Kharkiv, Kherson, Mykolaiv, Odesa, and Kyiv, allowing a wide geographical coverage. Moreover, INTERSOS is currently implementing Health, Protection, and NFIs interventions, funded by OCHA, AICS, GFFO and ECHO, encompassing several components: distribution of medicines to Regional Health Departments and shelters and equipment for clinics, Cash for Health, mobilisation of Protection mobile teams, establishment of community-based protection mechanisms, case management for CP/PWSN cases, psychosocial support (PSS), Protection Monitoring (PM), and distribution of material assistance to vulnerable individuals and households.

## **General purpose of the position**

The Project Manager ensures constant engagement by/with different support departments to ensure timely support to the project team.

The Project Manager is the budget holder for the whole GFFO-funded project grant/budget and supervises/monitors closely the financial planning, liquidity planning and budget utilisation/burn rate monitoring.

The financial/budget management is the final responsibility of the project manager for the specific project, and he/she must ensure that this goes together with a close log frame and work plan monitoring.

## **Main responsibilities and tasks**

**General:**

- Ensures the planning, implementation and monitoring/evaluation and sets targets as included in the project description. Flag significant deviations from the programme implementation plan and estimated expenditures; alert relevant staff.
- Guarantee efficient financial management as the main budget holder for the project in compliance with INTERSOS’ model and donor regulations.
- Team/HR management (staff and volunteers)
- Deliver quality project activity reporting, including findings in terms of impact/changes at the level of beneficiaries achieved through the project, compliant and consistent reporting per INTERSOS and donor requirements, in collaboration with the HQ Grants Unit
- Develop a clear understanding of the INTERSOS programme and country strategy among the project team – ensure also timely input/feedback by the team on strategic issues.
- Support the head of the programme in programme/project development.
- Ensure that programme delivery matches INTERSOS and donor technical minimum standards and seek technical section and MEAL department guidance and tools.
- Ensure a clear overview of actors and services in the area of intervention, permitting development and implementation of partnerships and referral pathways.
- Administrative and office support activities (agreements, amendments, signed reports, communications, etc.), ensuring the documentation cycle is up-to-date and that all departments’ requirements are aligned and addressed.

**Detailed responsibilities and tasks:**

- Ensure the full and timely implementation of the project proposal as approved, proactively respecting deadlines for reporting:
- Project kick-off and presentation/sharing of the project with teams
- Review and prepare a detailed activity plan with the team
- Verification of the targeting of beneficiaries

**Financial management and procurement:**

- Prepare, monitor and implement the financial and procurement plan.
- Prepare financial plan
- Approval of all purchases/contracting and budget line allocations
- Verify the bookkeeping entries in the INTERSOS accounting spreadsheets (JOURNAL): verify budget line allocations, budget expenditure status against actual delivery and the financial plan for the remainder of the project implementation period
- Ensure, for all purchases/contracting of goods/services/supplies, the correct INTERSOS procurement guidelines are applied and properly documented, in coordination with the Finance and Logistics departments.
- Verify the list of expenditures before finalising the interim and final financial reports
- Holds final responsibility for verification of all support documents’ completeness and correctness.

**People management:**

- Agree on and establish clear reporting and communication lines
- Team recruitment: liaises with the HR Department to secure up-to-date HR files.
- Permanent on-the-job coaching of teams to work on quality in delivery.
- Manage and evaluate the performance of the project staff.
- Conduct weekly and monthly meetings with the team to review the planning and discuss the main concerns to focus on for the upcoming period.
- Continuous/fast verification of data quality collected and received from field staff.
- Ensure teams respect INTERSOS rules and guidelines for the mission and adhere to INTERSOS’s Code of Conduct and Charter of Values.

**Monitoring & evaluation:**

- Ensure monitoring and verification for the targeting of beneficiaries.
- Applying a results-based management approach, monitor the project outcomes, in addition to the outputs and activities, including changes at the household and community level achieved through the project.
- Undertake (if the security situation allows) field visits to provide technical guidance and supervision to the team and to monitor the progress and quality of the different project activities.

**Reporting:**

- Ensure quality reporting on achievements through daily short briefings, monthly and weekly planning presented against weekly and monthly performance reports containing clear quantitative and qualitative information related to the activities.
- Secure regular reporting per team and compile, review and analyse reports on a monthly basis, to be reflected in INTERSOS’s Project Appraisal Tool.
- Prepare ad hoc progress reporting for the donor and official required interim and final project reports; prepare interim and final narrative reports for the donor in a timely and qualitative manner, looking into achievements against outcomes and outputs; and reflect lessons learnt clearly into recommendations for future programming.
- Holds final responsibility for all support documents (means of verification) and general project documents.
- Delivers regular communication products (including pictures) on the project to be used by the INTERSOS communication department in different outlets.

**Coordination and representation:**

- Support the Programme/Technical Coordinator(s) in attending cluster meetings and ensure timely reporting of highlights and relevant information for the intervention area.
- Participate in regular meetings with the donor representatives and partners and facilitate field visits by donor missions (when security allows), in coordination with the Programme Coordinator.
- Ensure systematic information and update sharing with the head of Programme
- Perform any other related duties as required.

## **Required profile and experience**

**Education**

- Advanced university degree in Social Sciences, Political Sciences, International Relations, Humanitarian and International Cooperation or a related field

**Professional Experience**

- Minimum 3 years of professional experience in the management of a humanitarian project/programme, including financial management and logistics responsibilities
- Minimum 1 year of experience in the implementation of multi-sector humanitarian programming

**Professional Requirements**

- Experience in complex emergency settings and insecure countries
- Administration, finance and budget management skills
- Essential computer literacy (word, excel and internet)
- Analytical thinking, analysis capacity and strategic program development skills
- Experience in establishing and maintaining collaborative relationships with donors and government counterparts, and with donors compliance and reporting

**Languages**

- Fluent knowledge of English (written and spoken)

**Personal requirements**

- Strong representation and negotiation skills
- Ability to ensure quick quality delivery in stressful environment
- Ability to adhere to deadlines and respect line management
- Strong interpersonal skills: communication, diplomatic skills and problem-solver
- Leadership, people management and development
- Organization and problem solving
- Commitment to INTERSOS principles

## **General conditions and benefits:**

- **Salary grid:** 11 - 3.430€ - 3.868€ monthly gross
- **Accommodation:** Shared Guesthouse
- **R&R:** INTERSOS staff required to work for extended periods at duty stations under hazardous, stressful and difficult conditions are granted a regular and mandatory period of Rest and Recuperation (R&R). This is due to protecting their health and well-being and ensuring optimal work performance upon the resumption of their duties, while, at the same time, preserving the operational readiness of the Organisation. R&R benefits are not financial compensation for the degree of hardship and insecurity of a duty station. Eligibility: staff members recruited as international field staff whose contract states one R&R Duty Station as the main Duty Station and whose contract duration is equal to or longer than 4 calendar months. R&R: 7 days of psycho-physical recovery every 8 weeks + 1000€ allowance.
- **Remuneration:** The monthly remuneration is defined, for each position, according to the standard salary grid and function grid, taking into account the experience of the selected candidate. It is communicated during the HR interview, or at any rate during the first stage of the selection process.
- **Transportation:** Round-trip flights for the humanitarian. For any mission lasting at least 9 months, an additional flight ticket to the Country of residence and return to the mission is covered by the Organisation for the humanitarian worker.
- **Medical insurance:** Injuries and death insurance; civil liability insurance, reimbursement for vaccines, medical certificate and PCR test for deployment; psychosocial support on request for the humanitarian worker.
- **Visa:** INTERSOS covers the costs and visa support for the humanitarian worker.
- **Annual Leave:** 2.5 days per month
- **Induction:** Online orientation course: each new staff member receives preparatory training before departure, adequate to provide the necessary information related to the structure of INTERSOS and the main decision-making processes and working tools, in order to facilitate entry into the Organisation.
- **Note 1:** INTERSOS applies a “Learning & Development Policy” which includes the possibility to receive capacitation and participate in internal and external training. Priority will be given to the staff working for INTERSOS for over two years.
- **Note 2:** The categorisation of Accompanied, RnR, and Unaccompanied Duty stations is subject to security criteria, access to health and education services, and is non-negotiable.

jobs.title: Market Systems Development Officer (MSD) - Nakivale Refugee Settlement
jobs.description:
**About HEKS/EPER:**
HEKS/EPER (Swiss Church Aid) is a faith-based international development and humanitarian organization committed to justice, human dignity, and sustainable development. In Uganda and South Sudan, our work focuses on supporting marginalized communities and building resilience through a triple nexus approach that integrates humanitarian response, sustainable development, and peacebuilding. We promote a rights-based, participatory, and conflict-sensitive approach that upholds dignity, inclusion, and accountability to affected populations.

**Standard functions:**

The Market Systems Development (MSD) Officer will lead the implementation of the skilling, enterprise development, private sector engagement and market linkage components of the project Empowering Youth and Women through Inclusive Skills Development (EWISE) in Nakivale Refugee Settlement. The project aims to improve the self-reliance and inclusive economic participation of vulnerable youth and women in refugee and host communities while enhancing environmental restoration. The MSD Officer will be responsible for the delivery of market-driven vocational and business skills training, apprenticeships and job placements with the private sector, business development services (BDS), market linkages, and financial inclusion. The MSD Officer works closely with the co-implementing partner, Department of Possibility (DoP), the Office of the Prime Minister (OPM), Refugee Welfare Councils, Isingiro District Local Government, UNHCR, the Directorate of Industrial Training (DIT) and private sector actors, and coordinates with the MEAL, Grants, Finance, and Procurement & Logistics teams to ensure quality, safeguarding, accountability, donor compliance and learning are integrated in the project management cycle. In addition, the MSD officer will provide technical support Market Systems Development (MSD) across other projects, dedicating approximately 10% of the position’s time to technical guidance, and promoting consistent application of the MSD approach across the country programme.

**Main responsibilities:**

**1. Programme Strategy and Implementation**

- Ensure effective and efficient planning and implementation according to approved budgets, workplan and HEKS/EPER policies
- Ensure that the project adopts the humanitarian-development Nexus approach and is aligned to the thematic areas of livelihoods, conflict transformation, climate adaptation, and protection
- Lead the labour market and skills demand assessment to ensure its integration into the project implementation cycle.
- Conduct private sector mapping and analysis of the systemic barriers to transition to work and dignified employment in Nakivale, Isingiro and Mbarara markets, including assessment of facilities and potential private sector actors.
- Ensure development of gender inclusive and appropriate Assessment and Training Packages (ATPs) and integration of a market systems approach to ensure interventions respond to market skill needs.
- Provide technical input to the development of project proposals across the country programme, ensuring that Market Systems Development (MSD) principles are appropriately integrated into context analyses, market assessments, theories of change, intervention strategies, and results frameworks.

**2. Project Cycle Management (PCM)**

- Coordinate beneficiary profiling and gender-inclusive selection of women and youth using vulnerability capacity assessment and market-alignment criteria.
- Oversee the development of inclusive training materials and curricula, with the private sector engaged in the design of the ATPs and support the profiling and engagement of trainers, instructors and facilitators.
- Ensure decentralized zonal-based technical, vocational and business skills training in the three zones of Nakivale through engagement of local artisans, including life skills, financial literacy, entrepreneurship and soft skills (FLESS), digital literacy and workplace readiness, with gender equality, safeguarding and conflict-sensitivity modules integrated.
- Coordinate beneficiary capacity and competency assessments, and certification of trainees with the Directorate of Industrial Training (DIT) to ensure work readiness.
- Support specialized training and market linkages of youth and women in community-based plastic-waste collection as a green business.
- Identify, verify and engage artisans, SMEs, cooperatives, employers and service providers in private sector for work-placements, apprenticeships and on-the-job training.
- In consultation with the Head of Programs, Head of Finance and Administration and Grants and Acquisition Coordinator, develop and ensure safe apprenticeships, job placements and private sector linkages through formal agreements and Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs).
- Conduct structured risk assessments of host enterprises (employer policies, feedback and response mechanisms, labour law compliance, safe pathways to self-reliance) to ensure the safeguarding of trainees in line with the Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS).
- Support the establishment and strengthening of micro and small businesses and green enterprises by managing the selection and distribution of toolkits, start-up kits and start-up capital.
- Design and deliver tailored Business Development Services, business incubation and mentorship to trainees.
- Develop a gender inclusive business tracker to track trainee graduation and enterprise growth and use it to tailor BDS to each business's stage and support a graduation pathway from aid dependency to dignified employment or self-employment.
- Facilitate contracts between groups and buyers, traders and local markets, trade fairs and exhibitions; link plastic-waste collection groups with recycling companies and aggregators to secure reliable market access and fair prices.
- Work with the MEAL team to track logframe indicators, conduct tracer studies, and document success stories, case studies and impact stories; contribute to the internal mid-term and end-term reviews.

**3. Donor Compliance, Reporting and Representation**

- Ensure compliance with donor contracts, HEKS/EPER’s Field Financial and Administrative Guidelines (FFAG), and national regulations as applicable to each thematic area.
- In consultation with the MEAL Officer and Grants and Acquisition Coordinator, ensure communications, visibility and advocacy efforts are aligned with programme goals.
- Prepare high-quality narrative inputs for donor reports, programme briefs and case studies on skilling, placements and enterprise development.
- Liaise with the MEAL Officer and lead the preparation of programme briefs, success stories, and case studies in compliance with HEKS/EPER and donor guidelines and requirements.
- Represent HEKS/EPER in livelihoods and economic inclusion of working groups and coordination platforms at settlement and district level (OPM, UNHCR, Isingiro District Local Government, CRRF structures) and build partnerships with the private sector.

**4. Budget Oversight and Financial Accountability**

- Develop project workplans, procurement plans and budget follow-ups (BFUs) to contribute to monthly forecasts and variance analysis.
- Review and approve procurement requests and expenditure plans within delegated thresholds.

**5. Partner Capacity Strengthening, MEAL and Learning**

- Provide technical assistance and capacity building to DoP on BDS, market systems approach, digitalisation, MEAL and safeguarding.

**6. Team Management and Capacity/Building**

- Provide day-to-day technical guidance to the project team and to DoP field staff working on skilling, business support and VSLAs; support performance appraisals of staff as delegated.
- Support HR processes such as the recruitment and onboarding of project staff and trainers.
- Ensure age, gender, disability, conflict sensitivity (Do No Harm) and environmental considerations are mainstreamed in all activities.
- Promote team cohesion and ensure staff, partners, trainers and private sector partners adhere to Do No Harm, Protection and HRBA principles and to HEKS/EPER's Gender and Adversity, PSEAH and child safeguarding policies.

**Any other task relevant to this role, assigned by the Supervisor.**

**Minimum requirements**

- Bachelor's degree in business administration, Economics, Agribusiness, Entrepreneurship, Development Studies, Vocational Education or a related field (a master's degree is an added advantage).
- Minimum 4 years of relevant experience in market systems development, skills development/TVET, youth and women economic empowerment, enterprise development or private sector engagement in humanitarian and/or development settings.
- Strong knowledge of project cycle management, budget control, donor reporting and community engagement.
- Demonstrated experience in business development services (BDS), business incubation, coaching and mentorship/apprenticeships, job placement and building partnerships or MoUs with private sector actors, artisans and SMEs.
- Experience working in refugee-hosting contexts and with refugee and host communities, women, youth and persons with disabilities.
- Good knowledge and understanding of DO NO HARM principles, safeguarding and the Human Rights Based Approach in development.
- Proficiency in MS Office and data tools (Excel, Power BI, KoboToolbox, etc.).
- Fluency in English; knowledge of Runyankole/Rukiga, Kinyarwanda, Kinyabwisha, Swahili or French is an added advantage.

jobs.title: Intersectional Procurement Manager basé à Bamako ou Ouagadougou - F/H
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

Cette position est redevable devant le Comité de pilotage intersectionnel des approvisionnements (ISSC), composé d’un représentant du département approvisionnement de chaque centre opérationnel participant aux activités d’achat mutualisées. Pour plus de détails sur la gouvernance, se référer au protocole d’accord de mutualisation (MOU)

**Contexte :**

**Mali :**

MSF est présent au Mali à travers quatre centres opérationnels (OCB, OCBA, WACA et OCP), chacun disposant d’un bureau de coordination à Bamako. Cette présence multi-OC fait du Mali un contexte particulièrement propice à la mutualisation des ressources et au renforcement de la collaboration intersectionnelle au niveau national.

Depuis 2021, les centres opérationnels concernés ont engagé une dynamique de travail conjoint, notamment à travers la mise en place de contrats intersectionnels pour certaines catégories d’achats à Bamako, telles que les produits d’hygiène, les fournitures de bureau, les denrées alimentaires et les services de transit. Toutefois, cette dynamique s’est développée dans un contexte où les ressources disponibles disposaient d’une expertise limitée en approvisionnement stratégique et portaient déjà une charge de travail importante.

Afin de combler cette lacune et de renforcer durablement la dynamique intersectionnelle, les centres opérationnels ont convenu de créer un poste de IPM en 2025, avec comme objectif de structurer et piloter la mise en place de contrats-cadres, tant au niveau de la coordination que des projets, en tenant compte des objectifs stratégiques à long terme ainsi que des risques économiques, sociaux et environnementaux.

C’est dans ce cadre qu’un IPM a été recruté en 2025 pour la mission Mali, permettant la contractualisation sur une base pluriannuelle de plusieurs familles d’achats stratégiques, notamment : le matériel électrique, les pièces détachées de véhicules, les produits alimentaires, le carburant, ainsi que le matériel et les consommables informatiques. Dans la continuité de cette démarche, d’autres catégories de biens et services devraient également faire l’objet de processus de contractualisation, notamment le transport, le transit et le dédouanement, les assurances, les audits externes, les agences de voyage et les pièces détachées de générateurs.
MSF constitue un acteur majeur du marché au Mali. La dynamique actuelle de coordination des achats et d’harmonisation de la gestion contractuelle a déjà permis d’améliorer l’efficience entre centres opérationnels pour plusieurs catégories critiques, tout en veillant à la disponibilité, à la qualité et à la conformité des biens et services. Il apparaît donc pertinent d’assurer la continuité de cette fonction, au bénéfice direct des opérations et des populations assistées par MSF au Mali.

**Burkina Faso**

MSF est présent au Burkina Faso à travers trois centres opérationnels (OCG, OCBA et OCP), avec huit projets actifs, chaque OC disposant d’un bureau de coordination à Ouagadougou. À ce jour, les activités d’approvisionnement sont menées de manière indépendante par chaque centre opérationnel, tout en s’appuyant sur un cadre d’échanges réguliers visant à partager les bonnes pratiques entre OCs.

Les familles d’articles couramment sollicitées sont variées et couvrent notamment les catégories suivantes : matériel électrique, carburant, consommables véhicules, équipements et consommables informatiques, eau et assainissement, produits alimentaires, pneumatiques et pièces détachées de véhicules.

En 2025, une étude de marché menée au Burkina Faso a mis en évidence plusieurs opportunités en matière d’approvisionnement stratégique, tant au niveau local que régional, en vue de mieux soutenir les opérations de MSF et d’en renforcer l’impact auprès des bénéficiaires.

Face à l’augmentation des besoins, et dans un contexte marqué par une expertise limitée des ressources existantes ainsi qu’une charge de travail déjà significative, la mission a identifié la nécessité de renforcer la fonction approvisionnement à travers la mutualisation de certaines activités et la mise à disposition d’une ressource expérimentée, dédiée à cette mission.
Dans cette perspective, le poste de IPM aura pour mandat de mettre en place la mutualisation des catégories d’achats les plus critiques, en cohérence avec les objectifs stratégiques de MSF et en intégrant les dimensions de risques économiques, sociaux et environnementaux. Le cahier des charges, défini par le Comité intersectionnel, portera sur des catégories à la fois stratégiques, critiques et récurrentes pour la mission.

MSF étant un acteur important du marché au Burkina Faso, la mise en place d’une dynamique de mutualisation des achats et de gestion harmonisée des contrats permettra d’améliorer l’efficience entre centres opérationnels, en particulier pour les catégories les plus critiques, tout en garantissant la disponibilité, la qualité et la compétitivité des biens et services.

**Objectif du poste :**

L’Intersectional Procurement Manager (IPM) définit et met en œuvre la stratégie d’achat afin de répondre aux besoins communs à l’ensemble des centres opérationnels (OC) présents dans le pays, conformément au protocole d’accord de mutualisation des achats signé entre les OC.

L’objectif de ce poste est de renforcer la disponibilité et la qualité des biens et services, d’améliorer la maîtrise des risques, et de mutualiser les efforts d’approvisionnement afin de générer des économies sans compromettre la qualité. Il vise également à simplifier la gestion des catégories d’achats et à éviter la mise en concurrence entre les centres opérationnels.

Le poste a par ailleurs pour finalité d’assurer une approche cohérente et harmonisée des approvisionnements au sein du mouvement MSF, à travers l’alignement des méthodologies, pratiques, outils et processus d’achat, dans le respect des protocoles, standards et procédures de MSF ainsi que de la réglementation locale, afin de renforcer la capacité des centres opérationnels à répondre efficacement aux besoins opérationnels.

**Responsabilités :**

**1.Effectuer une analyse des dépenses, identifier les catégories prioritaires communes à toutes les OCs et fournir une feuille de route de mise en œuvre.**

- Sur la base des informations fournies par les points focaux des achats des OCs (Coordinateur Supply / logistique, SCTL et/ou responsables des achats), établir une cartographie des dépenses pour identifier les priorités d'approvisionnement (fournisseurs clés et catégories).
- En collaboration avec le Comité de Pilotage, définir la stratégie d'approvisionnement intersectionnelle incluant les catégories à gérer au niveau intersectionnel et son plan de mise en œuvre.

**2. Définir et monitorer les fournisseurs intersection pour les catégories prioritaires**

- Créer une feuille de route pour la mise en œuvre des activités identifiées.
- Standardiser les listes des articles les plus couramment utilisés par catégorie dans les contrats communs entre les OCs pour les catégories prioritaires sélectionnées.
- Identifier les marchés et fournisseurs potentiels localement et régionalement en coordination avec d'autres opérations MSF dans d'autres pays pour les besoins communs.
- Diriger les processus d'appels d'offres ouverts pour les catégories et articles communs, en se concentrant sur l'efficacité, l'agilité, la qualité et le prix.
- Comprendre les outils d'approvisionnement et adapter les critères de sélection au contexte, encoder les données issues des divers appels d'offres et fournir une analyse pour soutenir les Coordinateurs Supply dans leur prise de décision.
- S'assurer de pratiques d'achat durables lors de la sélection des fournisseurs pour les catégories prioritaires et engager les fournisseurs actuels dans les ambitions durables de MSF.
- Évaluer la compétitivité des prix contractuels des contrats intersection avant renouvellement.
- Évaluer systématiquement la performance des fournisseurs sélectionnés pour les catégories prioritaires à l'aide d'outils d'évaluation et prendre des mesures correctives si nécessaire.
- Suivre physiquement les contrats et archiver systématiquement ceux-ci, mettre à jour l'outil de catalogue des prix utilisé sur la mission et le rendre accessible à toutes les parties concernées.

**3. Gérer un réseau fonctionnel pour les achats intersection**

- Organiser des réunions d’achat intersection au moins une fois par mois.
- Briefer les nouveaux points focaux achat / Supply de la mission et répondre à d’autres demandes de briefing ad hoc.
- S'assurer que les départements financiers reçoivent leurs copies des contrats et soient informés pour vérifier si les prix facturés sont conformes aux prix convenus.
- Veiller à ce que les produits soumis à la TVA soient répertoriés en collaboration avec le BIP (bureau des protocoles) et que l'application de l'exonération de la TVA soit accrue.
- Garantir la cohérence entre les termes contractuels des fournisseurs et les documents nécessaires pour l'application de l'exonération de TVA.
- Faire du réseautage avec d'autres organisations – Ex. Log Cluster et autres plateformes.
- Coordonner le travail avec les Responsable achats des OCs (PMs) afin d'éviter les chevauchements et la concurrence sur les mêmes activités. Le IPM se concentrera sur les catégories mutualisées convenues tandis que les PMs se concentreront sur les priorités propres à chaque OC, tout en collaborant étroitement sur les besoins opérationnels.
- Assurer l'implication adéquate des parties prenantes clés, y compris les référents techniques pour la validation des sources et des articles, afin de garantir une mise en œuvre réussie de la stratégie d’achat.
- Communiquer en temps opportun sur les problèmes, opportunités ou toute mise à jour importante liée à l'activité achat intersection.
- Fournir un soutien technique et accompagner le personnel des OCs pour contribuer au développement des meilleures pratiques et des capacités en matière d’achats.

**Hors périmètre :**

- Validation technique des sources pour les articles logistiques et médicaux nécessitant une telle validation.
- Passer les commandes aux centrales d’achat.
- Les activités transactionnelles comme le placement des commandes, la réception des marchandises et la facturation restent du ressort de chaque OC.

**Profil recherché :**

**Expérience / formation :**

- Diplôme universitaire en administration des affaires, gestion de la chaîne d'approvisionnement, achats ou similaire.
- 4+ ans d'expérience en achats/approvisionnement, incluant analyse de données, sourcing, négociation complexe et gestion de contrats ou dans un domaine similaire comportant les mêmes composantes.
- Connaissances approfondies des processus de chaîne d'approvisionnement et de budgétisation financière requises.
- Expérience internationale (en dehors du pays d'origine) et des missions de terrain dans le domaine des achats ou d'autres fonctions de la chaîne d'approvisionnement, en tant que responsable ou chef d'équipe d'approvisionnement ou postes similaires, avec MSF est requise.
- Connaissance du Mali / Burkina et expérience en intelligence de marché sont des atouts.

**Langue :**

- Maîtrise du français parlé et écrit, niveau minimum B2, est obligatoire. D'autres langues constituent un atout

**Compétences :**

- Esprit analytique, compétences organisationnelles et autonomie indispensables.
- Orientationsur les résultats et sens du service client requis.
- Capacité à travailler de manière transversale, dans un environnement multiculturel et à distance sont nécessaires.
- Capacités d'écoute, diplomatie avérée et aptitude à développer un réseau professionnel.
- Capacité à motiver et mobiliser les différents interlocuteurs
- Capacité avérée à travailler avec Office et ERP, en particulier une maîtrise d'Excel est indispensable.

**Condition de l'emploi :**

Contrat à durée déterminé de 12 mois.

**Nombre de postes: Deux postes (l'un au Mali et l'autre** **au Burkina Faso)**

**Prise de poste** : 1er décembre 2026.

jobs.title: Community Livelihoods Officer
jobs.description:
Child’s i Foundation was established in Uganda in 2009 and works towards advocating child rights and creating community-based alternatives to orphanages. We are a small non-profit with a big impact and work with governments, national partners, and our worldwide network of supporters to highlight the harm and cost of orphanages in Uganda and globally. We’re helping to reimagine the whole child protection and care system, repurpose orphanages and rebuild services at the heart of communities that are designed to strengthen and support birth, foster and adoptive families. Because every child needs a loving family, we are Child's i.

## Job Summary

The incumbent works with the Mpigi program team, and the rest of the Childs i staff in implementing the microfinance projects for grandmothers and the community in Mpigi District. He/she takes the lead in planning, coordinating and implementing microfinance activities. They ensure the successful formation of microfinance groups, conduct rapid appraisal of beneficiaries and provision of skills training on small businesses and income generating activities to beneficiaries. The incumbent conducts regular visits to monitor progress and conduct timely reporting. The role aims to build a microfinance strategy that encourages and enables investment in agricultural, business, and other income-generating initiatives while building up grandmother resilience to shocks through savings, assets, and social capital.

### Planning, Organizing and Management of MF related activities (50%)

- Develop work plans to ensure effective implementation of MF activities, while working closely with other microfinance staff, including taking on some supervisory roles as assigned by the program coordinator
- Technically lead to mobilise and establish MF groups in the selected communities
- Participate in beneficiary selection with relevant stakeholders
- Facilitate the identification and formation of MF groups among grandmothers and the community in general.
- Facilitate the establishment of village saving and loan groups (VSLAs) among the community, as a sustainability measure for the microfinance project and initiative.
- Plan and assess the microfinance needs of grandmothers, including undertaking an appraisal process for eligibility and qualification for loans by the applicants.
- Work with the procurement officer to ensure timely procurement of and delivery of the right quality and quantity of Microfinance kits and logistics.
- Witness and capture all data necessary on the disbursement of revolving funds to grandmother and other community groups.
- Identify technical capacity and challenges for vulnerable groups, skills, and knowledge they have in microfinance management, business development, and income-generating activities.
- Train Grandmothers and communities on VSLA methodology, including group governance and leadership

### Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning and Reporting (40%)

- Manage and maintain the microfinance loan performer application
- Oversee and monitor the grandmother groups on share purchases, social contributions, borrowing, and repayment of loans to ensure proper documentation and record keeping.
- Ensure timely preparation and submission of activity budgets, work plans, and progress reports of microfinance to the grandmother coordinator.
- Conduct regular follow-up visits to grandmother groups, their IGAs, and to members to see if they are applying the practices, and provide technical advice and mentoring.
- Track the progress of the grandmother groups and keep records.
- Carry out regular meetings with beneficiary groups to assess performance at the group and project levels.
- Consolidate and compile monthly, quarterly and annual reports, inclusive of success stories and lessons learned.

### Other (10 %)

- He/she is the secretary to the Revolving Fund Planning Committee (RPFC).
- Custodian of Microfinance meetings’ minutes and all microfinance records.
- Coordination of microfinance programs in Mpigi District.
- Assist in solving any conflicts among microfinance group members together with social workers
- Facilitate and link MF groups to training on life skills such as basic literacy and numeracy, household financial affairs, risk management and planning.
- Link up groups and vulnerable families with government programs and technical support staff
- Facilitate and link MF groups to economic development and income-generating activities
- Attend team meetings
- Any other duties as may be assigned by the Manager

## Qualification, Skills, and Experience

- Bachelor’s degree in community development, business administration, accounts, microfinance, economics or a related field
- Minimum1-year experience in VSLA methodology, livelihoods and IGA methodology
- Experienced facilitator and trainer, with training materials development skills
- Working experience in resilience initiatives is highly preferred
- Willingness to travel and leave in several rural project locations
- Ability to work with minimal supervision and achieve results
- Experience working with non-governmental organizations and local communities and authorities
- Ability to use standard computing packages
- Knowledge of some languages spoken in Central Uganda like Luganda, English etc

## Personal Qualities

- Organizes workload effectively while remaining aware of changing priorities and competing deadlines.
- A self-starter, who is highly self-motivated
- Results-oriented, critically thinking through solutions to challenges that arise.
- An excellent communicator, both verbally and in writing.
- A flexible, adaptive individual who thrives in a diverse and inclusive working environment.
- Demonstrated leadership, versatility, and integrity
- Positive attitude towards work

jobs.title: Deputy Director, Programs
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**JOB OVERVIEW**

The DDP leads, oversees, and ensures the compliance of IRC’s program portfolio, while ensuring alignment with organizational and donor guidelines. The DDP ensures internal and external coordination to develop high-quality proposals and deliver effective, timely programs. The DDP collaborates with all departments and partners, reports to the Country Director (CD), and is a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT). We are looking for a dynamic leader with strong cross-departmental collaboration skills, able to drive strategic success and support an inclusive, motivated team, in particular by empowering women to exercise leadership.

In coordination with the Country Director, the DDP establishes and maintains strong relationships with donors, as well as with DRC government entities and authorities.

The DDP directly supervises the senior program coordinators/managers responsible for proposal development, program quality, and implementation.

The incumbent is expected to spend at least 40% of their time supporting programs and teams in the provinces and in the field.

**MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Program Implementation**

- Oversee and ensure that programs are implemented to high quality standards and within the required timelines, including by supporting Program Coordinators and Technical Coordinators in the use of structured and realistic project management tools (including work plans, procurement plans, and spending plans), in coordination with the Operations teams.
- Closely monitor budgets, expenditures, and program progress to ensure that grants are implemented within budget and closed on time, ensuring consistent Project Cycle Management (PCM) routines and taking prompt, structured corrective action when needed.
- Ensure clear accountability, well-defined roles and responsibilities, and highly effective communication and coordination channels between teams within the Programs Department.
- Provide the CD with accurate, up-to-date advice on developments and opportunities in programming and project implementation, accompanied by recommendations for action.
- Support the MEAL Coordinator in implementing the country office MEAL strategy, ensuring that information from MEAL systems and client feedback mechanisms, including donor reporting, informs every stage of the project cycle.
- Ensure that appropriate technical assistance is provided by IRC Technical Units, external consultants, or partner agencies, as needed.

**2. Strategic Planning and Implementation**

- Lead the development, review, and implementation of the Strategy Action Plan (SAP) and the SAP-IP, fostering ownership of the strategy across all programmatic departments, ensuring delivery of strategic commitments, and applying IMPACT quality standards.
- Ensure that programming is aligned with the strategic priorities of the IRC DRC SAP and with Impact at Scale (I@S) priorities (where applicable), including program planning, project design, and staff communications.
- In coordination with the CD and other colleagues, update the country program and sector strategies annually, as part of the SAP process, so that they remain relevant and operationally effective in the face of changing contexts.
- Lead the development and rollout of strategic initiatives such as research and innovation, and ensure that cross-cutting issues (gender, climate change, and disaster risk reduction) are integrated into sector programming.

**3. Grants, Partnerships, and Business Development**

- Foster a partnership-driven, equality-based culture and working environment that reflects partnership principles and values and celebrates partnership successes (including risk sharing with partners and holding leadership accountable for a safeguarding culture in safe partnership).
- Ensure that IRC’s role in the DRC focuses on how we can add the most value to government actors and systems at the central and local levels, as well as to civil society and the private sector, within the framework of the SAP and of program planning and implementation.
- Provide overall direction and leadership to the IRC DRC Grants and Program Development teams by ensuring that a robust business development strategy, processes, and systems are in place, and that adequate funding is secured to deliver the intended results for clients.
- Oversee sound program design and proposal strategy for each new funding opportunity, including needs- and evidence-based program design, strong technical and operational engagement in design processes, and rigorous, competitive budgeting.
- Ensure that the Program, Grants, and Finance teams produce high-quality financial and narrative reports for donors.
- Lead the implementation of the IRC DRC Partnership Strategy and sector partnership plans, advancing localization commitments while maintaining high-quality, efficient services for clients; conduct stakeholder analysis and develop long-term partnerships with local civil society, government authorities, and private sector actors to promote locally led decision-making.
- Lead the implementation of IRC’s PEERS framework, ensuring cross-departmental collaboration, effective management of partnership risks, and responsive feedback systems with partners, while strengthening internal capacity through structured training, recruitment, and performance management aligned with partnership principles.
- Lead engagement with consortium partners, including strategic direction and coordination of program design or implementation.
- Increase the impact of IRC programming by maintaining and strengthening the trust of donors, partners, and key collaborators, while proactively positioning IRC for new program development opportunities.

**4. Human Resources and Staff Development**

- Recruitment and Performance: In coordination with the People & Culture team, ensure that the IRC DRC Program team is made up of high-quality staff who embody the organization’s values. Participate in recruitment and manage individual and collective performance, including development plans, performance standards, and evaluations, in line with organizational standards.
- Team Cohesion: Ensure that the Program team collaborates effectively, with clear mutual expectations and priority support for field teams.
- Foster collaboration, accountability, and staff well-being through quality management practices, performance monitoring systems, and leadership suited to the dynamics of remote work.

**5. Liaison/Representation and Coordination**

- Maintain a solid understanding of IRC programs in order to represent the organization and its interests externally in a professional manner, including with donors and government authorities, to ensure the sustainability of programs across the portfolio.
- Encourage and support greater program cohesion through coordination initiatives and information sharing among key country program staff.
- Actively contribute to advocacy initiatives, platforms, and external coordination forums, providing data from IRC programs to strengthen the protection of beneficiaries’ rights
- Participate actively in the Senior Management Team and serve as acting CD when necessary.

**KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

- **Position reports to:** Country Director and technical to Deputy Regional Director (Management in Partnership)
- **Positions under direct supervision:**

\- Technical sector program coordinators

**-** Senior Grants and Business Development Coordinator

**-** Partnership Coordinator

**-** MEAL Coordinator

- **Indirect reporting:** N/A
- **Other internal and/or external contacts:** *E-SMT Members and different partners and leaders of other NGOs*

**JOB REQUIREMENTS**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in International Development, International Relations, a relevant social science, or equivalent experience in related fields

**Experience:** Experience in a refugee context or a complex humanitarian and development environment with:

- More than 10 years of experience, including at least 5 years at program management level
- Excellent budget management and experience managing a wide range of donor contracts, including large-scale programs with substantial budgets
- Experience leading programs through both a direct operational approach and partnerships with local NGOs

**Skills and Abilities:**

- Excellent leadership, people management, interpersonal and negotiation skills, with a proven ability to build gender-balanced, harmonious, high-performing teams
- Strategic thinking, prioritization and ability to meet deadlines in a demanding environment
- Flexibility to adapt to changing needs
- Ability to work effectively and efficiently within a culturally diverse team
- Strong diplomatic skills to establish and maintain good working relationships with partners, donors and peers in a sensitive environment
- Excellent command of English and French, written and spoken
- Commitment to IRC’s core values: Integrity, Equality, Accountability and Service

**Working environment:**

**Location:** Goma

**Security:** The DDP will be based in Goma and will be required to travel regularly to the provinces of South Kivu, North Kivu, Ituri, Haut-Katanga, and Tanganyika. Goma is the capital of North Kivu and has a population of approximately one million. The city is rated Orange 4 on the MONUSCO security scale. As in any large city in the world, it is advisable to take precautions to prevent crime and theft.

**Accommodation:** This is an unaccompanied position, and the DDP will be housed in individual accommodation.

**Version française**

**APERÇU DU POSTE**

Le DDP dirige, supervise et assure la conformité du portefeuille de programmes de l’IRC, tout en veillant à son alignement avec les directives de l’organisation et des bailleurs. Le DDP assure la coordination interne et externe afin d’élaborer des propositions de haute qualité et de mettre en œuvre des programmes efficaces et dans les délais. Le DDP collabore avec l’ensemble des départements et des partenaires, relève de la Directrice Pays et est membre de l’Équipe de Direction Senior (SMT). Nous recherchons un leader dynamique, doté de solides compétences de collaboration transversale, capable de piloter la réussite stratégique et de soutenir une équipe inclusive et motivée, notamment en donnant aux femmes les moyens d’exercer un leadership.

En coordination avec le Directeur Pays, le DDP établit et entretient des relations solides avec les bailleurs, ainsi qu’avec les entités et autorités gouvernementales de la RDC.

Le DDP supervise directement les coordinateurs/responsables seniors de programmes chargés de l’élaboration des propositions, de la qualité des programmes et de leur mise en œuvre.

Le titulaire du poste devra consacrer au moins 40 % de son temps à l’appui aux programmes et aux équipes dans les provinces et sur le terrain.

**PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS**

**1. Mise en œuvre des programmes**

- Superviser et veiller à ce que les programmes soient mis en œuvre selon des normes de qualité élevées et dans les délais requis, notamment en appuyant les Coordinateurs de Programmes et les Coordinateurs Techniques dans l’utilisation d’outils de gestion de projet structurés et réalistes (y compris les plans de travail, les plans de passation de marchés et les plans de dépenses), en coordination avec les équipes Opérations.
- Suivre de près les budgets, les dépenses et l’avancement des programmes afin de garantir que les subventions sont mises en œuvre dans les limites du budget et clôturées à temps, en assurant des routines cohérentes de gestion du cycle de projet (PCM) et en prenant rapidement des mesures correctives structurées en cas de besoin.
- Garantir une redevabilité claire, des rôles et responsabilités bien définis, ainsi que des canaux de communication et de coordination très efficaces entre les équipes du Département des Programmes.
- Fournir au DP des conseils précis et à jour sur les évolutions et les opportunités en matière de programmation et de mise en œuvre des projets, accompagnés de recommandations d’action.
- Appuyer le Coordinateur MEAL dans la mise en œuvre de la stratégie MEAL du bureau pays, en veillant à ce que les informations issues des systèmes MEAL et des mécanismes de retour d’information des clients, y compris les rapports aux bailleurs, alimentent chaque étape du cycle de projet.
- Veiller à ce qu’une assistance technique appropriée soit fournie par les Unités Techniques de l’IRC, des consultants externes ou des agences partenaires, selon les besoins.

**2. Planification et mise en œuvre stratégiques**

- Diriger l’élaboration, la révision et la mise en œuvre du Plan d’Action Stratégique (SAP) et du SAP-IP, en favorisant l’appropriation de la stratégie par l’ensemble des départements programmatiques, en assurant la réalisation des engagements stratégiques et en appliquant les normes de qualité IMPACT.
- Veiller à ce que la programmation soit alignée sur les priorités stratégiques du SAP de l’IRC RDC et sur les priorités d’Impact at Scale (I@S) (le cas échéant), y compris la planification des programmes, la conception des projets et la communication avec le personnel.
- En coordination avec le DP et d’autres collègues, mettre à jour chaque année les stratégies du programme pays et des secteurs, dans le cadre du processus SAP, afin qu’elles restent pertinentes et efficaces sur le plan opérationnel face à l’évolution des contextes.
- Diriger l’élaboration et le déploiement d’initiatives stratégiques telles que la recherche et l’innovation, et veiller à ce que les questions transversales (genre, changement climatique et réduction des risques de catastrophe) soient intégrées dans la programmation sectorielle.

**3. Subventions, partenariats et développement des affaires**

- Promouvoir une culture et un environnement de travail axés sur le partenariat et fondés sur l’égalité, qui reflètent les principes et valeurs du partenariat et célèbrent les réussites en la matière (y compris le partage des risques avec les partenaires et la redevabilité de la direction quant à une culture de sauvegarde dans le cadre d’un partenariat sûr).
- Veiller à ce que le rôle de l’IRC en RDC se concentre sur la manière dont nous pouvons apporter le plus de valeur aux acteurs et systèmes gouvernementaux aux niveaux central et local, ainsi qu’à la société civile et au secteur privé, dans le cadre du SAP et de la planification et de la mise en œuvre des programmes.
- Assurer l’orientation et le leadership d’ensemble des équipes Subventions et Développement de Programmes de l’IRC RDC, en veillant à ce qu’une stratégie, des processus et des systèmes robustes de développement des affaires soient en place et à ce que des financements adéquats soient mobilisés pour obtenir les résultats escomptés pour les clients.
- Superviser la qualité de la conception des programmes et de la stratégie de proposition pour chaque nouvelle opportunité de financement, y compris une conception de programme fondée sur les besoins et les données probantes, un engagement technique et opérationnel fort dans les processus de conception, et une budgétisation rigoureuse et compétitive.
- Veiller à ce que les équipes Programmes, Subventions et Finance produisent des rapports financiers et narratifs de haute qualité à l’intention des bailleurs.
- Diriger la mise en œuvre de la Stratégie de Partenariat de l’IRC RDC et des plans de partenariat sectoriels, en faisant progresser les engagements en matière de localisation tout en maintenant des services efficaces et de haute qualité pour les clients ; mener une analyse des parties prenantes et développer des partenariats à long terme avec la société civile locale, les autorités gouvernementales et les acteurs du secteur privé afin de promouvoir une prise de décision pilotée localement.
- Diriger la mise en œuvre du cadre PEERS de l’IRC, en assurant la collaboration interdépartementale, une gestion efficace des risques liés aux partenariats et des systèmes de retour d’information réactifs avec les partenaires, tout en renforçant les capacités internes par la formation structurée, le recrutement et la gestion de la performance, en cohérence avec les principes du partenariat.
- Diriger l’engagement auprès des partenaires de consortium, y compris l’orientation stratégique et la coordination de la conception ou de la mise en œuvre des programmes.
- Accroître l’impact de la programmation de l’IRC en maintenant et en renforçant la confiance des bailleurs, des partenaires et des acteurs clés, tout en positionnant de manière proactive l’IRC pour de nouvelles opportunités de développement de programmes.

**4. Ressources humaines et développement du personnel**

- Recrutement et performance : En coordination avec l’équipe Personnes & Culture (People & Culture), veiller à ce que l’équipe Programmes de l’IRC RDC soit composée de personnel de grande qualité qui incarne les valeurs de l’organisation. Participer au recrutement et gérer la performance individuelle et collective, y compris les plans de développement, les normes de performance et les évaluations, conformément aux normes de l’organisation.
- Cohésion d’équipe : Veiller à ce que l’équipe Programmes collabore efficacement, avec des attentes mutuelles claires et un appui prioritaire aux équipes de terrain.
- Favoriser la collaboration, la redevabilité et le bien-être du personnel par des pratiques de gestion de qualité, des systèmes de suivi de la performance et un leadership adapté à la dynamique du travail à distance.

**5. Liaison/Représentation et coordination**

- Maintenir une solide compréhension des programmes de l’IRC afin de représenter l’organisation et ses intérêts de manière professionnelle à l’extérieur, y compris auprès des bailleurs et des autorités gouvernementales, afin d’assurer la pérennité des programmes sur l’ensemble du portefeuille.
- Encourager et soutenir une plus grande cohésion des programmes par des initiatives de coordination et le partage d’informations entre les principaux membres du personnel du programme pays.
- Contribuer activement aux initiatives et plateformes de plaidoyer ainsi qu’aux forums externes de coordination, en fournissant des données issues des programmes de l’IRC afin de renforcer la protection des droits des clients.
- Participer activement à l’Équipe de Direction Senior et assurer l’intérim du DP en cas de besoin.

**PRINCIPALES RELATIONS DE TRAVAIL**

- **Le poste est rattaché au :** Directeur Pays et, sur le plan technique, au Directeur Régional Adjoint (Management en Partenariat)
- **Postes sous supervision directe :**

**-** Coordinateurs techniques des programmes sectoriels

**-** Coordinateur Senior Subventions et Développement des Affaires

**-** Coordinateur Partenariats

**-** Coordinateur MEAL

- **Rattachement indirect :** N/A
- **Autres contacts internes et/ou externes :** *Membres de l’E-SMT et différents partenaires et dirigeants d’autres ONG*

**EXIGENCES DU POSTE**

**Formation :** Licence (Bachelor) en développement international, relations internationales, sciences sociales pertinentes, ou expérience équivalente dans des domaines connexes

**Expérience :** Expérience dans un contexte de réfugiés ou dans un environnement humanitaire et de développement complexe, avec :

- Plus de 10 ans d’expérience, dont au moins 5 ans à un niveau de gestion de programme
- Excellente maîtrise de la gestion budgétaire et expérience de la gestion d’un large éventail de contrats de bailleurs, y compris de programmes de grande envergure dotés de budgets importants
- Expérience de la direction de programmes à la fois selon une approche opérationnelle directe et à travers des partenariats avec des ONG locales

**Compétences et aptitudes :**

- Excellentes compétences en leadership, en gestion d’équipes, en relations interpersonnelles et en négociation, avec une capacité avérée à constituer des équipes équilibrées en termes de genre, harmonieuses et très performantes
- Pensée stratégique, sens des priorités et capacité à respecter les délais dans un environnement exigeant
- Flexibilité pour s’adapter à l’évolution des besoins
- Capacité à travailler de manière efficace et efficiente au sein d’une équipe culturellement diverse
- Solides compétences diplomatiques pour établir et entretenir de bonnes relations de travail avec les partenaires, les bailleurs et les pairs dans un environnement sensible
- Excellente maîtrise de l’anglais et du français, à l’écrit comme à l’oral
- Engagement envers les valeurs fondamentales de l’IRC : Intégrité, , Egalité, Responsabilité et Service

**Environnement de travail :**

**Lieu** : Goma

**Sécurité :** Le DDP sera basé à Goma et devra se déplacer régulièrement dans les provinces du Sud-Kivu, du Nord-Kivu, de l’Ituri, du Haut-Katanga et du Tanganyika. Goma est la capitale du Nord-Kivu et compte environ un million d’habitants. La ville est classée Orange 4 sur l’échelle de sécurité de la MONUSCO. Comme dans toute grande ville du monde, il est conseillé de prendre des précautions pour prévenir la criminalité et les vols.

**Hébergement :** Il s’agit d’un poste non accompagné, et le DDP sera hébergé dans un logement individuel.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**The Vacancy**

We are looking for a passionate and creative Social Media Coordinator to help deliver inspiring digital content that connects supporters with our mission and showcases the impact of our work around the world.

In this exciting role, you will support the planning and delivery of engaging social media campaigns, create compelling content across multiple platforms and help grow Islamic Relief UK's digital reach. Working as part of a dynamic Marketing team, you will play an important role in raising awareness, increasing engagement and generating support for life-changing humanitarian programmes globally.

**About the role**

- Supporting the development and implementation of Islamic Relief UK's organic social media strategy
- Managing and maintaining content across our social media channels, ensuring all content reflects Islamic Relief's brand, values and tone of voice
- Planning, creating and publishing engaging content across platforms including Facebook, Instagram, X, LinkedIn and other emerging channels
- Maintaining an up-to-date social media content calendar and ensuring content is planned and scheduled effectively
- Supporting the delivery of high-profile campaigns that raise awareness, drive engagement and generate fundraising income
- Developing compelling copy and working with creative teams to produce impactful digital content
- Monitoring social media performance and using insights, analytics and audience data to optimise content and campaign effectiveness
- Keeping up to date with emerging social media trends, best practice and platform developments to identify new opportunities for growth
- Managing online engagement and helping to foster positive relationships with supporters and online communities
- Supporting the development of relationships with influencers, content creators and key stakeholders to extend the reach of Islamic Relief's messaging
- Utilising social media management and reporting tools to monitor activity, evaluate performance and provide actionable recommendations
- Working collaboratively with colleagues across Marketing, Fundraising and Communications to ensure integrated and effective campaign delivery
- Providing operational and strategic support to the Digital Engagement Manager and deputising where required

**What we are looking for**

You will have experience creating platform-specific content, managing multiple priorities and using social media strategically to achieve organisational objectives. With excellent communication skills and a strong understanding of digital trends, you will be confident working collaboratively across teams and engaging with a diverse range of stakeholders.

- Degree level qualification or equivalent professional experience
- Significant experience creating engaging, channel-specific content across social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram, X (Twitter), LinkedIn and Snapchat
- Experience supporting the delivery of social media strategies and campaigns
- Experience producing and managing live video content to drive engagement and communicate key messages
- Experience working within the charity, third sector or not-for-profit environment, or a strong understanding of the sector and its communications needs
- Knowledge and appreciation of international development, humanitarian work and Islamic humanitarian values
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills with strong copywriting and proofreading abilities
- Experience using social media management, monitoring and listening tools, with knowledge of platforms such as Sprout Social being advantageous
- Strong understanding of social media trends, audience behaviours and digital best practice
- Experience using data, reporting and insights to optimise content performance and inform future activity
- Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple campaigns and deadlines simultaneously
- Experience using graphic design software such as Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail
- Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building skills
- A creative and innovative approach to content development and audience engagement
- The ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team
- A results-focused mindset with the ability to deliver against objectives and targets
- Strong motivation and empathy towards the aims and objectives of Islamic Relief
- Flexibility to work occasional evenings and weekends and travel when required
