jobs.title: Establishment of a Pre-Qualified Rooster of Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning Consultants
jobs.description:
**Introduction** Plan International strives to advance children’s rights and equality for girls all over the world. As an independent development and humanitarian organization, we work alongside children, young people, our supporters and partners to tackle the root causes of the challenges facing girls and all vulnerable children. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood and enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national, and global levels using our reach, experience, and knowledge. For over 80 years, we have been building powerful partnerships for children, and we are active in over 75 countries.

**Plan International Nigeria** is part of the global federation of Plan International and was registered in Nigeria in 2014. Plan International has five thematic areas which define our work, influencing priorities and partnerships. These are Education, Economic Empowerment, Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights, Health Nutrition and WASH; and Protection, with Youth Leadership, Climate Change and Gender as cross-cutting areas.

As the organisation continues to expand its portfolio and respond to increasingly complex development and humanitarian challenges, the demand for specialised MERL expertise has grown significantly. Assignments requiring external expertise include baseline studies, evaluations, operational research, humanitarian assessments, learning reviews, outcome harvesting, knowledge management products and strategic evidence generation. To improve responsiveness while maintaining technical quality and compliance with procurement requirements, Plan International Nigeria intends to establish a pre-qualified roster of MERL consultants comprising both individual consultants and consulting firms with demonstrated expertise across multiple technical disciplines.

**Purpose of the Scope of Work**

The purpose of this Scope of Work is to establish a roster of highly qualified Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning (MERL) consultants who can provide specialised technical services to Plan International Nigeria on an as-needed basis. The roster will serve as a mechanism for rapidly identifying and engaging consultants with the appropriate expertise for specific assignments while ensuring transparency, fairness, value for money and compliance with Plan International Nigeria's procurement policies.

Selection into the roster does not constitute a contract or guarantee of future work. Rather, it signifies that the consultant has met the minimum technical and professional requirements required to compete for future assignments through a streamlined call-down process.

**Objectives of the Consultant Roster**

The specific objectives of establishing the MERL Consultant roster are to:

- Establish a pool of highly competent consultants capable of delivering high-quality MERL assignments across Plan International Nigeria's programme portfolio.
- Reduce procurement lead times while maintaining transparency, competition and value for money.
- Improve the quality, consistency and credibility of evaluations, research and learning products commissioned by Plan International Nigeria.
- Strengthen organisational learning through access to specialists in evaluation, research, outcome harvesting and knowledge management.
- Improve the utilisation of evaluation findings by ensuring consultants generate actionable recommendations and high-quality knowledge products.
- Enhance technical support available to country, regional and project teams across development and humanitarian programming.
- Promote innovation in MERL through access to consultants experienced in adaptive and participatory evaluation methodologies.
- Build a long-term network of trusted technical experts capable of supporting Plan International Nigeria's evolving evidence needs.

**Scope of Services**

Consultants on the roster will be eligible for a broad range of MERL assignments, potentially spanning both development and humanitarian contexts. While the exact scope of each assignment will be defined in a specific Terms of Reference (ToR) when the assignment arises, the typical services and activities consultants in the roster may be requested to deliver include:

- **Evaluation Studies**: Baseline studies, Midline evaluations, Endline evaluations, Final project evaluations, Country Strategy evaluations, Thematic evaluations, Meta-evaluations, Real-time evaluations, Process evaluations, Performance evaluations, Impact evaluations, Cost-effectiveness and value-for-money studies. Assignments should be designed in accordance with internationally recognised evaluation standards, including the OECD-DAC evaluation criteria where applicable
- **Research Services**: Consultants may be required to undertake Operational research, Formative research, Applied research, Behavioural and social research, Mixed-methods research, Policy research, Institutional assessments, Barrier analyses, Market assessments, Gender analyses, Political economy analyses, Conflict analyses, Social inclusion studies, Situation analyses, Rapid evidence assessments, Literature reviews, Secondary data analyses
- **Humanitarian Assessments:** Multi-sector needs assessments, Rapid needs assessments, Emergency response evaluations, Humanitarian situation analyses, Post-distribution monitoring, Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) assessments, Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA) evaluations, Recovery assessments, Resilience assessments
- **Learning and Adaptive Management:** Outcome Harvesting, Outcome Mapping, Most Significant Change (MSC), Developmental Evaluation, Contribution Analysis, Process Tracing, Learning Reviews, Reflection Workshops, After-Action Reviews, Pause-and-Reflect Sessions, Adaptive Management Reviews, Learning Agenda Development
- **Monitoring System Strengthening:** Development of monitoring frameworks, Indicator development and refinement, Theory of Change development, Logical Framework development, Results Framework development, Data Quality Assessments (DQAs), Digital data collection system design, Dashboard development, Routine monitoring system reviews, Capacity assessments, MERL capacity strengthening
- **Knowledge Management and Evidence Products:** Beyond conducting studies, consultants may be required to transform evidence into products suitable for different audiences. These may include: Technical reports, Policy briefs, Learning briefs, Research papers, Evidence summaries, Case studies, Success stories, Infographics, Donor briefing papers, Communication materials based on research findings
- Consultants must have demonstrated experience integrating gender-transformative, child-centered and youth-led approaches into research, evaluation and learning processes.

**Note:** *Each specific assignment will be governed by its own detailed ToR and possibly an individual contract, which will stipulate the precise scope, deliverables, timeline, and any specialized requirements. The above list illustrates the typical range of tasks that fall under the roster’s remit, indicating the breadth of expertise that consultants should possess*

**Competency Areas**

To ensure assignments are matched with appropriate expertise, consultants will be pre-qualified under one or more technical competency areas. Applicants may apply under multiple categories where they can demonstrate the required experience.

**Category A: Evaluation Specialists**

Specialists capable of designing and leading: Baseline studies, Midline evaluations, Endline evaluations, Performance evaluations, Impact evaluations, Country Strategy evaluations, Multi-project evaluations

**Category B: Research Specialists**

Experts in qualitative, quantitative and mixed-methods research capable of conducting operational, applied and policy-oriented studies.

**Category C: Learning and Outcome Harvesting Specialists**

Specialists with demonstrated expertise in Outcome Harvesting, Outcome Mapping, Most Significant Change, Developmental Evaluation, Contribution Analysis, Learning facilitation, Knowledge capture, Adaptive programming

**Category D: Humanitarian MERL Specialists**

Professionals experienced in humanitarian contexts including emergency assessments, humanitarian performance monitoring & evaluations, conflict-sensitive programming and accountability to affected populations, anticipatory action, humanitarian development & peace nexus programming

**Category E: Data Analytics and Digital MERL Specialists**

Experts in Statistical analysis, Data visualization, GIS, Dashboard development, Power B, R, Python, SPSS, STATA, KoboToolbox, ODK, SurveyCTO

**Category F: Gender, Inclusion and Child Rights Specialists**

Experts with demonstrated experience in gender-transformative analysis, Child rights programming, disability inclusion assessments, safeguarding audits and assessments, protection research, social norms analysis etc

**Category G: Knowledge Management and Learning Specialists**

Experts in synthesising evidence into accessible products including policy briefs, learning papers, donor reports, executive summaries and organisational learning products.

**Engagement and Selection Process**

Plan International Nigeria will use a structured yet flexible process to establish and utilise the consultant roster:

- Roster Creation / Prequalification: An open call for expressions of interest will be advertised to invite qualified consultants (individuals and firms) to apply for inclusion in the MERL consultancy roster. Applicants will undergo a competitive vetting process evaluating their technical expertise, relevant experience, capacity, and references. Only candidates meeting the predefined criteria and quality standards will be pre-qualified and admitted to the roster. The outcome will be a vetted roster of consultants across various specialties.

Assignment Call-Down (Direct Competitive Selection): When a MERL assignment arises that falls within the scope of this roster, Plan International Nigeria can engage a consultant from the roster without a public tender. In these cases, a limited competitive selection among roster members will be conducted. Typically, a brief ToR or request for a short proposal will be shared with a subset or all of the relevant pre-qualified consultants, and they will be invited to submit a targeted technical and financial proposal. The selection will then be made based on the best value offer (considering technical fit, availability, timeline, and cost). This mechanism ensures speed and efficiency, reducing hiring lead time while still maintaining competition and transparency among pre-vetted candidates.

- Public Tender Option: For assignments that exceed the financial threshold for direct selection from the roster, or in scenarios where the needed expertise is highly specialized and not sufficiently covered by roster members, Plan International Nigeria retains the option to go for a public advertisement and open tender. This ensures compliance with procurement policies for larger contracts and provides flexibility to source beyond the roster if needed (for example, if donor regulations or specific procurement rules require an open process). The existence of the roster does not override Plan’s commitment to fair and open competition when required.
- Flexibility in Engagement: The Supply Chain Unit, in consultation with the MERL Unit, will determine the most appropriate procurement method for each assignment. Factors considered will include urgency of the assignment, the estimated budget relative to threshold, the availability of suitable expertise in the roster, and any donor-specific procurement stipulations.
- Applications will be evaluated using a weighted scoring system to ensure transparency, fairness and consistency.

**Objectives of Assignments**

Specific responsibilities, deliverables, and timelines will be defined in the Terms of Reference issued for each assignment. Depending on the nature of the engagement, consultants may be required to design methodologies, collect and analyse data, facilitate learning processes, develop knowledge products, and present findings to stakeholders.

**Key Tasks and Responsibilities of the Consultants**
- Individual consultants/firms engaged under this SoW will generally be expected to undertake a suite of tasks corresponding to the full cycle of an evaluation or research study. While specific tasks will be detailed in each assignment’s TOR, typical responsibilities include:
- Once contracted for an assignment, the consultant will conduct initial consultations with Plan International Nigeria’s team (MERL staff, project managers, technical advisors) to understand the context and requirements. The consultant will develop an Inception Report, which comprises a refined methodology, evaluation matrix, detailed work plan, data collection tools and a sampling plan. The inception phase may include a literature review and preliminary data scan. The consultant is responsible for incorporating Plan’s and stakeholders’ feedback and validating the approach before fieldwork begins.
- Design and finalize data collection tools and protocols, ensuring they are contextually appropriate and aligned with the approved methodology. The consultant will also develop necessary training materials for enumerators.
- Oversee and conduct the data collection as per the agreed methodology. This involves coordinating fieldwork logistics (with support from Plan staff if provided), supervising enumerator teams, ensuring adherence to ethical standards (especially when engaging with children or vulnerable populations), and performing ongoing quality control (spot-checks, daily data reviews).
- Prepare the draft report documenting all aspects of the assignment. The report should include an executive summary, background, methodology (including limitations), findings, conclusions, and recommendations. The consultant will submit the draft for review by Plan International Nigeria. After receiving feedback (from Plan staff, donor or key stakeholders), the consultant will address all comments and revisions to produce the Final Report. The final report should be of publishable quality, meeting Plan International’s standards for clarity, insight, and evidence.
- The consultant will present key findings and recommendations to relevant stakeholders. This might involve presentations or validation workshops with Plan staff, donor representatives, government partners, and community stakeholders.
- Ensure that all data and materials from the assignment are properly handed over to Plan International Nigeria at the conclusion of the assignment. This includes raw datasets (in an agreed format, e.g., Excel, SPSS), transcripts or recordings of qualitative data, copies of completed survey forms if paper-based, the final cleaned data with codebooks, and any other relevant documentation. The consultant must also maintain confidentiality of all data (per ethical standards) and ensure its secure transfer.
- Throughout the assignment, the consultant will work closely with Plan’s MERL team and relevant program staff. This entails maintaining regular communication (e.g., weekly or bi-weekly progress updates), proactively flagging any challenges, and ensuring alignment with Plan’s internal frameworks (like project logframes or MERL frameworks).
- Plan International Nigeria reserves the right to request revisions where deliverables do not meet expected technical, editorial, safeguarding or quality standard

**Regulatory Documents**

Consulting Firms/ Individual Consultants must have the following documents to be considered:
- A **detailed company profile** that clearly outlines your business activities and areas of expertise. Individual Consultants are to submit a detailed CV.
- Evidence of valid registration with corporate affairs commission, with the Memorandum and Articles of Association, and forms CAC2 and CAC7 or a status report. Individual Consultants are to submit a valid means of identification.
- Evidence of a tax clearance certificate for any of the years ending in 2024 or 2025. Personal Income tax certificate is acceptable for Individual Consultants.
- Properly filled Annex C, D & E

**Consultant Qualifications and Experience**

To be eligible for inclusion in the MERL consultancy roster and to successfully deliver assignments, the consultant (individual or firm) must demonstrate the following minimum qualifications and experience:

**Individual Consultants**

- An advanced degree (Masters or Ph.D.) in a relevant field such as Social Sciences, Public Health, Development Studies, Education, Statistics, Economics, or other disciplines related to international development and evaluation.
- At least 7–10 years of proven experience leading and conducting evaluations, research studies, and baseline/endline assessments in development or humanitarian contexts. This experience should include a mix of sectoral areas relevant to Plan International’s work (for example: child protection, education, gender and inclusion, youth livelihoods, health/nutrition, etc.) and demonstrate the consultant’s ability to handle various types of MERL assignments.
- Additional professional certifications in evaluation, research methods, project management, statistics or data science will be considered desirable.

**Consulting Firms**

Consulting firms should demonstrate access to multidisciplinary teams comprising specialists in: Evaluation, Quantitative Research, Qualitative Research, Statistics, Data Management, Gender and Inclusion, Child Rights, Knowledge Management, Humanitarian Programming, GIS and Data Visualisation.

In addition, individual consultants and firms should demonstrate the following:

- Strong competencies in both quantitative and qualitative research methodologies. Consultants/firms should have a track record of designing robust sampling strategies, crafting surveys and interview protocols, conducting statistical analysis (using tools like SPSS, STATA, or R), and qualitative analysis (using NVivo, ATLAS.ti, or similar). Experience with participatory evaluation techniques and mixed-methods approaches is highly valued.
- Demonstrated familiarity with Nigerian context (or similar contexts in West Africa), including understanding of cultural, social, and security considerations that influence field research. Prior work in Nigeria or the region, particularly in similar thematic sectors as Plan Nigeria, is a strong advantage. Experience working with vulnerable and marginalized groups (children, youth, women, persons with disabilities, internally displaced persons, etc.) in research processes is essential.
- Excellent analytical and report writing skills, with an ability to present complex findings in a clear, concise manner. The consultant/ firm should demonstrate strong facilitation and communication skills for leading workshops or presenting findings to stakeholders. Proficiency in English is required; knowledge of local languages (e.g., Hausa, Kanuri, Yoruba, Pidgin) is an asset, especially for facilitating fieldwork.
- Proficiency in relevant software and tools for data collection and analysis (for instance, electronic data capture tools like KoboToolbox/ODK for field surveys, GIS for mapping if needed, advanced Excel for data visualization, etc.). The consultant/firm should also be comfortable training others on these tools if the assignment involves enumerator training.
- Demonstrated ability to deliver assignments on time and to a high standard, as evidenced by references or sample reports from previous work. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail are necessary. Additionally, the consultant should have a track record of working collaboratively with clients and stakeholders, including adaptability to feedback and changing conditions, while maintaining independence and objectivity in evaluation.
- Plan International Nigeria encourages expertise in adaptive management, systems thinking, complexity-aware monitoring and evaluation approaches.

Further information on this consultancy, including all mandatory annexes to be completed, can be found via the link below\*\*:\*\*

[https://tinyurl.com/mwdmjscm](https://tinyurl.com/mwdmjscm)

jobs.description:
**PRÉSENTATION ALIMA**

**L’ESPRIT ALIMA :** La raison d’être d’ALIMA est de sauver des vies et de soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, sans aucune discrimination identitaire, religieuse ou politique, à travers des actions basées surla proximité, l’innovation et l’alliance d’organisations et d’individus. Nous agissons avec humanisme, impartialité et dans le respect de l’éthique médicale universelle. Pour accéder aux patients et aux patientes, nous nous engageons à intervenir de façon neutre et indépendante.

**LES VALEURS et PRINCIPES de notre action, inscrits au sein de notre CHARTE :**

- Le patient et la patiente d’abord
- Révolutionner la médecine humanitaire
- Responsabilité et liberté
- Améliorer la qualité de nos actions
- Faire confiance
- L’intelligence collective
- La responsabilité environnementale

ALIMA promeut et défend les principes des droits humains fondamentaux. ALIMA a une approche de tolérance zéro envers les personnes coupables d’actes de violences sexistes et sexuelles ainsi qu’envers l’inaction face à des faits de violence supposés ou avérés. La protection des personnes bénéficiant et impactées par notre intervention est notre priorité absolue dans tout ce que nous faisons. Toute personne collaborant avec ALIMA s’engage à :

- Respecter la charte, le code de conduite, les politiques institutionnelles incluant la politique de protection contre les abus de pouvoir et les violences sexistes et sexuelles, la politique de prévention de la corruption et de la fraude ;
- Signaler toute violation aux politiques, documents cadre et procédure à une supérieure, un supérieur, une référente, un référent.

**SOIGNER - INNOVER - ENSEMBLE :** Depuis sa création en 2009, ALIMA a touché plus de 18 millions de bénéficiaires dans 15 pays, principalement en Afrique. En 2024, nous avons développé 59 projets de réponse médicale humanitaire pour répondre aux besoins de populations touchées par les conflits, les épidémies et l’extrême pauvreté. L’ensemble de ces projets se font en appui aux autorités sanitaires nationales à travers les structures de santé (dont hôpitaux et centres de santé). Notre action découle d’une adaptation constante aux réalités du terrain et aux progrès de la médecine. En 2024, ALIMA a atteint 5,9 millions de bénéficiaires. Nous travaillons en partenariat, notamment avec des ONGs locales, dès que cela est possible afin de nous assurer que nos patients et patientes bénéficient de l’expertise là où elle se trouve, que ce soit au niveau de leur pays ou du reste du monde. Par ailleurs, pour améliorer la réponse humanitaire, nous menons des projets de recherches opérationnelles et cliniques notamment dans le domaine de la lutte contre la malnutrition et les fièvres virales hémorragiques.

**L'ÉQUIPE ALIMA :** plus de 2000 personnes œuvrent actuellement pour ALIMA. Les équipes terrain, au plus proche des patients, reçoivent leur support des équipes de coordination généralement basées en capitale des pays d’intervention. Celles-ci reçoivent le support des 4 équipes desk et de l’équipe du service urgences et ouvertures basées au siège opérationnel de Dakar, Sénégal. Les équipes de Paris et New-York travaillent activement à la collecte de fonds ainsi qu’à la représentation d’ALIMA. Le reste de la Galaxie ALIMA comprend des individus et des équipes partenaires qui travaillent pour le compte d’autres organisations telles que les ONGs médicales BEFEN, ALERTE Santé, SOS Médecins / KEOOGO, AMCP, les organismes de recherche PACCI, INSERM, INRB, les Universités de Bordeaux ou de Copenhague, l’ONG Solidarités International et bien d’autres.

**NOS THÉMATIQUES PROJET :** Malnutrition, Santé sexuelle et reproductive incluant les violences basées sur le genre, Santé Primaire et secondaire, la chirurgie, les soins pédiatriques, les maladies tueuses tel que Paludisme, IRA, Diarrhée, Épidémies (Fièvres hémorragiques, méningite, Choléra, Rougeole, Dengue, Covid-19).

**NOS PAYS D’INTERVENTIONS :** Mali, Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, Ethiopie, Haïti, Nigeria, Niger, Tchad, République Démocratique du Congo, Cameroun, Guinée, Soudan du Sud, Sénégal, Mauritanie et Soudan.

**PROTECTION DES BÉNÉFICIAIRES ET DES MEMBRES DE LA COMMUNAUTÉ**

**Niveau 3 :** le titulaire du poste aura des contacts avec des enfants ou/et des adultes vulnérables soient fréquemment (par exemple une fois par semaine ou plus), soit régulièrement (par exemple quatre jours dans un mois ou plus ou pendant la nuit) parce qu'il travaille dans le cadre de programmes nationaux, ou parce qu'il visite des programmes nationaux, ou parce qu'il est responsable d’application du processus de recrutement ; Par conséquent, la vérification du casier judiciaire ou la présentation d'un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs sera nécessaire. Dans les situations où l’impossibilité de fournir un casier judiciaire ou un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs est constatée, une déclaration sur l’honneur sera demandée.

**LIENS FONCTIONNELS ET HIÉRARCHIQUES**

Le référent RH fait partie de l’équipe du Desk 3 et rend compte directement au Responsable des Programmes (superviseur hiérarchique) et à la Responsable RH Opérationnelle (lien fonctionnel).

Il collabore avec toute l’équipe du Desk (équipe pluridisciplinaire constituée par plusieurs référents métiers : médical, logistique, finance, RH, bailleurs supervisant plusieurs pays d’intervention) dont il/elle fait partie afin de fournir le meilleur support possible aux équipes terrain et de construire une stratégie long terme pour chaque pays.

Il/elle collabore également avec les Référents RH des autres Desks, les Chargés de recrutement et de suivi de pool, l’équipe du bureau administratif, les référents techniques du bureau de Dakar et les équipes de Coordination dans les pays d’intervention dont il a la charge.

Il accompagne et conseille les coordinateurs RH et les coordinateurs finances/RH sur les terrains.

Ce poste est donc multidimensionnel avec de nombreux interlocuteurs et demande une grande capacité de communication, d’adaptation et par conséquent une grande aisance à créer des relations de confiance.

**MISSION ET ACTIVITÉS PRINCIPALES**

Point focal pour les ressources humaines au niveau du Desk, la/le e Référent(e) RH soutient la motivation des acteurs en poste, leurs compétences au service des objectifs Projets, dans un climat de confiance et en accord avec nos valeurs afin de garantir l’enjeu collectif de la qualité et du développement de nos opérations.

La/Le Référent(e) RH mène sa mission :

- En animant, avec le Responsable Programme et le reste de l’équipe desk, ainsi que les gestionnaires de pool, la dynamique de composition d’équipe pour les besoins des projets.
- En participant au développement des talents par la proposition de parcours / formations / accompagnements objectifs, adaptés et construits avec les Référents techniques pools, les gestionnaires de pool ainsi que la Chargée de formation.
- En appuyant les Coordinateurs RH ou Responsables RH dans la garantie du cadre administratif et légal ALIMA de gestion des ressources humaines au sein des pays d’intervention.
- En soutenant les Coordinateurs ou Responsables RH sur le terrain dans la recherche de solutions à des problèmes RH complexes afin de soutenir les projets et de s’assurer que les équipes sur le terrain ont les moyens de sauver des vies et d’assurer une meilleure prise en charge des personnes les plus vulnérables.

**Activités principales :**

- Avec les desks et les coordinations des pays, conseille la composition d’équipe, identifie les besoins en recrutement international, suit le développement des salarie.e.s et parcours et vient en appui / accompagnement des managers à tous les niveaux.
- Avec les chargés de recrutement, les référent.e.s techniques pools et les référent.e.s RH, co-identifie les personnes pour pourvoir les postes définis en interne (placement) ou en externe (recrutement) à l’aide des supports adéquats (réunions pools, tests, entretiens, références…) dans le délai imparti et avec objectif une composition d’équipe optimale.
- Soutient et accompagne tout le long le travail des Coordinateurs RH (CORH) et des équipes RH dans les pays, aide dans le suivi des objectifs définis par les Manager des Coordinateurs RH, apporte un soutien technique sur toutes les problématiques de gestion des ressources humaines : politique de recrutement, suivi du personnel (bilan, formation, procédures disciplinaires…), identification des talents, développement des compétences, mobilité, évolution, composition d’équipe, grille de fonctions et salaires.
- Avec les Coordinateurs RH (CORH), directement lors des ouvertures de pays, lors des ouvertures et fermetures des projets s’assure que les politiques RH, la Charte et les autres politiques cadres ALIMA sont mises en œuvre dans le respect du cadre légal propre à chaque pays.
- Apporte une expertise et un soutien sur l’utilisation des outils RH, principalement Homère, Odoo et autres fichiers de suivi du personnel national et international.
- En collaboration avec le Référent Finance Desk, les autres membres du Desk et les équipes de coordination des Pays, assure un suivi RH opérationnel des budgets et des propositions de financement des missions d’intervention en veillant à leur cohérence avec les besoins opérationnels, les effectifs et les ressources disponibles.
- Elle.il participe à la définition des politiques RH auprès du DRH et intervient sur des sujets transversaux : stratégie de recrutement active, gestion de parcours, formation, SIRH, amélioration des outils/procédures.
- Il s’assure de la complétude, promptitude et pertinence des informations/données RH remontées par les terrains et les consolide au niveau desk.
- Mise en œuvre des mesures de prévention contre les abus de pouvoir, les violences sexistes et sexuelles :
- Appui le développement de diagnostic sur les pays d’intervention et l’élaboration d’un plan d’action qui sera révisé régulièrement ;

jobs.title: Consultant – Comparative, Gender-Sensitive and Youth-Inclusive Assessment of Georgia’s Diaspora Engagement Policy & Institutional Framework
jobs.description:
**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration
**Duty Station of the Consultancy**: Tbilisi, Georgia. Remote assignment - 2 missions to Georgia envisaged for the presentation of preliminary findings and participation in the validation of the final report.

**Duration of Consultancy:** 24 November 2026 – 8 April 2027 (20 working days).

**Nature of the consultancy:** Conduct an international comparative, gender-sensitive and youth-inclusive assessment of diaspora engagement policies, institutional arrangements and practices, and to contribute to evidence-based recommendations for strengthening Georgia’s diaspora engagement framework.

The international consultant (IC) will specifically contribute international comparative expertise, identify relevant global good practices and provide methodological and analytical input to the Georgia-specific review undertaken jointly with the national consultant.

**Project Context and Scope**

Georgia has a large and diverse diaspora community worldwide whose knowledge, skills, networks, investments and other resources represent an important potential contribution to the country’s social and economic development. According to international estimates, nearly half a million Georgian-born migrants live abroad, while the broader diaspora is considerably larger and geographically dispersed across Europe, North America and other regions. Georgia’s diaspora represents a significant source of human, social, cultural and economic capital that can contribute to innovation, investment, entrepreneurship, knowledge transfer and local development.

Over the years, the Government of Georgia has implemented a range of initiatives aimed at maintaining ties with Georgian communities abroad and promoting diaspora engagement, including diaspora outreach programmes, grant schemes, cultural initiatives and institutional coordination. However, existing efforts remain fragmented, and there is a need for a more comprehensive, evidence-based, gender-sensitive and youth-inclusive approach that can respond to the evolving profile, needs and aspirations of diaspora communities.

To address these challenges, IOM is implementing the project “Georgia’s Global Diaspora Engagement Initiative for National Development”, which aims to strengthen the enabling environment for effective and sustainable diaspora engagement and support greater contributions of diaspora communities to national development. The project seeks to institutionalize diaspora engagement as a core component of Georgia’s development agenda through strengthened policies, institutional arrangements, coordination mechanisms, and innovative approaches to diaspora investment, innovation and knowledge exchange.

As part of this effort, IOM will undertake a comprehensive policy and institutional analysis of diaspora engagement in Georgia. The analysis will assess existing policy frameworks, institutional arrangements, coordination mechanisms, and stakeholder engagement practices, while also examining opportunities for strengthening diaspora participation in national development processes. Particular attention will be paid to the meaningful engagement of women and young diaspora members and to identifying international good practices relevant to the Georgian context. The policy and institutional analysis will serve as a foundational activity under the project and will provide the evidence base for strengthening policy coordination, identifying institutional gaps and opportunities, supporting stakeholder consultations, and informing future strategic planning on diaspora engagement. The assignment will contribute to ensuring that diaspora engagement policies and mechanisms are evidence-based, inclusive, and aligned with international good practices while remaining responsive to the specific needs and priorities of Georgia.

Under the direct supervision of the IOM Programme Manager, the IC will provide an comparative, gender-sensitive and youth-inclusive assessment of diaspora engagement policies, institutional arrangements and practices, identify relevant global good practices and provide methodological and analytical input to the Georgia-specific review, to contribute to evidence-based recommendations for strengthening Georgia’s diaspora engagement framework.

The consultant will undertake the following tasks:

A. Develop the methodology and analytical approach and review relevant materials

- Review the existing analytical and policy framework for diaspora engagement in Georgia, as well as relevant project documentation and materials provided by IOM, with the support of the national consultant.
- Develop an inception report with the findings from the literature review and methodology for assessing diaspora policies and institutional arrangements from an international comparative perspective.
- Ensure that gender equality and meaningful youth participation are integrated throughout the methodology.
- Agree with IOM and the national consultant on the workplan, division of responsibilities and approach to consultations.

B. Conduct an international comparative review

IC will review selected international and global approaches to diaspora engagement, with particular attention to: a) diaspora policy and strategy development; b) institutional and coordination mechanisms; c) diaspora consultation and representation; d) engagement of diaspora professionals, entrepreneurs and investors; e) mobilization of diaspora knowledge, skills and networks; f) youth diaspora engagement and women’s participation.

IC will identify relevant global good practices and innovative approaches. Analyse the conditions under which these practices have been effective and assess their relevance and applicability to the Georgian context.

C. Contribute to the policy and institutional analysis of Georgia

With the support of and in close coordination with the National Consultant, the International Consultant (IC) will provide international comparative, methodological and analytical expertise to the assessment of Georgia’s diaspora engagement policy and institutional framework. The IC will ensure that the Georgia-specific assessment is informed by relevant international experience and good practices, while remaining responsive to Georgia’s institutional, policy and socio-economic context.

The IC will:

- Contribute to the assessment of Georgia’s existing diaspora engagement policy and strategic framework, including relevant legislation, policies, strategies, action plans and other key government and institutional documents, with a focus on their objectives, scope, implementation arrangements, coherence and alignment with broader national development priorities.
- Assess the institutional architecture for diaspora engagement, including the mandates, roles and responsibilities of relevant government institutions and other key stakeholders involved in diaspora affairs. Particular attention will be given to institutional coordination, division of responsibilities, information-sharing and mechanisms for ensuring a coherent and whole-of-government approach to diaspora engagement.
- Examine existing mechanisms and practices for diaspora consultation, participation and representation, including opportunities for diaspora communities and diaspora organizations to contribute to policy development, programme design, implementation and monitoring. The assessment should consider the extent to which existing mechanisms enable meaningful, inclusive and sustained engagement.
- Provide comparative perspectives on Georgia’s institutional and coordination arrangements, drawing on the international comparative review undertaken under this assignment. The IC will identify relevant models and approaches from other countries and assess their potential relevance and applicability to the Georgian context, taking into account differences in institutional structures, diaspora profiles and national circumstances.
- Assess existing approaches to mobilizing diaspora human, social, professional, financial and knowledge resources, including mechanisms for engaging diaspora professionals, entrepreneurs, investors, researchers and other skilled members of the diaspora in national and local development. Where relevant, the assessment should consider existing or potential mechanisms for knowledge transfer, investment, innovation, entrepreneurship and skills exchange.
- Identify key policy and institutional gaps, overlaps, coordination challenges and opportunities affecting effective diaspora engagement in Georgia. This should include consideration of the enabling environment, institutional capacity, stakeholder coordination, outreach and communication mechanisms, and the sustainability and effectiveness of existing engagement approaches.
- Assess the inclusiveness of the existing diaspora engagement framework, with particular attention to the participation and representation of women and young diaspora members. The assessment should identify structural, institutional or practical barriers to their meaningful participation and highlight opportunities and entry points for strengthening their engagement in policy processes, programmes, investment, entrepreneurship, knowledge exchange and other forms of national development.
- Contribute to the identification of priority areas for strengthening Georgia’s diaspora engagement framework, drawing on evidence from the Georgia-specific assessment, stakeholder consultations and international comparative experience. Recommendations should be practical, context-sensitive and, where possible, linked to specific institutional or policy entry points.
- Work closely with the National Consultant to ensure complementarity between the international comparative and Georgia-specific components of the analysis, jointly review emerging findings, and integrate relevant national evidence and stakeholder perspectives into the comparative assessment.

Gender equality, youth inclusion and meaningful participation of diverse diaspora groups should be systematically integrated across all aspects of the analysis rather than treated as stand-alone considerations.

D. Support consultations and validation processes

The consultant will support IOM and the national consultant in preparing and conducting:

- Stakeholder consultations, validation workshops and IWG meetings, including contributing consultation methodologies, agendas and guiding questions.
- Prepare presentations and analytical materials;
- Facilitate and/or co-facilitate discussions and incorporating stakeholder feedback into the final report.

Based on the policy and institutional review, international comparative analysis and stakeholder consultations, the consultant will contribute to a set of practical recommendations, based on evidence and international experience, aimed at strengthening Georgia’s diaspora engagement framework

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**
Georgia’s Global Diaspora Engagement Initiative for National Development

**Category B Consultants: Tangible and measurable outputs of the work assignment**

- **Deliverable 1**: Inception Report, with Methodology and Analytical Framework. A concise inception report to be submitted by 8 December 2026.
- **Deliverable 2**: International Comparative Review of Diaspora Engagement Policies and Practices with institutional and coordination models and special focus on diaspora youth and women engagement, mobilization of diaspora knowledge, skills and resources, to be submitted by 29 January 2027.
- **Deliverable 3**. Analytical Inputs to the Joint (with the National Consultant) Policy and Institutional Review, including comparative assessment of Georgia’s existing framework, key policy and institutional gaps, opportunities and entry points, gender and youth considerations and comparative lessons relevant to Georgia to be submitted by 15 March 2027.
- **Deliverable 4**: Final report with actionable recommendations, validated by the stakeholders, to be submitted by 8 April 2027.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- Delivers the listed deliverables on time and with good quality.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Advanced postgraduate degree (i.e., PhD, MA, MSc) in Demography, Economics, Sociology, Statistics, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Public Affairs, and/or other disciplines relevant to the assignments.
- **Experience & Skills**
- Demonstrated experience in research, policy analysis, comparative policy analysis, developing policy recommendations and/or programmatic work related to the migration, development area.
- Demonstrated experience in diaspora engagement, migration and development, migration governance or related fields.
- Knowledge of diaspora engagement policies and institutional models in different regional contexts would be an advantage.
- Experience conducting assessments on migration and development, preferably in Eastern Europe, or South Caucasus.
- Proficiency in qualitative and quantitative research methodologies, including field data collection, stakeholder consultations, and policy analysis.
- Previous engagement with government institutions, international organizations, or NGOs on migration and development issues.
- Demonstrated ability to work in English, with excellent oral and written communication skills.

**Travel required**

- Remote assignement, with two missions to Georgia envisaged for the presentation of preliminary findings and participation in the validation of the final report. Consultancy fee will cover all travel and other expenses of the consultant and shall constitute the only financial entitlement which will be disbursed to the consultant.

**Languages**

- For this consultancy, excellent command of English is required.
- Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

- IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.
- **Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:
- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.
- **Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators
- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

jobs.title: Senior Research Officer - MSNA - Global, Based in Amman
jobs.description:
## **BACKGROUNG ON IMPACT & REACH**

REACH was born in 2010 as a joint initiative of two International NGOs ([IMPACT Initiatives](http://www.impact-initiatives.org/) and [ACTED](http://www.acted.org/)) and the United Nations Operational Satellite Applications Programme ([UNOSAT](http://www.unitar.org/unosat/)). REACH’s **purpose** is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarter is based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support on its fields of intervention.

## **BACKGROUND ON MULTI-SECTOR NEEDS ASSESSMENT (MSNA)**

Over the past 10 years, REACH has established itself as a leader in the delivery of independent, crisis-wide Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessments (MSNAs). MSNAs respond directly to Grand Bargain commitments by providing impartial, unbiased, comprehensive, context-sensitive, and timely data to inform humanitarian decision-making. In doing so, MSNAs promote a shift in how humanitarian needs are measured and how response planning and prioritization decisions are made. MSNA data enables and promotes needs-based, evidence-based and people-centred decision making when it comes to aid. MSNAs are delivered on an annual cycle aligned with the Humanitarian Planning Cycle (HPC). IMPACT delivers approximately 20 MSNAs each year across some of the world’s most severe humanitarian crises. In 2026, IMPACT embarked on an exciting but ambitious journey to expand and improve the MSNA programme. The goal is to improve the resilience of the data and information system underpinning humanitarian aid policy by streamlining delivery of MSNAs, making them easier, faster and cheaper to deliver by 2028. Delivering on this agenda requires a scale-up of the Global MSNA Team, close coordination with country teams delivering MSNAs, and with our Global Data Team (GDT) based in Amman. This position is therefore based in our Regional Office in Amman.

### **We are currently looking for a Senior Research Officer to join the Global MSNA Team of the Research Systems Unit (RSU).**

**Title:** Senior Research Officer – Research and Development (MSNA)

**Location:** Amman, Jordan, with travel (up to 20% field deployment)

**Line management:** Reports to the MSNA Research and Development (R&D) Specialist; administratively hosted by the IMPACT/ACTED office in Amman

**Contract duration:** 12 months, with possibility of extension.

**Start date:** ASAP

## **POSITION PROFILE**

This position is situated within the Research Systems Unit (RSU) of the Global Programmes Section. Under the overall guidance of the Research Manager, the RSU supports the delivery of core, multi-sectoral research across IMPACT’s countries of operation. Reporting directly to the MSNA Research & Development (R&D) Specialist (based in Geneva), and working closely with the Global Data Team (GDT), the Senior Research Officer will lead and support various initiatives within the R&D workstream of the Global MSNA Team including, among others, MSNA toolkits and methods, the Multi-Sector Needs Index (MSNI), cross-crisis analysis, mortality & nutrition data modules, and digitalization of workflows.

The position is based in Amman in order to keep methodological development close to the responses where MSNAs are implemented at the largest scale, and to strengthen day-to-day technical support to country teams in the region.

## **FUNCTION & RESPONSIBILITIES**

The SAO will support the below core areas of work:

***MSNA toolkit and methods***

- Lead the update of the MSNA sectoral indicator guidance, in coordination with sectoral specialists, and including making guidance notes fit for a public audience.
- Lead the development of the clean dataset template and the analysis tables template, taking account of the capacity of lower-resourced country teams.
- Contribute to the update of the MSNA Global Indicator Bank, the Data Analysis Plan (DAP) template, the KoBo template and checker, and the MSNA sampling guidance, including making relevant resources public.
- Support the coherence and interoperability of the toolkit across the research cycle, and its adaptation for external audiences and partner organisations.
- Fill in the gaps of the toolkit by developing additional resources, as needed.

***MSNA and cross-crisis analysis***

- Develop a revamped Multi-Sector Needs Index (MSNI) guidance note, fit for external audiences, sharing it with other MSNA producers and supporting its uptake.
- Contribute to MSNI lessons learned from the 2026 cycle, any revisions to the framework, and support its presentation to external stakeholders.
- Support the production of cross-crisis analysis, including the consolidation and standardization of large country datasets and the processing of related documentation on data collection and sampling methods across countries.
- Contribute to global MSNA analysis products – quantitative analysis to identify key global trends and findings, and the production of short briefs, dashboards or other similar products for global audiences.
- Support external engagement with global stakeholders, donors and other REACH partners on MSNI and cross-crisis findings, including website articles, webinars and similar activities.

***Digitalization, automation and country support***

- Work with the R&D Specialist and the Global Data Team on reusable analysis pipelines, the consolidated R package environment (including *humind*), and the specification of the MSNA Explorer.
- Contribute to the automation of repetitive MSNA workflows, including support for review of minimum requirements and tool checks.
- Provide technical support and guidance to REACH MSNA country teams at various stages of the research cycle, including research design and sampling methodologies; data collection planning; data processing, cleaning and management; quantitative data analysis; and the reporting and dissemination of inter-sectoral findings.
- Provide ad hoc surge support including country deployment up to 20% – remotely and/or through a field deployment, depending on the extent of support required and the specific needs of the country team.
- Contribute technical content to the Training and Certification Programme, in particular on indicator selection and analysis.

***Country support and quality assurance (approx. 30%)***

- Act as HQ focal point for several MSNA countries according to the MSNA team split per MSNA Cycle. This will involve: monthly check-ins, ad-hoc support throughout the full research cycle ensuring country teams have the resources needed to produce high-quality data and analysis, document reviews, and reporting progress and challenges through the MSNA Info Tracker & HQ MSNA meetings, and proactively flagging issues to the wider MSNA team.
- Support in facilitation of the MSNA CoP and maintaining of the MSNA FAQ and intranet hub.
- Review country outputs against the MSNA minimum requirements at each phase of the cycle – Terms of Reference (ToRs) , Data Anaysis Plans (DAPs), KOBO tools, clean datasets, analysis, MSNI frameworks and bulletins – in coordination with the research quality assurance (RQ) and sectoral (STU) units.

***Key deliverables in the first 12 months***

- Lead the revision and publication of key MSNA toolkit components, including sectoral guidance notes, technical templates and resources, ensuring coherence, usability, and accessibility for both REACH and external MSNA producers.
- Under the guidance of the R&D Specialist, prioritise and implement any methodological revisions to the MSNI Analytical framework, develop internal and external guidance & training materials to support the establishment and implementation of a standardized analytical framework and delivery of key metrics by country teams for the 2027 cycle.
- Support the R&D Specialist with the development, documentation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of a data pipeline that consolidates, harmonizes, validates, and processes MSNA datasets from multiple countries, enabling efficient comparative analysis, global reporting, including year-on-year trends analysis, and integration with the web-based MSNA Explorer.
- Advance the automation of key MSNA workflows, in particular the MSNI, and provide technical support to country teams throughout the research cycle, including research design, sampling, data management, analysis, and reporting, while contributing technical content to the MSNA Training and Certification Programme.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- Excellent academic qualifications, including Master's degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. development, humanitarian studies, international relations, research methods, social sciences, statistics).
- At least 2 years of experience in the humanitarian sector and/or field-based roles in fragile or development contexts.
- Experience with designing and implementing primary research, in particular large-scale quantitative surveys and/or humanitarian needs assessments.
- Solid understanding of statistical concepts and methods, including sampling.
- Advanced proficiency in R and/or Python for data processing, analysis and reproducible workflows is required for this position; familiarity with version control (Git) and with R package development is a strong asset (please share any public accounts (e.g., Github) with us in your CV).
- Experience developing, testing or otherwise working with multidimensional indices based on quantitative data to summarize multiple data points into easily digestible information an asset.
- Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting, including the ability to explain methodological choices to non-technical audiences.
- Ability to translate programmatic requirements into clear and technically feasible specifications, and to effectively bridge programmatic needs and technical implementation, in collaboration with the Global Data Team and under the R&D Specialist.
- Strong interpersonal skills, including good external engagement and coordination skills.
- Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility.
- Ability and willingness to engage in short term field deployments, including to complex and challenging security environments.
- Fluency in English required; proficiency in Arabic, French, or Spanish an asset.
- Familiarity with the humanitarian system and global humanitarian policy frameworks, in particular the Grand Bargain, the HPC and the JIAF.
- Experience with mortality and/or nutrition survey methods (e.g. SMART) an asset.
- Prior experience leading the design or implementation of MSNAs an asset.
- Familiarity with GIS principles and experience using GIS software an asset (e.g., ArcGIS, R, and/or QGIS).
- Ability to operate InDesign, a strong plus.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 2’580 CHF and 2’640 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.

jobs.title: Senior Corporate Development Officer
jobs.description:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

Reporting to the Senior Director, Corporate Partnerships, the Senior Corporate Development Officer is responsible for developing corporate partnerships in support of Habitat for Humanity International's (HFHI) mission. The Senior Corporate Development Officer is responsible for identifying, securing, and cultivating corporate partnerships, while also stewarding and expanding existing relationships to deepen engagement and grow support of HFHI's mission. This position will work closely with resource development leadership and key HFHI program stakeholders to maximize fundraising opportunities primarily through strategic partnership with Fortune 500 companies and other major corporations headquartered as assigned. This role will manage a portfolio of prospects representing a revenue range from $5-$10 million annually.

**Key Responsibilities:**

At Habitat for Humanity International, we believe everyone deserves a decent place to live. Reporting to the Senior Director, Corporate Partnerships, the **Senior Corporate Development Officer** will play a key role in advancing Habitat's mission by securing and growing strategic corporate partnerships that generate critical funding and engagement opportunities. This role leads the development, cultivation, and stewardship of corporate partnerships, with a primary focus on Fortune 500 companies and other major corporations.

**Why This Role Matters**

Through strategic relationship building and revenue generation, this role helps expand Habitat's ability to create housing opportunities and strengthen communities. The Senior Corporate Development Officer will manage a portfolio generating approximately $5-$10 million annually while helping position Habitat for long-term growth through innovative, mission-aligned corporate partnerships.

**What You'll Do**

- Develop and execute corporate partnership strategies aligned with partner business objectives and Habitat's mission.
- Identify, cultivate, solicit, and secure new corporate partnerships.
- Grow and steward an existing portfolio of corporate partners to increase engagement, revenue, and long-term impact.
- Build diverse funding streams through corporate philanthropy, sponsorships, employee engagement, workplace giving, cause marketing, gifts-in-kind, and programmatic support.
- Lead collaboration efforts with Habitat Area Offices to coordinate, pursue, and strengthen corporate partnerships.
- Facilitate partnership planning, strategy discussions, proposal development, and donor stewardship activities across Habitat's network.
- Develop compelling presentations, proposals, and partnership opportunities that align corporate social responsibility objectives with Habitat's funding priorities.
- Negotiate partnership agreements in collaboration with internal legal and finance teams.
- Serve as the primary relationship manager for key corporate partners and prospects.
- Work closely with Resource Development colleagues, affiliate leaders, and program teams to maximize partnership opportunities and deliver exceptional partner experiences.
- Track partnership performance, maintain accurate CRM records, prepare revenue forecasts, and provide pipeline and stewardship reporting.
- Mentor and support team members, sharing expertise and fostering collaboration across the organization.

**What You'll Bring**

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
- Minimum of 5 years of experience in fundraising, sales and/or prospect development.
- Demonstrated success securing complex six- and seven-figure multiyear commitments from Fortune 500 companies.
- Experience developing and managing partnership strategies.
- Ability to understand corporate priorities and build mutually beneficial partnership opportunities.
- Excellent communication, presentation, relationship-building, and negotiation skills.
- Strong project management, reporting, analytics, and organizational skills.
- Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a complex, matrixed environment.
- Highly collaborative, proactive, and solution-oriented approach.
- Strong attention to detail and commitment to excellent customer service.
- Proficiency with business software, databases, spreadsheets, and reporting tools.
- Ability to effectively manage organizational resources, including travel expenses.
- Strong problem-solving and strategic thinking capabilities.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Working knowledge of corporate social responsibility, sales, cause marketing, marketing, public relations, sponsorships, and employee engagement strategies.
- Experience using donor or constituent management systems, including Blackbaud CRM.
- Knowledge of and passion for Habitat for Humanity's global mission.

**What We Offer**

At Habitat for Humanity International, you'll join a mission-driven organization committed to creating impact through partnership, collaboration, and innovation. You'll have the opportunity to work alongside colleagues around the world, build meaningful corporate relationships, and help create lasting change for families and communities globally.

**Ready to help grow transformative corporate partnerships that expand access to affordable housing worldwide? Apply today and bring your expertise, creativity, and collaboration skills to a global organization dedicated to building a world where everyone has a decent place to live.**

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$97,300.00 USD

\-

$144,775 USD

/

Annual

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

jobs.description:
## About the Organization

"Be Aware And Share" (BAAS) is an independent non-profit organization that supports people in need and contributes to social inclusion. Founded in September 2015 in Basel (Switzerland), BAAS primarily focuses on supporting people on the move in Europe. In addition to material and social support as well as educational and recreational opportunities for displaced people, BAAS also carries out awareness-raising and information activities in Switzerland. At the moment, the organization is mainly focusing on supporting refugees in Ioannina in Northwestern Greece at its Community Center. The activities are carried out by volunteers and are financed exclusively by donations. BAAS is a politically and religiously independent organization.

## Positions

We are looking for two new members to join our Executive Board who are passionate about solidarity with people on the move and keen to participate in shaping a dynamic grassroots NGO. The new members will be part of the Executive Board along with the other board members. Board Members work with various professionals in the organization to ensure that BAAS achieves its annual goals and will continue to build a network of supporters to work towards our vision of a peaceful, solidary and mutually inclusive society. We are looking for experienced professionals to take the organization forward by overseeing the operational, financial and technical aspects of Be Aware And Share. The positions are voluntary and require approximately 8 hours of work per week. A minimum commitment of 1 year is expected. The board member will work remotely but is expected to visit BAAS’ Community Center in Ioannina, Greece. The Executive Board is willing to revise the division of responsibilities within the board. However, we are specifically looking for individuals who have a solid background in public relations and project management.

## Overall Responsibilities

● Lead the strategic and executive bodies of the organization

● Coordinate and lead quarterly, and annual operational reviews and periodic forecast updates

● Provide leadership and manage the efforts of all active association members and ensure appropriate support

● Ensure that activities are informed by a resource-based approach through direct contact with working groups

● Represent the organization in Swiss and other humanitarian networks

## Specific Responsibilities PR

● Overviewing the activities of the PR Working Group

● Project management and collaboration on the rebranding process for the digital and graphic identity

● Developing a communication strategy and ensuring its implementation

● Collaboration with the other Working Group on various projects throughout the year
