jobs.title: Chargé(e) de projet national(e) – Haïti, Amérique latine et Caraïbes
jobs.company: Geneva Centre for Security Sector Governance
jobs.description:
Au DCAF, nous envisageons un monde où la gouvernance démocratique du secteur de la sécurité favorise une paix et un développement durables ainsi que la dignité humaine pour tous.

Notre mission est de promouvoir la sécurité de tous grâce à des réformes du secteur de la sécurité inclusives, participatives et menées à l'échelle nationale, fondées sur les normes et les bonnes pratiques internationales.

Le DCAF contribue à rendre la paix et le développement plus durables en aidant les États partenaires et les acteurs internationaux qui les soutiennent à améliorer la gouvernance de leur secteur de la sécurité à travers des réformes inclusives et participatives. Il développe des outils et analyses innovants, encourage l’adoption de normes et de bonnes pratiques, fournit des conseils juridiques et politiques et soutient le renforcement des capacités des acteurs étatiques et non étatiques du secteur de la sécurité.

Les activités de l'entité Afrique et Amériques du DCAF dans la région Amérique latine et Caraïbes (LAC) visent à soutenir les gouvernements, les parlements, les institutions de sécurité et la société civile en renforçant les capacités et en promouvant les normes et les bonnes pratiques, afin de contribuer à un secteur de la sécurité plus efficace, efficient et transparent, soumis à un contrôle approprié des autorités compétentes, à l'écoute des populations et responsable devant elles.

Afin de renforcer nos activités dans la région LAC, nous recherchons une personne engagée et dynamique pour le poste suivant :

**Chargé(e) de projet national(e) – Haïti, Amérique latine et Caraïbes**

**Lieu : Port-au-Prince, Haïti**

**Date d'entrée en fonction : dès que possible, sous réserve de financement**

**Taux d'activité : 100 %**

**Durée : Contrat à durée déterminée de 12 mois, avec possibilité de prolongation**

**Le poste**

Ce poste joue un rôle essentiel dans la mise en œuvre d'une intervention visant à établir une unité de coordination au sein de la Police nationale d'Haïti (PNH), afin de rationaliser l'aide extérieure et la coordination interne associée. Pour inscrire l'appui à la PNH dans le système de sécurité au sens large et favoriser les synergies avec les initiatives connexes, le projet prévoit également des ateliers techniques et des formations.

La personne titulaire du poste apporte un appui transversal au conseiller international intégré à la cellule de coordination de la PNH (Bureau de Coordination Conjointe – BCC). En étroite coordination avec le siège du DCAF, elle soutient également la mise en œuvre globale du projet, notamment la planification, la réalisation et le compte rendu des ateliers, formations et activités de renforcement des capacités.

**Principaux domaines d'activité**

**Analyse du contexte et conseils**

- Fournir en continu des analyses politiques, des conseils sur le contexte local (notamment sur l'évolution de la situation sécuritaire) et des orientations culturelles au conseiller international et au siège du DCAF.
- Suivre l'environnement opérationnel local et fournir des analyses pour orienter les activités du projet.

**Appui à la mise en œuvre du projet**

- Mener des recherches documentaires ciblées et rédiger des notes d'analyse pour soutenir le travail du conseiller et la mise en œuvre globale du projet.
- Participer aux événements pertinents et en rendre compte conformément aux objectifs définis au préalable.
- Organiser des événements et ateliers stratégiques afin de favoriser les synergies entre les initiatives internationales d'appui au secteur de la sécurité.
- Soutenir les activités plus larges du DCAF en Haïti en identifiant de nouvelles possibilités d'intervention et en contribuant à la conception de nouvelles activités ou de nouveaux projets, en étroite coordination avec le siège du DCAF et le conseiller international.
- Rédiger les principaux livrables du projet, les concepts d'activités spécifiques, les termes de référence, les protocoles d'accord, les conventions, les synthèses contextuelles et les présentations ; collaborer au besoin avec des spécialistes et des consultants.
- Contribuer à la conception, à la planification et à la réalisation des activités de suivi, d'évaluation, de redevabilité et d'apprentissage (MEAL) ; rédiger les rapports du projet en veillant à leur qualité et à leur remise dans les délais fixés.
- Fournir, selon les besoins, un appui administratif souple pour assurer la bonne exécution du projet, notamment en gérant les aspects logistiques, administratifs et de communication liés aux ateliers, formations et missions du DCAF en Haïti (y compris la préparation des ordres du jour et la prise de notes officielles lors des réunions et événements).
- Contribuer au suivi financier des activités et au contrôle du budget.

**Qualifications, compétences et expérience requises**

- Diplôme universitaire de niveau avancé (master ou équivalent) en relations internationales, sciences politiques, études de sécurité, droits humains, droit, études du développement, études des conflits ou domaine connexe.
- La nationalité haïtienne ou un permis de travail valable en Haïti au moment de la candidature est une condition préalable.
- Une parfaite maîtrise professionnelle du français et du créole haïtien, à l'oral comme à l'écrit, est requise. La maîtrise de l'anglais constitue un atout important.
- Au moins trois ans d'expérience professionnelle pertinente dans la coopération internationale ou la gestion de projets, idéalement dans la gouvernance/réforme du secteur de la sécurité (GSS/RSS), l'état de droit ou les droits humains.
- Bonne connaissance démontrée de la gouvernance du secteur de la sécurité, des enjeux liés aux droits humains et du contexte institutionnel et politique en Haïti, notamment grâce à des contacts établis et à une expérience auprès d'acteurs étatiques et non étatiques variés (société civile, médias, institution du Médiateur).
- Compétences avérées en gestion de projets et en recherche ; solides capacités d'appui administratif et maîtrise de la suite Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
- Excellentes capacités d'organisation et de planification, aptitude démontrée à gérer des priorités concurrentes, à travailler sous pression et à respecter des délais serrés.
- Personnalité dynamique, autonome et proactive, capable de travailler de manière indépendante avec un minimum de supervision.
- Excellentes compétences relationnelles et de communication, avec une capacité démontrée à établir et entretenir des relations de travail efficaces dans une équipe multiculturelle évoluant à un rythme soutenu.

**Nous offrons**

- Une expérience professionnelle enrichissante, dynamique et porteuse de sens
- L’occasion de rejoindre une équipe diversifiée, collaborative, respectueuse, engagée et animée par des valeurs communes
- La possibilité de contribuer à renforcer la sécurité de toutes et tous grâce à des réformes du secteur de la sécurité prises en charge au niveau national, inclusives et participatives, fondées sur les normes internationales et les bonnes pratiques

jobs.title: Oficial de Cadena de Suministro - Guasdualito (Republicado)
jobs.description:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Cadena de Suministro** altamente calificado con sede en **Guasdualiuto, Edo. Apure.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**Descripción del propósito / objetivo del cargo:**

El Oficial de Cadena de Suministro es responsable de todas las adquisiciones de bienes y servicios, almacenamiento, transporte de bienes y personas, gestión de flotas de vehículos y apoyo logístico general al programa general en Apure de conformidad con el marco interno de Danish Refugee Council – DRC y las regulaciones impuestas por los donantes.

**Responsabilidades:**

**COMPRAS**

- Asegurar el cumplimiento de los procesos de compra requeridos para el adecuado funcionamiento de las operaciones de DRC en Apure.
- Colaboración directa con los equipos de programa para la planificación local de las necesidades de compra y logísticas de los programas de DRC en Apure.
- Generar seguimiento y trazabilidad de las solicitudes de compra.
- Validar la integridad documental de los procesos según los requerimientos de los donantes.
- Contacto con proveedores para cotizaciones y evaluaciones de compras locales.
- Comunicación directa con proveedores relacionados con la entrega de insumos en los programas de DRC.
- Seguimiento a devoluciones o reclamaciones con proveedores.
- Preparación de solicitudes de pago para el trámite de los equipos de Finanzas de DRC.
- Cualquier otra tarea que le asigne el Gerente de Línea / Técnico.

**LOGÍSTICA**

- Asegurar la entrega oportuna de los materiales solicitados, teniendo en cuenta los procesos y tiempos establecidos por DRC.
- Control, registro y seguimiento de los activos fijos gestionados en la oficina local.
- Realizar inventarios y llevar el control detallado del inventario general de DRC.
- Garantizar la gestión de los servicios generales para los equipos de trabajo (alojamiento, personal, visitantes, oficinas, lugares de almacenamiento y seguridad).
- Implementar procesos de registro, control, seguimiento y verificación de elementos del programa asignados al personal y a los logísticos de la oficina.
- En colaboración con el Líder de equipo de Cadena de Suministro apoyar en la inducción al personal de la oficina sobre los procesos de DRC.
- Cualquier otra tarea que le asigne el Gerente de Línea / Técnico.

**GESTIÓN DE ALMACEN**

- Comprobar que todos los activos antiguos y nuevos estén correctamente registrados y etiquetados.
- Gestionar el inventario de suministros de oficina y consumibles.
- Monitorear y administrar las existencias según los procedimientos de almacenamiento de DRC.
- Preparar y revisar todos los informes mensuales de movimiento de inventario antes de enviarlos al Oficial de Cadena de Suministro para su validación.
- Recogida o entrega de mercancías.
- Asegurar que todos los artículos en el almacén estén correctamente almacenados, apilados y contabilizados con precisión en todo momento.

**GESTION DE LOTA**

- Asegurar el cumplimiento de los procesos de gestión de flota de DRC en Apure, Venezuela.
- Garantizar la disponibilidad de los vehículos para las operaciones de programa.
- Controlar el uso y consumo del servicio de transporte en la oficina local.

**ADMINISTRACIÓN**

- Participar y ayudar en la implementación del ERP (DRC Dynamics).
- Colaboración con la unidad de finanzas para el correcto registro de la cadena de abastecimiento.
- Coordinación con la unidad de finanzas para la oportuna ejecución de los pagos.
- Redacción de contratos y acuerdos marco para la operación local.

**Experiencias y competencias técnicas:**

- Al menos 2 años de experiencia laboral con una ONG internacional en un rol similar.
- Vocación de servicio.
- Enfoque al detalle.
- Capacidad de auto-organización.
- Motivación por el trabajo en el sector humanitario.
- Orientación de servicio a los programas.
- Conocimiento de sistemas de ERP para compras.
- Manejo Avanzado de OneDrive, MS Word, Excel y Adobe PDF.
- Capacidades analíticas.
- Orientación a la resolución de problemas.
- Capacidad de trabajo bajo incertidumbre.

**Educación (Incluir certificados, licencias)**

Profesional con 2 años de experiencia, Título Universitario pertinente en logística y / o gestión de la cadena de suministro o cualificación profesional equivalente.

**Idiomas:**
Fluidez en inglés ( Deseable )escrito y hablado

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda H.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**:

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Domingo 15 de noviembre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

**Fecha de inicio aproximada:** Noviembre 2026

jobs.title: Meal Field Assistant
jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**PROJECT**

Integrated Shelter, Food Security and Livelihoods Support for Safe, Dignified and Sustainable Return in Abul Thohur (Idleb) and Madiq Castle (Hama)

**DUTY STATION**

Idlib, Syria, with regular field visits to Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate, and other project locations as required

**ABOUT THE PROJECT**

IHH is implementing an integrated humanitarian and early-recovery project funded by the OCHA Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF), supporting safe, dignified and sustainable return in Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate.

The project combines shelter rehabilitation, winterization and Core NFI assistance, cash assistance for food, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread provision, agricultural support for returning wheat farmers, and rehabilitation of community irrigation infrastructure. These complementary interventions aim to address urgent household needs, restore essential infrastructure, protect agricultural livelihoods and strengthen community recovery.

**JOB SUMMARY**

IHH is seeking four MEAL Field Assistants to support the implementation of monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning activities across the project's target locations. Working under the guidance of the IHH MEAL Department, the postholders will conduct field data collection and monitoring, verify beneficiary and activity information, support post-distribution and post-implementation monitoring, document community feedback, and report findings in a timely and accurate manner.

The role involves frequent field visits across the project's multi-sector activities, including shelter rehabilitation, winterization and Core NFI assistance, cash-for-food assistance, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread provision, agricultural support, and irrigation infrastructure rehabilitation. MEAL Field Assistants will use approved tools and methods to collect reliable evidence, check data quality, and help ensure that affected people can safely access information and feedback channels.

The position requires strong attention to detail, impartiality, respectful communication, and strict adherence to informed consent, confidentiality, data protection, safeguarding and PSEA requirements. MEAL Field Assistants support field-level monitoring and data collection under the MEAL team's guidance; they do not independently change project targeting, make programme decisions, or investigate sensitive complaints.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Field Monitoring and Data Collection

- Conduct regular field monitoring visits to project locations in Abul Thohur and Madiq Castle in accordance with the approved MEAL plan, documenting activity progress, implementation quality, access constraints and emerging issues.
- Collect quantitative and qualitative data using approved methods and tools, including KoboToolbox or other digital data-collection platforms, structured questionnaires, observation checklists and approved monitoring forms.
- Support distribution monitoring and post-distribution monitoring (PDM) for cash assistance, winterization, Core NFI and food assistance, including beneficiary interviews and verification of whether assistance was received safely and as intended.
- Support monitoring of shelter rehabilitation, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread activities, agricultural support and irrigation infrastructure works by collecting field observations and beneficiary feedback, without replacing technical inspections or engineering certification.
- Participate in baseline, endline, post-implementation monitoring, market monitoring, needs assessments and other data-collection exercises as assigned by the MEAL Officer.
- Conduct key informant interviews (KIIs), focus group discussions (FGDs) and household surveys when assigned and trained, ensuring that questions are asked consistently and responses are recorded accurately.
- Report delays, access constraints, implementation gaps, safeguarding concerns and other issues through the appropriate reporting lines without delay.

Data Quality and Documentation

- Check completed questionnaires and monitoring forms for completeness, consistency and accuracy before submission, and promptly flag missing data, anomalies, potential duplication or other discrepancies to the MEAL Officer.
- Use approved digital tools and data-collection protocols, including consent procedures, skip logic and validation rules, and seek guidance when a tool or question is unclear.
- Support first-level data cleaning, data entry, coding, verification and organization of quantitative and qualitative information using approved systems and templates.
- Maintain accurate and organized electronic and hard-copy MEAL records, including survey forms, field visit notes, monitoring checklists, attendance records and supporting evidence.
- Prepare clear field notes and concise monitoring updates, ensuring that findings are factual, traceable and submitted within agreed deadlines.
- Collect photographs or other supporting evidence only when authorized and appropriate, and in line with consent, safety and data-protection requirements.
- Support the compilation of indicator tracking information and reporting inputs by submitting complete, timely and verifiable field data to the MEAL team.

Accountability to Affected People and Feedback Mechanisms

- Inform beneficiaries and community members about available feedback and complaints channels and how to access them safely, including during field visits and monitoring exercises.
- Receive, record and refer feedback or complaints through IHH's approved Complaints and Response Mechanism (CRM), following the established procedures and confidentiality requirements.
- Escalate sensitive protection, safeguarding, fraud, corruption or sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) concerns immediately through designated reporting channels; do not investigate such cases independently or share details with unauthorized persons.
- Support follow-up and closure of feedback cases only as instructed by the responsible CRM or MEAL focal point, and contribute to communicating authorized responses to affected people where appropriate.
- Apply impartiality, non-discrimination, accessibility and do-no-harm principles, and report barriers that may prevent women, older persons, persons with disabilities or other vulnerable groups from participating safely.
- Coordination, Reporting and Learning
- Coordinate with the MEAL Officer and relevant programme and field teams to schedule monitoring visits and ensure safe, timely access to project locations, while maintaining the independence and impartiality of MEAL functions.
- Provide timely updates on completed monitoring activities, data-collection progress, field constraints, beneficiary feedback and issues requiring follow-up.

Contribute to periodic monitoring summaries, PDM reports, assessment findings, lessons learned and other reporting products using approved formats.

- Share evidence-based observations with the MEAL team to support corrective action, adaptive management and learning, while respecting confidentiality and need-to-know access.
- Support logistics for surveys, interviews, focus group discussions and monitoring visits, including coordination of appointments and preparation of approved tools and materials.
- Perform other related MEAL duties assigned by the supervisor, consistent with the role and project needs.
- REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE
- Bachelor's degree or diploma in Social Sciences, Statistics, Economics, Development Studies, Public Health, Information Management or another relevant field.
- At least 1–2 years of relevant experience in MEAL, monitoring and evaluation, field data collection, research or accountability activities, preferably with a humanitarian or development organization.

Experience working directly with conflict-affected, displaced or vulnerable communities in Syria is an advantage.

- Practical experience conducting field visits, household surveys, interviews, focus group discussions, beneficiary follow-up or post-distribution monitoring.
- Familiarity with digital data-collection tools such as KoboToolbox, ODK or equivalent platforms is an advantage.
- Basic working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word, and the ability to organize and check data accurately.
- Understanding of accountability to affected populations, feedback and complaints mechanisms, informed consent, confidentiality, data protection, safeguarding and PSEA principles.
- Ability to follow approved questionnaires and protocols, maintain impartiality, and report data-quality concerns accurately.
- Strong communication, interpersonal and organizational skills, with the ability to engage respectfully with diverse communities.
- Ability to work independently in the field, manage competing priorities and travel regularly to project locations in Abul Thohur and Madiq Castle.
- Fluency in Arabic, both written and spoken, is essential. Working knowledge of English is an advantage.Knowledge of Turkish is also an advantage.

**CORE COMPETENCIES**

- Field monitoring and accurate data collection.
- Data quality checks, verification and documentation.
- Beneficiary communication, accountability and safe referral of feedback.
- Use of digital data-collection tools and adherence to approved protocols.
- Confidentiality, impartiality and ethical engagement with affected people.
- Reporting, teamwork and timely escalation of issues.
- Attention to detail, organization and time management.
- Commitment to humanitarian principles, safeguarding, PSEA and data protection.
- WORKING CONDITIONS

The positions will be field-based, with regular travel to project locations in Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate, according to the approved MEAL plan and operational needs. The successful candidates must be willing and able to work regularly in the field and coordinate closely with the IHH MEAL Department, programme teams and affected communities.

**Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.**

jobs.title: Trainer and Editorial Mentor - Consultancy
jobs.description:
**Project**: Words That Protect: Gender-Responsive Media and Journalist Networks in Iraq

**Component:** Evidence-Based Gender-Responsive VAW Reporting

**Contract type:** Consultancy

**Location:** Remote, with required attendance at two project workshops in Baghdad and/or Erbil

**Assignment period:** November 2026 – April 2027

## **1. Background**

Words That Protect supports gender-responsive journalism and more responsible media coverage of violence against women in Iraq.

Under Component 2, the project will select and train 30 Iraqi journalists, with equal representation of women and men. Participants will form 15 mixed-gender teams, each consisting of one female and one male journalist, to produce and publish 15 stories addressing violence against women.

The training and production process will be informed by the findings of the project’s baseline media study and by the SEED and Silence and Omissions frameworks. Following the first in-person workshop, participants will enter a structured production and mentorship period covering story development, research, risk assessment, editorial review and publication. Each Trainer and Editorial Mentor will be responsible for supporting seven or eight journalist teams.

## **2. Purpose of the Assignment**

The Trainer and Editorial Mentor will contribute to participant selection, prepare and deliver the project training, and provide structured editorial mentorship to the assigned journalist teams throughout story development, research, production, revision and publication.

The Trainer and Editorial Mentor will support the teams in applying gender-responsive and survivor-centred reporting principles in practice. This includes reviewing story proposals and production plans, supporting the preparation of production budgets, managing the risk-assessment process, monitoring research and production, reviewing stories against the approved standards, and supervising the preparation and implementation of publication plans.

The participating journalists retain responsibility for conducting the research, producing the stories and completing the required revisions. The Trainer and Editorial Mentor leads the detailed editorial mentorship process, provides regular feedback and approves the teams’ submissions before they are delivered to the MiCT project team. MiCT maintains overall oversight of the project and reviews the key editorial and production deliverables.

### **Key Responsibilities**

1. Participate in the participant-selection process by evaluating applications and conducting interviews, with the support and under the management of the MiCT project team.
2. Prepare the required training materials covering the following main topics:
- Gender-responsive journalism principles.
- Survivor-centred approaches to reporting.
- Ethical and legal frameworks for reporting on violence against women in Iraq.
- Appropriate terminology in reporting on violence against women.

- Ethical interviewing practices.
- Ethical use of images and informed consent.
- Violence-against-women support services and safe referral pathways.
- Trauma-informed reporting methods.
- The practical application of the SEED and Silence and Omissions frameworks through reporting scenarios and editorial exercises based on the Iraqi context.

1. Adapt the training materials and mentorship methods in line with the SEED and Silence and Omissions frameworks and the preliminary findings of the study conducted by the MiCT team as part of the project.
2. Deliver the first in-person training workshop and facilitate its practical exercises and editorial activities.
3. Contribute to forming mixed-gender journalist teams, with each team consisting of one female and one male journalist.
4. Provide editorial mentorship to seven or eight journalist teams.
5. Review and approve the story topics and production plans developed by the assigned teams. Review and adjust the proposed production budgets and submit final copies of the story proposals and budgets approved by both the mentor and the participating journalists to the MiCT project team.
6. Manage the risk-assessment process for the assigned teams. Review and approve each team’s risk-assessment file and submit an approved copy to the MiCT project team before the team begins any fieldwork.
7. Closely supervise the research and story-production process and provide regular editorial mentorship. Ensure that each team maintains a complete and properly organised shared research file and task-tracking file.
8. Review each story against the approved standards, oversee the required revisions and grant final editorial approval. Submit the approved version to the MiCT project team by the agreed deadline. The review must ensure linguistic accuracy, factual accuracy, source verification, journalistic quality and integrity, and compliance with the methodological standards for sensitive reporting on gender-based violence.
9. Contribute to selecting publishing outlets and supervise the preparation and implementation of publication plans by the journalist teams. Submit the final publication plans approved by the mentor to the MiCT project team.
10. Update the team-performance tracking sheet monthly.
11. Attend periodic MiCT team meetings, maintain active communication and work in coordination with the project team.
12. Attend the closing workshop in Iraq, to be held in Baghdad or Erbil between the end of March and the beginning of April 2027.
13. Be available for interviews and complete the required evaluation forms.

### **Deliverables**

1. Training materials covering the agreed topics and adapted to the SEED and Silence and Omissions frameworks and the preliminary findings of the project study.
2. Final story proposals and production budgets approved by the mentor and participating journalists.
3. A risk-assessment file for each assigned team, approved by the mentor and submitted to the MiCT project team before the team begins fieldwork.
4. Final publication plans approved by the mentor.
5. Final versions of the journalistic stories approved by the mentor and submitted to the MiCT project team by the agreed deadline.
6. Monthly updates to the team-performance tracking sheet.
7. A progress report covering the period from the beginning of the mentorship phase until the completion of the publication process.

### **Required Qualifications**

1. Extensive professional journalism and editorial experience.
2. Previous experience in similar training, editorial mentorship or supported journalistic production assignments.
3. Demonstrated experience in gender-responsive journalism and survivor-centred journalism.
4. Broad and active professional networks within the media and journalism sector.
5. Experience training and mentoring journalists throughout the research, production, editorial review and publication process.
6. Strong editorial review, fact-checking, source-verification and risk-assessment skills.
7. Ability to manage and follow up with multiple journalist teams while maintaining organised documentation and meeting agreed deadlines.
8. Strong communication and teamwork skills.
9. Fluency in Arabic and sufficient professional English to work with the project frameworks and materials.
10. Previous experience in the Iraqi context, or in projects targeting Iraqi journalists and media institutions, is preferred.

jobs.title: Research Assistant - Consultancy
jobs.description:
**About the Role:**

MiCT is seeking a Research Assistant to support research and media monitoring activities in Iraq, with a particular focus on coverage of violence against women. The position will contribute to mapping and analysing Iraqi media coverage, supporting the development of research findings, and coordinating with trainers, mentors and project staff to integrate these findings into project activities.

**Level of Effort**

50 working days over the assignment period.

## **Key Responsibilities**

1. Monitor coverage of 5–7 cases of violence against women across Iraqi media outlets.
2. Compile a diverse and, as far as possible, comprehensive mapping of Iraqi media outlets and organisations.
3. Contribute to adapting the methodological frameworks under the supervision of the Head of Research.
4. Conduct manual research in Arabic to verify the completeness and breadth of the sample, in accordance with the parameters established by the Head of Research.
5. Participate in analysis and the development of research findings as needed.
6. Coordinate communication between the Head of Research, trainer and mentors to integrate the research findings into participant training.
7. Ensure that mentors and participants apply a consistent analytical framework based on the SEED Foundation guide during the development of their investigations, addressing framing, source selection, omissions, terminology, contextualisation, and survivor safety and privacy.
8. Coordinate with the M&E Coordinator to establish the research findings as a contextual baseline for evaluation and adapt the research content-analysis tool for assessing participant outputs through the peer review activity.
9. Support communication and coordination across project activities, including liaison with project staff, participants, trainers and mentors, follow-up on agreed actions, and coordination of activity arrangements, as required.

## **Required Qualifications**

1. A university degree in journalism, media studies, communication, social sciences, gender studies or a related field.
2. At least two years of relevant professional experience in research, media monitoring, journalism or media development.
3. Familiarity with the Iraqi media landscape and the range of outlets, ownership structures and audiences it comprises.
4. Strong Arabic-language research skills, including manual searches across media websites and social media platforms.
5. Experience in qualitative research or media content analysis.
6. Knowledge of gender-responsive journalism and ethical reporting on violence against women, including survivor safety and privacy.
7. Ability to apply analytical frameworks consistently and maintain organised, traceable research records.
8. Proficiency in spreadsheets and digital tools for organising and managing research data.
9. Strong analytical, organisational and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively within a diverse team.
10. Ability to handle sensitive information confidentially and responsibly.
11. Previous experience with MiCT would be considered an advantage.

## **Reporting and Coordination**

The Research Assistant will work under the supervision of the Head of Research and coordinate regularly with the project team.

Work will be carried out directly in the shared research files maintained by the Head of Research, with contributions and updates reviewed as part of ongoing supervision.

jobs.title: Writing Consultancy: Global Learning Report – Rollout of Gender Transformative and Conflict Sensitivity (GTCS) Guidelines

1. **The Rollout Process & Feedback:** How the guidelines were introduced, methodology of sensitization workshops, uptake by country offices and partners, and feedback collected from participants.
2. **Topline Initial Findings & Recommendations:** Key insights, operational challenges, adaptations made, and forward-looking recommendations distilled from individual country reports.

**Can you inspire visionary donors to make lifesaving healthcare possible when disaster strikes? Do you have what it takes to build a Major Donor Programme from scratch?**

UK-Med is a frontline medical aid charity founded on the values and expertise of the NHS. For more than 30 years, we have worked towards a world where everyone gets the healthcare they need when emergencies overwhelm local health services. We are verified by the World Health Organization as an Emergency Medical Team a global benchmark of quality and trust. Over the past five years, we have responded to 49 emergencies, often running multiple complex operations simultaneously.

We are looking for an exceptional, experienced Philanthropy and Partnerships relationship manager to help shape the next chapter of UK-Med’s growth by building and leading meaningful relationships with individuals, Trusts and Foundations, and companies who share our commitment to lifesaving humanitarian healthcare.

**This is a brand-new role for the organisation demonstrating our commitment to growing sustainable income from private sources and a real opportunity for a talented, resilient senior fundraiser to build a plan and portfolio almost from scratch.**

This is an exciting time to join us. Over the past 5 years, UK-Med has delivered healthcare to more than 1 million people in emergencies, while our voluntary income has grown significantly. We now want to build on that momentum by welcoming more philanthropists into our mission and creating thoughtful, lasting partnerships with the potential to transform our impact.

You will bring UK-Med’s work to life for current and prospective supporters, connecting their interests and ambitions with opportunities to make a meaningful difference. Working closely with our Director of Fundraising, CEO, trustees and senior colleagues, you will create inspiring opportunities for engagement and ensure every relationship is valued through thoughtful, personal stewardship.

We’re looking for an accomplished relationship fundraiser with experience of developing major donor, Trust, and corporate partnerships and securing significant multi-year income. You will be a compelling communicator and trusted relationship-builder, able to engage people with warmth, credibility and discretion while representing communities affected by humanitarian emergencies with care and dignity.

You’ll join a collaborative and creative Fundraising & Communications team at a pivotal point in UK-Med’s journey, with the opportunity to help philanthropy become an increasingly powerful and sustainable force behind our lifesaving work.

We offer competitive benefits, a friendly working environment and the opportunity to make a real difference through humanitarian work.

jobs.title: Especialista de Transferencias Monetarias - Caracas (Staff National)
jobs.description:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Especialista de Transferencia Monetaria** altamente calificado con sede en **Caracas, Venezuela.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL CARGO:**

El/la Especialista de Transferencias Monetarias brindará apoyo técnico a DRC Venezuela para la preparación, diseño, implementación y mejora continua de programas de asistencia basada en efectivo y cupones (Cash and Voucher Assistance – CVA) en diferentes sectores. La posición contribuirá a consolidar capacidades, herramientas y procesos que permitan implementar CVA de manera segura, basada en mercados, sensible a la protección y conforme a los procedimientos de DRC.

La posición trabajará de manera transversal con Programas, MERA, Finanzas, Supply Chain y equipos territoriales. De manera complementaria y según las prioridades de la operación, podrá apoyar análisis de mercados, inclusión financiera y otras iniciativas de recuperación económica relacionadas con la programación de CVA.

**PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILIDADES**

**Preparación, diseño y calidad técnica de CVA**

- Apoyar el desarrollo, contextualización y actualización de procedimientos, herramientas y flujos de trabajo para la implementación de programas de transferencias monetarias en DRC Venezuela.
- Contribuir al análisis de factibilidad y opciones de respuesta, considerando necesidades y preferencias de las personas participantes, funcionamiento de mercados, riesgos de protección y capacidad operacional.
- Apoyar el diseño de intervenciones de asistencia multipropósito y de transferencias monetarias o cupones vinculadas a objetivos sectoriales.
- Apoyar la definición y revisión de criterios de elegibilidad, mecanismos de registro y verificación, valores de transferencia y frecuencia de asistencia, en coordinación con los equipos técnicos.
- Brindar acompañamiento técnico y control de calidad a los equipos durante el diseño, lanzamiento, implementación, revisión y cierre de proyectos con componentes de CVA.
- Contribuir con insumos técnicos para notas concepto, propuestas, presupuestos, modificaciones e informes de proyectos que incorporen CVA.
- Identificar dificultades técnicas u operativas durante la implementación y acompañar a los equipos en la definición de medidas correctivas.

**Mercados, proveedores financieros y mecanismos de entrega**

- Apoyar y, cuando corresponda, liderar evaluaciones rápidas de mercado y ejercicios de monitoreo de precios, disponibilidad, acceso y capacidad de abastecimiento.
- Traducir los hallazgos de mercado en recomendaciones prácticas sobre modalidad, valor de transferencia, mecanismos de entrega y otras decisiones programáticas.
- Dar seguimiento al mapeo y análisis de proveedores de servicios financieros (FSP) y mecanismos de entrega desarrollados por DRC, actualizando la información cuando sea necesario.
- Dar seguimiento técnico al proceso de procurement de FSP, en coordinación con Supply Chain, Finanzas y Programas, y participar en la evaluación técnica de ofertas y selección del/de los proveedor(es), de acuerdo con los procedimientos de DRC y la segregación de funciones correspondiente.
- Apoyar el establecimiento y prueba de arreglos operativos con el/los FSP seleccionados, incluyendo listas de pago, intercambio seguro de información, confirmación de pagos, pagos fallidos, reintentos, reporting y reconciliación.
- Dar seguimiento al desempeño de los mecanismos de entrega e identificar ajustes para mejorar seguridad, accesibilidad, eficiencia y experiencia de las personas participantes.
- Identificar barreras de acceso financiero y oportunidades de inclusión financiera relacionadas con las poblaciones atendidas.

**Monitoreo, protección y rendición de cuentas**

- Trabajar con MERA para incorporar CVA en evaluaciones, indicadores, monitoreo, PDM y ejercicios de aprendizaje, y asegurar que los hallazgos informen ajustes programáticos.
- Trabajar con Protección para identificar y mitigar riesgos relacionados con modalidad, acceso, exclusión, fraude, seguridad, protección de datos y salvaguardas.
- Promover mecanismos accesibles de información, participación, retroalimentación y quejas para las personas participantes.
- Promover la consideración de género, edad, discapacidad, diversidad, protección y acceso seguro y digno a lo largo del ciclo de CVA.

**Fortalecimiento de capacidades y aprendizaje**

- Identificar necesidades de fortalecimiento de capacidades de los equipos de DRC en CVA y programación basada en mercados.
- Desarrollar y facilitar capacitaciones, coaching, ejercicios de simulación y acompañamiento práctico durante la implementación.
- Mantener organizado y actualizado un repositorio básico de SOP, herramientas, lineamientos y materiales técnicos relevantes para CVA.
- Documentar y compartir buenas prácticas, retos y lecciones aprendidas para favorecer la continuidad y mejora de la programación.

**Coordinación y apoyo complementario de recuperación económica**

- Representar a DRC, según delegación, en espacios técnicos relevantes para CVA y asistencia basada en mercados como el Grupo de Asistencia Basada en Mercados (GABM), y contribuir a análisis, herramientas y recomendaciones conjuntas.
- Mantener coordinación con recursos técnicos regionales y globales de DRC y aplicar lineamientos y estándares relevantes al contexto de Venezuela.
- De manera complementaria y según las prioridades de la operación, apoyar análisis de mercados, inclusión financiera y otras iniciativas de recuperación económica vinculadas o no con CVA.

**Experiencia y competencias:**

- Mínimo 3 años de experiencia profesional relevante en programas humanitarios, sociales o de desarrollo en contextos o con poblaciones afectadas por crisis, desplazamiento o vulnerabilidad socioeconómica.
- Experiencia en una o más áreas relevantes para CVA, como análisis de mercados, seguridad alimentaria, recuperación económica, medios de vida, inclusión financiera, banca o pagos digitales, protección social, focalización de participantes, MERA/gestión de información o asistencia en efectivo.
- Capacidad analítica para interpretar información de necesidades, mercados, servicios financieros o monitoreo y convertirla en recomendaciones operacionales.
- Capacidad para trabajar de manera transversal con equipos programáticos y áreas de soporte, facilitando procesos y acuerdos entre distintas funciones.
- Buenas habilidades de comunicación, facilitación, organización, coordinación y resolución de problemas.
- Conocimiento del contexto venezolano y sensibilidad frente a riesgos de protección, acceso y exclusión.

**Se valorará especialmente**

- Experiencia previa en programas de transferencias monetarias y/o cupones, aunque no es requisito excluyente.
- Conocimiento de estándares, metodologías o herramientas de CVA y programación basada en mercados.
- Experiencia trabajando con proveedores de servicios financieros, sistemas de pago, servicios bancarios, remesas, microfinanzas o mecanismos digitales.
- Formación o certificaciones en CVA, análisis de mercados, inclusión financiera, MERA, protección social, seguridad alimentaria, gestión de proyectos u otras áreas relacionadas.

**Education**

- Título universitario en economía, ciencias sociales, desarrollo, administración, relaciones internacionales, finanzas, ingeniería, u otras disciplinas relevantes.

**Languages**

- Español fluido, oral y escrito.
- Conocimiento intermedio/avanzado de inglés será considerado una ventaja, particularmente para acceder a lineamientos y recursos técnicos globales.

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda G**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**:

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

jobs.title: Field Finance Officer
jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**PROJECT**

Integrated Shelter, Food Security and Livelihoods Support for Safe, Dignified and Sustainable Return in Abul Thohur (Idleb) and Madiq Castle (Hama)

**DUTY STATION**

Idlib, Syria, with regular field visits to Abul Thohur and Madiq Castle

**REPORTS TO**

Finance Department, IHH Gaziantep Office

**PROJECT DURATION**

1 October 2026 – 30 September 2027

**ABOUT THE PROJECT**

IHH is implementing an integrated humanitarian and early recovery project in Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate. The project combines shelter rehabilitation, winterization and core NFI assistance, cash-for-food assistance, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread, agricultural support to wheat farmers, and rehabilitation of community irrigation infrastructure.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Field Finance Officer will support the day-to-day financial administration and control of project activities in the field, coordinating closely with the IHH Procurement Department and the Finance Department at the IHH Gaziantep Office. The role focuses on reviewing payment documentation, maintaining accurate financial records, supporting timely payments and advances, tracking expenditures, and ensuring that transactions comply with IHH procedures and donor rules.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Financial Transactions and Documentation**

**·** Review payment requests, invoices, receipts, claims, purchase orders, contracts, and other supporting documents for completeness, accuracy, and appropriate authorization before processing.

**·** Support the processing and documentation of approved payments, cash advances, per diems, and other project-related expenses in accordance with IHH procedures.

**·** Maintain well-organized financial files and transaction registers, ensuring that all supporting documents are properly coded, filed, and readily available for review.

**·** Verify that expenses are recorded against the correct project, budget line, and activity, and promptly follow up on missing or inconsistent documentation.

**Cash Management and Reconciliation**

**·** Maintain accurate records of cash received and disbursed, where applicable, and safeguard cash and financial documents in line with IHH cash-handling procedures.

**·** Track cash advances and ensure that they are liquidated within the required deadlines, following up with staff and activity teams on outstanding balances.

**·** Support regular cash counts, reconciliations, and checks of financial records, reporting any discrepancies to the Finance Manager.

**Budget Monitoring and Reporting**

**·** Maintain project expenditure trackers and support periodic budget-versus-actual reviews in coordination with the Finance Manager and Project Manager.

**·** Flag unusual expenses, potential overspending, underspending, or other variances and provide accurate supporting information for follow-up.

**·** Contribute to periodic financial reports, expenditure forecasts, payment plans, and other financial information requested by the Finance Manager.

**·** Support audit preparation and internal or donor financial reviews by retrieving and organizing complete records and supporting documentation.

**Programme and Field Coordination**

**·** Coordinate closely with the IHH Procurement Department and the Finance Department at the IHH Gaziantep Office, as well as programme, logistics, and field teams, to clarify procurement and payment requirements, verify supporting documents, and facilitate the timely processing of approved transactions.

**·** Support financial documentation and field-level verification related to project activities, including shelter rehabilitation, cash assistance, food assistance, bakery support, agricultural activities, and irrigation rehabilitation, as assigned.

**·** Ensure that beneficiary- or supplier-related financial records are handled confidentially and shared only with authorized personnel.

**·** Immediately report suspected fraud, irregular transactions, conflicts of interest, or breaches of financial procedures through the appropriate IHH reporting channels.

**Compliance and Other Duties**

**·** Comply with IHH financial policies, internal controls, anti-fraud and anti-corruption requirements, safeguarding standards, and applicable donor rules.

**·** Maintain accurate, up-to-date, and auditable financial records, both electronically and in hard copy where required.

**·** Perform other finance-related duties assigned by the Finance Manager that are consistent with the position and project needs.

**Qualifications and Experience**

**·** Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field.

**·** At least two years of relevant experience in finance, accounting, or financial administration; experience with an NGO or humanitarian organization is an advantage.

**·** Practical experience reviewing payment documents, maintaining financial records, handling advances, and supporting reconciliations.

**·** Good knowledge of Microsoft Excel and other MS Office applications; experience with accounting or financial management systems is an advantage.

**·** Good understanding of internal controls, supporting-document requirements, and the importance of compliance with organizational procedures and donor rules.

**Skills and Competencies**

**·** High accuracy, attention to detail, and strong organizational skills.

**·** Integrity and ability to handle financial information with discretion and confidentiality.

**·** Good communication and coordination skills, with the ability to work effectively with programme and operations colleagues.

**·** Ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and work under pressure.

**·** Fluency in Arabic and a good working knowledge of English are required; Turkish is an advantage.

**·** Willingness to travel regularly to project locations in Abul Thohur and Madiq Castle.

**Application Note**

IHH is committed to safeguarding, accountability, equal opportunity, and the prevention of fraud, exploitation, and abuse. The selected candidate will be expected to comply with IHH policies and code of conduct.

jobs.title: Head of Programmes
jobs.description:
The Head of Programmes will play a key role in shaping and strengthening SEED’s programme portfolio, providing leadership, management oversight and technical guidance to our international Programme Managers. The role will support teams to develop and deliver high-quality, impactful programmes that respond to community priorities, reflect good international practice and contribute to SEED’s strategic objectives and commitment to community-led development.

Working across SEED’s programme portfolio, the role will connect international Programme Managers with national Heads of Department and the Director of Programmes and Operations, strengthening collaboration and ensuring that programmes benefit from shared learning and expertise. The Head of Programmes will provide senior oversight while creating space for innovation, reflection and continuous improvement, helping teams to deliver programmes that are effective, responsive and ambitious in their impact.

The postholder will be a programme professional with five to eight years of international development programme design and delivery experience, able to provide practical advice whilst creating a supportive and positive management environment for international Programme Managers.

Candidates without programme management, people management and grant writing experience will not be considered for the post.

This is a new post for our expanding team and is therefore for a six-month period and, after review, has the potential to extend. It is paid at a local salary, with a contribution to flights of £1,200 and insurance of up to £650.

## Key responsibilities

- Provide oversight to SEED’s programmes across Community Health, Education, WASH, Sustainable Livelihoods and Conservation, ensuring an integrated and coherent approach to programme delivery.
- Work closely with Programme Managers, providing expert advice and constructive challenge to ensure programmes are well designed, appropriately resourced and delivered to a high standard in line with SEED’s strategic objectives, policies and values.
- Review programme plans, budgets, proposals, reports and other key programme documentation, providing guidance and quality assurance where required.
- Maintain an overview of programme performance, identifying emerging issues, opportunities, gaps and areas requiring additional management attention.
- Ensure that programmes respond appropriately to community priorities and feedback and remain relevant to changing needs and circumstances.
- Lead on the oversight of SEED’s programme development pipeline, ensuring that future programme opportunities are identified and developed sufficiently in advance of existing projects ending.
- Provide oversight into project budgets, ensuring that financial and narrative reporting is accurate, timely and of a high standard.
- Identify opportunities for programmes to complement and strengthen one another and encourage integrated approaches across SEED’s programme portfolio.
- Provide high-quality line management to SEED’s international Programme Managers through regular supervision, ongoing performance review, annual appraisal and supportive professional development.
- Provide additional management and programme capacity where required to cover staffing gaps or periods of increased workload, ensuring continuity and quality of programme delivery.
- Build a positive, collaborative and accountable team culture in which Programme Managers feel supported while taking ownership of their programmes and responsibilities.
- Work closely with Programme Managers and the MEL Coordinator to ensure that programmes are designed with appropriate monitoring, evaluation and learning processes.
- Ensure that evidence, learning and community feedback are actively used to adapt programmes and inform decision-making.
- Work closely with Malagasy Heads of Department to ensure effective collaboration between international Programme Managers and Malagasy colleagues and that programmes draw appropriately on local knowledge and expertise.
- Work closely with the Director of Programmes and Operations to ensure that SEED’s programmes continually develop in line with organisational strategy, evidence and community feedback.
- Where appropriate, represent SEED’s programmes to donors, partners and other external stakeholders.
- Ensure all of SEED’s policies and procedures are evident throughout the work of the department, including those for safeguarding, whistleblowing and anti-corruption, and undertake continual training to ensure these are promoted at all times

## Person specification

## Experience and qualifications

- At least a first-degree-level qualification or equivalent professional experience in international development or a related discipline.
- Minimum of five years' professional experience in programme management in the Global South.
- Minimum of three years' experience in grant writing, with a proven record of successful funding applications.
- Minimum of five years' professional experience in line management, including supervising, reviewing and mentoring international staff.
- Experience of living and working in the Global South, with the ability and desire to work effectively with teams from different economic and cultural backgrounds and across multiple language barriers.

## Technical and professional skills

- Sound knowledge of international development frameworks and contemporary global issues facing countries in the Global South.
- Familiarity with programme and project management tools, including logical frameworks, Theory of Change models, budgets, activity plans and monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) frameworks.
- Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills, with a demonstrable ability to gather, assess and assimilate facts and data from a range of sources and use these to inform decisions.
- Proven ability to recognise and appropriately manage challenging situations and find practical solutions.
- High degree of written and spoken English, with the ability to edit and produce high-quality English-language documents for donors and publication.
- French language skills to at least B2 level would be highly desirable.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
- Ability to work to tight deadlines in an organised manner and to a consistently high standard.

## Staff management, support and development

- Ability and desire to build capacity within both international and national teams, supporting colleagues to develop their skills and professional confidence.
- Excellent listening and verbal communication skills, combined with a flexible, patient and supportive approach to managing people.
- Ability to provide clear guidance, advice and support to colleagues in relation to SEED's ethos, policies and procedures, helping to protect their safety and the reputation of the organisation.
- Ability to support staff to develop the professional and social attitudes required for living and working in another country and, where necessary, to manage and address aspects of staff behaviour appropriately.
- Demonstrable awareness of and comfort with increased social and professional responsibility, including the ability to exercise sound judgement when supporting and managing others.

## Cross-cultural working

- Strong cross-cultural negotiation skills, with curiosity about and respect for effective ways of working in different cultural contexts.
- Cultural sensitivity and respect, with the ability to build positive and effective working relationships across cultural, economic and professional differences.
- Ability and desire to work collaboratively across multiple language and cultural contexts and to support effective communication between international and national colleagues.

## Communication, teamwork and personal qualities

- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the confidence to give clear guidance while maintaining positive and respectful relationships.
- Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
- Passion, curiosity and motivation for the role, with the ability to enthuse and motivate others.
- Demonstrable commitment to SEED's ethos and approach, with the ability to act as a positive ambassador for the organisation at all times.
- Ability and commitment to work in accordance with, and advocate for, all of SEED's policies and procedures, including safeguarding those with whom SEED works and reporting concerns appropriately.
- A flexible, patient and professional approach, with a strong awareness of the responsibilities associated with working internationally and representing SEED.

jobs.title: Senior Conservation Research Assistant (Madagascar)
jobs.description:
**Position Overview:**

This is a rare opportunity to live and work in Madagascar, one of the world’s most biodiverse and conservation-critical regions, leading long-term, field-based research in a remote setting. We are seeking a highly motivated Senior Research Assistant (SRA) with a relevant MSc and 1–3 years of practical field research experience to lead SEED Madagascar’s conservation research programme on the ground.

As the Senior Research Assistant, you will oversee the day-to-day operations of SEED’s research camp and play a central role in the design, implementation and reporting of our field-based research. Working closely with SEEDs Conservation Research Programme Coordinator and both international and national staff, you will manage data collection, ensure the quality and integrity of research activities and contribute to the analysis and dissemination of findings to donors and the wider conservation community.

Additionally, you will provide leadership and pastoral support to short-term volunteers, ensuring they receive appropriate training, guidance and supervision during their time in the field. This role is integral to advancing SEED’s mission, combining rigorous scientific research with strong team leadership and collaboration in a challenging but highly rewarding field environment.

*Location:* Fort Dauphin, Madagascar

*Timeframe*: 24 months with potential to extend;

*Terms and conditions:* Local salary to support with accommodation and living costs (field-based food/transport provided); contribution to flights and insurance

**Key Duties and Responsibilities:**

- **Research Leadership**
- Lead and manage the research team in the field, ensuring effective data collection and high research standards.
- Lead field-based research on key species and ecosystems, including setting up transects and collecting relevant ecological data.
- Contribute to the development of new research projects and conservation initiatives, helping to identify priority areas for future work.
- Support in the expansion of SEED’s research program by fostering relationships with other conservation organisations and researchers.
- **Data Management & Reporting**
- Ensure data is accurately collected, cleaned and organised in accordance with research protocols.
- Collaborate with the SCRP Coordinator in data analysis and the preparation of research reports for both internal use and external donors.
- Contribute to the development of research papers, presentations, and other publications for the international conservation community.
- Work with the SCRP Coordinator to identify opportunities for research collaborations and funding.
- Assist in the preparation of proposals and reports for research funding and project development.
- **Volunteer Coordination & Training**
- Support in the day-to-day management and pastoral care for short-term volunteers, ensuring their well-being and smooth integration into the field team.
- Lead training sessions for volunteers, ensuring they understand and follow research protocols, data collection methods, and safety procedures.
- **Collaboration & Team Management**
- Work closely with both the international and national research staff to ensure effective communication and team cohesion.
- Foster a positive working environment, promoting collaboration and sharing of knowledge between staff and volunteers.
- Ensure that all fieldwork is carried out in accordance with SEED’s health, safety, and ethical guidelines.
- **Community Engagement & Outreach**
- Support the SEED Madagascar team in engaging with communities, including facilitating meetings, conducting surveys, and helping with outreach initiatives.
- Provide clear interpretation and translation when necessary, ensuring effective communication between international staff and local communities.
- **Logistics & Operations**
- Assist in managing the logistical aspects of field research, including equipment, transport, and accommodation for staff and volunteers.
- Oversee the day-to-day operations of the research camp, ensuring smooth logistical coordination and resource management.
- **Policy & Compliance**
- Ensure compliance with SEED’s policies, including safeguarding, anti-corruption and whistleblowing procedures.
- Participate in ongoing training to promote adherence to SEED’s health, safety and ethical standards.
- **Additional Tasks**
- Assist with other tasks as requested by the Director of Programmes and Operations, Conservation Research Coordinator, or Senior Research Assistant within the scope of this role.

**Personal specification:**

- A Masters degree in a conservation-related field
- Proven experience in handling, cleaning, and analysing data, with proficiency in statistical analysis using programming software (e.g., R, Python, or similar)
- At least 1-3 years experience in field data collection, including the use of GPS and/or GIS for mapping and spatial analysis
- Experience in compiling conservation reports, academic papers, or similar documents, with the ability to present data and findings clearly and professionally
- Specialist knowledge of either primatology, herpetology or botany
- Able to or willing to learn to safely handle and identify reptiles and amphibians
- Previous experience of collecting data with a working knowledge of GPS and/or GIS
- Hold a current First Aid certificate
- Demonstrate an understanding of and commitment to SEED Madagascar’s ethos and approach and be a good ambassador for SEED Madagascar at all times
- Have passion, curiosity and motivation for the job and the ability to enthuse others
- Have the ability and desire to work with teams from different economic and cultural backgrounds and across multiple language barriers
- Have the ability and desire to build capacity and share skills across cultures
- Demonstrate proven ability to recognise and appropriately deal with challenging situations
- Demonstrate an awareness of and comfort with increased social and professional responsibility, working at all times with cultural sensitivity and respect
- Demonstrate the ability, social skills and confidence to give clear guidance and support to other members of the team in respect of the philosophy and procedures of SEED Madagascar in order to protect both their safety and the reputation of the NGO
- Be punctual and be able to work to tight deadlines in an organised manner and to a high standard
- Have a flexible and patient attitude
- Have excellent problem-solving skills
- Be able to work both independently and as part of a team.

jobs.title: Programme Officer - Financial Resilience
jobs.description:
The Financial Resilience Officer will work closely with both national and international staff to strengthen the financial management capacity of project participants and community-based associations across SEED Madagascar’s programmes. The role will focus on developing training in financial literacy, basic business management and community savings schemes, while supporting project teams to embed financial resilience components into their work.

This is a superb opportunity for a development professional with 2-4 years of experience to support livelihoods, financial development and/or resilience building.

\*Title:\*Financial Resilience Officer
*Location:* Fort Dauphin, Anosy Region, Madagascar

*Timeframe:* 24 months (probationary period 3 months)

*Terms and conditions:* Local salary, contribution to a return flight to post of £1,200 and to insurance of

£650

**Core Duties**

- Collaboratively develop context-appropriate capacity building, skill sharing and training activities on the topics of savings, financial management, and financial planning for different demographic groups and communities across the Anosy region.
- Support the creation and strengthening of Community Savings Groups (CSGs), including facilitation of training in savings practices, recordkeeping, group governance, and long-term planning.
- Identify which of these methods and activities are contextually compatible with SEED’s programme portfolio across the departments, with a focus on Rural Livelihoods.
- Support the development of scalable, context-appropriate pilots to strengthen financial resilience, either adapting existing programme activities or scoping new activities based on local needs.
- Ensure a collaborative approach to project development, working closely with national staff and adopting participatory methods with local communities to ensure inclusive dialogue throughout.

- Oversee and expand the programme’s Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) framework, including designing surveys with the national staff, data entry, data analysis, and tracking metrics against logframe goals and outcomes.
- Produce research reports, to a high standard of English, that clearly demonstrate the successes and challenges of SEED’s financial resilience initiatives.
- Compile funding proposals based on past evaluation, team discussion and international best practice in an engaging and professional manner.
- Work alongside the Project manager in budget tracking, forecasting and reconciliation to ensure that the project remains on track.
- Take an active part in project management and international team meetings, leading where appropriate and supporting other team members
- Form part of the team representing projects or SEED when required.
- Ensure all SEEDs policies and procedures are evident throughout the work of the department, including those for safeguarding, whistleblowing and anticorruption, and undertake continual training to ensure these are promoted at all times.
- Complete other ad-hoc tasks as required by the Head of Department, Programme Manager, or Director of Programmes and Operations to further the aims and work of the organization.

**Person specification**

- Degree-level qualification in or relating to international development, rural livelihoods, development economics, or financial resilience, or equivalent experience.
- Minimum of 2 years’ professional experience with similar programmes, including project development, monitoring, evaluation and learning, and reporting.
- Demonstrable experience of capacity building and/or education programmes, particularly in rural settings or covering topics such as financial management, savings schemes and strategies, or strengthening livelihoods.
- Demonstrable experience in setting up and/or supporting community savings groups (CSGs), VSLAs, or similar financial mechanisms in rural settings.
- Experience of living and working in a developing country with the ability and desire to work with teams from different economic and cultural backgrounds and across multiple language barriers. Proficiency in monitoring and evaluation methods, including quantitative data management and analysis in Excel and qualitative data collection tools such as survey design and focus group facilitation, and willing to use AI when necessary to assist in quantitative data management and analysis.
- Experience designing training and record-keeping materials appropriate for varying literacy levels, using tools such as Canva (workshop handouts) and Word (ledgers, governance templates, and other field-facing documents), and willing to use AI when necessary to assist in document creation.
- Demonstrated ability to design workshop curricula and group governance structures (such as savings group roles and record-keeping systems), and to contribute to overall programme strategy.
- Experience managing programme activities within budget, including tracking spend against planned allocations.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
- Demonstrable experience managing a variety of tasks and shifting priorities at short notice.
- Demonstrate proven ability to recognise and appropriately deal with challenging situations and problem-solve.
- Be punctual and be able to meet tight deadlines in an organised manner and to a high standard.
- Be able to work both independently and as part of a team.
- Fluency in written and spoken English with excellent written communication skills.
- Excellent listening and verbal communication skills and a flexible, patient, and positive attitude.
- Demonstrate an understanding of and commitment to SEED’s ethos and approach and be a good ambassador for the organisation at all times.
- Have passion, curiosity and motivation for the job and the ability to enthuse others.
- Demonstrate an awareness of and comfort with increased social and professional responsibility, working at all times with cultural sensitivity and respect.
- Demonstrate the ability, social skills and confidence to give clear guidance and support to other members of the team in respect of the philosophy and procedures of SEED in order to protect both their safety and the reputation of the NGO.
- Be able to work to and advocate for all of SEEDs policies and procedures, safeguarding those that SEED works with and reporting any concerns appropriately.

**About the Organisation**

SEED Madagascar is a British Charity working in partnership with communities in the southeast of Madagascar. We integrate high-quality community health, rural livelihoods; education infrastructure and conservation programmes to support long term, sustainable change and add to international best practice through research and publication across all of our programmatic areas. We are now looking for entry level interns and officers to work alongside national staff and expand our team.

jobs.title: Media and Communications Officer
jobs.description:
This is an exciting opportunity for a skilled Media and Communications Officer to play a central role in delivering the communications strategy of an international NGO in the heart of Madagascar.

Based in the coastal town of Fort Dauphin, the Officer will oversee the daily running of SEED’s social media and content development, manage a junior team member, and strengthen collaboration between the Communications and Programmes teams. The role includes supporting with major fundraising appeals, producing engaging donor updates, and developing innovative content across all platforms, including expanding SEED’s presence on TikTok.

The successful candidate will work closely with both national and international staff, contributing to impactful campaigns that showcase SEED’s work in sustainable development and conservation. Predominantly office-based with occasional travel to rural project sites, the role offers a diverse range of responsibilities for a communications professional looking to develop their leadership skills while contributing to meaningful, community-driven development.

*Location:* Fort Dauphin, Anosy Region, Madagascar
*Commitment:* 24 months, extendable, 40 hours a week
*Salary:* Local salary, up to £1,200 contribution for a return flight and up to £650 contribution towards insurance

jobs.title: Programme Officer - Community Health
jobs.description:

Focused in SEEDs maternal and child health programme, you will support the development, funding, reporting and evaluation of this work, offering support to other projects where required and working closely with national teams delivering projects on the ground.
